title: Upadeśasāhasrī
author: Ādi Śaṅkara

source.edition: Sengaku Mayeda, Śaṅkara’s Upadeśasāhasrī (1973; critical edition 2006)
source.changes: Full local Sanskrit text: 671 verse passages and 116 prose passages (787 source-marked units) from Padyabhāga and Gadyabhāga. Source markers are normalized for display; an original English translation is included for every unit. Verses I.1.1–I.1.26 and I.2.1–I.2.4 now have original simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses; their former translations are retained in separate fields. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.3.1–I.3.4 and I.4.1–I.4.5; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.5.1–I.5.5 and I.6.1–I.6.6; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.7.1–I.7.6; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.8.1–I.8.6; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.9.1–I.9.9; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.10.1–I.10.14; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.11.1–I.11.16 and corrected a Devanāgarī typo at I.11.8; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.12.1–I.12.10 and corrected two Devanāgarī spelling errors; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.12.11–I.12.19; former translations are retained separately. Added simple literal readings and token-by-token glosses for verses I.13.1–I.13.12; normalized a long-vowel spelling in I.13.17 for the next batch.

units.label: Verse I.1.1
units.deva: चैतन्यं सर्वगं सर्वं सर्वभूतगुहाशयम् । यत् सर्वविषयातीतं तस्मै सर्वविदे नमः
units.iast: caitanyaṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaṃ sarvabhūtaguhāśayam । yat sarvaviṣayātītaṃ tasmai sarvavide namaḥ
units.translation: Salutation to that all-knowing one: consciousness, all-pervading, all, dwelling in the heart-cave of every being, beyond every object.

gloss.en: dwelling in the heart-cave of all beings

units.editionTranslation: Salutations to that all-knowing One: all-pervading consciousness, dwelling in the hearts of all beings, and beyond every object of experience.

units.label: Verse I.1.2
units.deva: समापय्य क्रियाः सर्वा दाराग्न्याधानपूर्विकाः । ब्रह्मविद्याम् अथेदानीं वक्तुं वेदः प्रचक्रमे
units.iast: samāpayya kriyāḥ sarvā dārāgnyādhānapūrvikāḥ । brahmavidyām athedānīṃ vaktuṃ vedaḥ pracakrame
units.translation: Having completed all ritual acts, beginning with marriage and establishing the sacred fires, the Veda now began to speak the knowledge of Brahman.
units.editionTranslation: Having brought all ritual acts to an end, beginning with marriage and the establishing of sacred fires, the Veda now sets out to teach the knowledge of Brahman.

units.label: Verse I.1.3
units.deva: कर्माणि देहयोगार्थं देहयोगे प्रियाप्रिये । ध्रुवे स्यातां ततो रागो द्वेषश् चैव ततः क्रियाः
units.iast: karmāṇi dehayogārthaṃ dehayoge priyāpriye । dhruve syātāṃ tato rāgo dveṣaś caiva tataḥ kriyāḥ
units.translation: Actions are for obtaining a body; with embodiment, pleasure and pain certainly arise. From them come attachment and aversion, and from these, actions.
units.editionTranslation: Ritual actions are performed for the sake of obtaining a body; with embodiment come pleasure and pain, inevitably; from these arise attachment and aversion, and from them, actions.

units.label: Verse I.1.4
units.deva: धर्माधर्मौ ततो ऽज्ञस्य देहयोगस् तथा पुनः एवं नित्यप्रवृत्तो ऽयं संसारश् चक्रवद् भृशम्
units.iast: dharmādharmau tato 'jñasya dehayogas tathā punaḥ evaṃ nityapravṛtto 'yaṃ saṃsāraś cakravad bhṛśam
units.translation: Then merit and demerit arise; for the ignorant, embodiment follows again. Thus this saṃsāra keeps turning continuously, like a wheel.
units.editionTranslation: From action arise merit and demerit; for the ignorant these lead again to embodiment. Thus this cycle of worldly existence turns on without end, like a wheel.

units.label: Verse I.1.5
units.deva: अज्ञानं तस्य मूलं स्याद् इति तद्धानम् इष्यते । ब्रह्मविद्यात आरब्धा ततो निःश्रेयसं भवेत्
units.iast: ajñānaṃ tasya mūlaṃ syād iti taddhānam iṣyate । brahmavidyāta ārabdhā tato niḥśreyasaṃ bhavet
units.translation: Ignorance is its root; therefore its removal is sought. From undertaking the knowledge of Brahman, the highest good arises.
units.editionTranslation: Ignorance is its root, and its removal is therefore sought. Knowledge of Brahman is undertaken for that purpose; from it comes the highest good.

units.label: Verse I.1.6
units.deva: विद्यैवाज्ञानहानाय न कर्माप्रतिकूलतः । नाज्ञानस्याप्रहाणे हि रागद्वेषक्षयो भवेत्
units.iast: vidyaivājñānahānāya na karmāpratikūlataḥ । nājñānasyāprahāṇe hi rāgadveṣakṣayo bhavet
units.translation: Knowledge alone is for the removal of ignorance; action is not its direct opposite. While ignorance remains, attachment and aversion do not cease.
units.editionTranslation: Knowledge alone removes ignorance; action is not its direct opposite. Until ignorance is removed, attachment and aversion cannot come to an end.

units.label: Verse I.1.7
units.deva: रागद्वेषक्षयाभावे कर्म दोषोद्भवं ध्रुवम् । तस्मान् निःश्रेयसार्थाय विद्यैवात्र विधीयते
units.iast: rāgadveṣakṣayābhāve karma doṣodbhavaṃ dhruvam । tasmān niḥśreyasārthāya vidyaivātra vidhīyate
units.translation: When attachment and aversion have not ceased, action inevitably gives rise to faults. Therefore knowledge alone is taught here for the highest good.

gloss.en: when attachment and aversion have not ceased

units.editionTranslation: So long as attachment and aversion remain, action inevitably gives rise to faults. Therefore knowledge alone is taught here as the means to the highest good.

units.label: Verse I.1.8
units.deva: ननु कर्म तथा नित्यं कर्तव्यं जीवने सति । विद्यायाः सहकारित्वं मोक्षं प्रति हि तद् व्रजेत्
units.iast: nanu karma tathā nityaṃ kartavyaṃ jīvane sati । vidyāyāḥ sahakāritvaṃ mokṣaṃ prati hi tad vrajet
units.translation: Objection: As long as one lives, daily action must be done. Could action assist knowledge toward liberation?
units.editionTranslation: Objection: “As long as one lives, daily rites must be performed. Could action not assist knowledge in bringing about liberation?”

units.label: Verse I.1.9
units.deva: यथा विद्या तथा कर्म चोदितत्वाविशेषतः । प्रत्यवायस्मृतेश् चैव कार्यं कर्म मुमुक्षुभिः
units.iast: yathā vidyā tathā karma coditatvāviśeṣataḥ । pratyavāyasmṛteś caiva kāryaṃ karma mumukṣubhiḥ
units.translation: Objection: Knowledge and action are equally enjoined, and omission is remembered as a fault; therefore seekers of liberation must perform the action.

gloss.en: because a fault of omission is remembered

units.editionTranslation: “Knowledge and action are alike prescribed by scripture; omission of the prescribed rite is also remembered as a fault. Seekers of liberation should therefore perform their duties.”

units.label: Verse I.1.10
units.deva: ननु ध्रुवफला विद्या नान्यत् किंचिद् अपेक्षते । नाग्निष्टोमो यथैवान्यद् ध्रुवकार्यो ऽप्य् अपेक्षते
units.iast: nanu dhruvaphalā vidyā nānyat kiṃcid apekṣate । nāgniṣṭomo yathaivānyad dhruvakāryo 'py apekṣate
units.translation: Objection: Knowledge has a certain result and depends on nothing else. The Agniṣṭoma rite also has a certain result, yet it depends on other factors.
units.editionTranslation: Objection: “Knowledge has a certain result and depends on nothing else. Yet even the certain result of the Agniṣṭoma rite requires other factors.”

units.label: Verse I.1.11
units.deva: तथा ध्रुवफला विद्या कर्म नित्यम् अपेक्षते । इत्य् एवं केचिद् इच्छन्ति न कर्म प्रतिकूलतः
units.iast: tathā dhruvaphalā vidyā karma nityam apekṣate । ity evaṃ kecid icchanti na karma pratikūlataḥ
units.translation: Some hold this view: “In the same way, knowledge, whose result is certain, depends on regular action”; action is not directly opposed to it.
units.editionTranslation: “In the same way, even though its result is certain, knowledge depends on the regular rites.” Some hold this view, though action is not directly opposed to knowledge.

units.label: Verse I.1.12
units.deva: विद्यायाः प्रतिकूलं हि कर्म स्यात् साभिमानतः । निर्विकारात्मबुद्धिश् च विद्येतीह प्रकीर्तिता
units.iast: vidyāyāḥ pratikūlaṃ hi karma syāt sābhimānataḥ । nirvikārātmabuddhiś ca vidyetīha prakīrtitā
units.translation: Action is indeed opposed to knowledge when done with a sense of agency. Knowledge is declared here to be understanding of the changeless Self.
units.editionTranslation: Action, performed with the sense of agency, is opposed to knowledge. Knowledge is declared here to be understanding of the changeless Self.

units.label: Verse I.1.13
units.deva: अहं कर्ता ममेदं स्याद् इति कर्म प्रवर्तते । वस्त्वधीना भवेद् विद्या कर्त्रधीनो भवेद् विधिः
units.iast: ahaṃ kartā mamedaṃ syād iti karma pravartate । vastvadhīnā bhaved vidyā kartradhīno bhaved vidhiḥ
units.translation: Action proceeds from the thought, “I am the doer; this is mine.” Knowledge depends on reality; an injunction depends on a doer.
units.editionTranslation: Action proceeds from the thought ‘I am the doer; this is mine.’ Knowledge depends on the reality as it is; an injunction depends on an agent.

units.label: Verse I.1.14
units.deva: कारकाण्य् उपमृद्नाति विद्याब्बुद्धिम् इवोषरे । तत्सत्यमतिम् आदाय कर्म कर्तुं व्यवस्यति
units.iast: kārakāṇy upamṛdnāti vidyābbuddhim ivoṣare । tatsatyamatim ādāya karma kartuṃ vyavasyati
units.translation: Knowledge crushes the factors of action, like the thought of knowledge in barren soil. Taking that idea of truth, one decides to act.
units.editionTranslation: Knowledge crushes the factors of action, as insight dries up in barren ground. Taking truth to be established, [the opponent] resolves to perform action.

units.label: Verse I.1.15
units.deva: विरुद्धत्वाद् अतः शक्यं कर्म कर्तुं न विद्यया । सहैवं विदुषा तस्मात् कर्म हेयं मुमुक्षुणा
units.iast: viruddhatvād ataḥ śakyaṃ karma kartuṃ na vidyayā । sahaivaṃ viduṣā tasmāt karma heyaṃ mumukṣuṇā
units.translation: Therefore, because they are opposed, action cannot be done together with knowledge. So the seeker of liberation who knows should give up action.
units.editionTranslation: Because they are opposed, action cannot be performed together with knowledge. Therefore the seeker of liberation should renounce action.

units.label: Verse I.1.16
units.deva: देहाद्यैर् अविशेषेण देहिनो ग्रहणं निजम् । प्राणिनां तद् अविद्योत्थं तावत् कर्मविधिर् भवेत्
units.iast: dehādyair aviśeṣeṇa dehino grahaṇaṃ nijam । prāṇināṃ tad avidyotthaṃ tāvat karmavidhir bhavet
units.translation: As long as living beings identify themselves without distinction with the body and the rest, action is enjoined; this identification arises from ignorance.

gloss.en: with the body and the rest

units.editionTranslation: Living beings identify themselves without distinction with the body and the rest. That identification arises from ignorance; on it rests the injunction to act.

units.label: Verse I.1.17
units.deva: नेति नेतीति देहादीन् अपोह्यात्मावशेषितः । अविशेषात्मबोधार्थं तेनाविद्या निवर्तिता
units.iast: neti netīti dehādīn apohyātmāvaśeṣitaḥ । aviśeṣātmabodhārthaṃ tenāvidyā nivartitā
units.translation: By “not this, not this,” the body and the rest are set aside, and the Self alone remains. By that, ignorance is removed for understanding the undifferentiated Self.
units.editionTranslation: By the teaching ‘not this, not this,’ the body and the rest are set aside and the Self alone remains. Knowledge of the undifferentiated Self removes ignorance.

units.label: Verse I.1.18
units.deva: निवृत्ता सा कथं भूयः प्रसूयेत प्रमाणतः । असत्य् एवाविशेषे हि प्रत्यगात्मनि केवले
units.iast: nivṛttā sā kathaṃ bhūyaḥ prasūyeta pramāṇataḥ । asaty evāviśeṣe hi pratyagātmani kevale
units.translation: How could that ignorance, once removed, arise again through a means of knowledge, when only the undifferentiated inward Self is real?
units.editionTranslation: How could ignorance, once removed, arise again through a means of knowledge, when only the one inward Self, without distinction, is real?

units.label: Verse I.1.19
units.deva: न चेद् भूयः प्रसूयेत कर्ता भोक्तेति धीः कथम् । सद् अस्मीति च विज्ञाने तस्माद् विद्यासहायिका
units.iast: na ced bhūyaḥ prasūyeta kartā bhokteti dhīḥ katham । sad asmīti ca vijñāne tasmād vidyāsahāyikā
units.translation: If it does not arise again, how could the thought “I am the doer and enjoyer” arise? With the knowledge “I am Being,” [action] is an aid to knowledge.
units.editionTranslation: If it does not arise again, how could the thought ‘I am the doer and enjoyer’ return? When one knows ‘I am Being,’ knowledge alone supports knowledge.

units.label: Verse I.1.20
units.deva: अत्यरेचयद् इत्य् उक्तो न्यासः श्रुत्यात एव हि । कर्मभ्यो मानसान्तेभ्य एतावद् इति वाजिनाम्
units.iast: atyarecayad ity ukto nyāsaḥ śrutyāta eva hi । karmabhyo mānasāntebhya etāvad iti vājinām
units.translation: The Veda itself says that renunciation surpasses action; the Vājasaneyins say that this extends from actions through mental action.
units.editionTranslation: The Veda itself says that renunciation surpasses [all other paths], and that the Vājasaneyins teach this: all action, even mental action, is set aside.

units.label: Verse I.1.21
units.deva: अमृतत्वं श्रुतं तस्मात् त्याज्यं कर्म मुमुक्षुभिः । अग्निष्टोमवद् इत्य् उक्तं तत्रेदम् अभिधीयते
units.iast: amṛtatvaṃ śrutaṃ tasmāt tyājyaṃ karma mumukṣubhiḥ । agniṣṭomavad ity uktaṃ tatredam abhidhīyate
units.translation: Immortality is taught; therefore, seekers of liberation must give up action. “Like the Agniṣṭoma,” it is said; this is explained here.
units.editionTranslation: Immortality is taught as the result; therefore seekers of liberation should renounce action. The Agniṣṭoma comparison was raised, and this is the reply:

units.label: Verse I.1.22
units.deva: नैककारकसाध्यत्वात् फलान्यत्वाच् च कर्मणः । विद्या तद्विपरीतातो दृष्टान्तो विषमो भवेत्
units.iast: naikakārakasādhyatvāt phalānyatvāc ca karmaṇaḥ । vidyā tadviparītāto dṛṣṭānto viṣamo bhavet
units.translation: Action is not accomplished by one factor alone, and its result is different. Knowledge is the opposite of that; therefore the example is not comparable.
units.editionTranslation: “Because action depends on many factors and has a different result, it is unlike knowledge, which is the opposite; the example is therefore not comparable.”

units.label: Verse I.1.23
units.deva: कृष्यादिवत् फलार्थत्वाद् अन्यकर्मोपबृंहणम् । अग्निष्टोमस् त्व् अपेक्षेत विद्यान्यत् किम् अपेक्षते
units.iast: kṛṣyādivat phalārthatvād anyakarmopabṛṃhaṇam । agniṣṭomas tv apekṣeta vidyānyat kim apekṣate
units.translation: Because it is for a result, action is supported by other actions, as farming is. The Agniṣṭoma depends on them; what else does knowledge depend on?
units.editionTranslation: “Other actions support an action that produces a result, as farming does; the Agniṣṭoma depends on them. What else does knowledge depend on?”

units.label: Verse I.1.24
units.deva: प्रत्यवायस् तु तस्यैव यस्याहंकार इष्यते । अहंकारफलार्थित्वे विद्येते नात्मवेदिनः
units.iast: pratyavāyas tu tasyaiva yasyāhaṃkāra iṣyate । ahaṃkāraphalārthitve vidyete nātmavedinaḥ
units.translation: The fault of omission belongs only to one in whom ego is held to exist. Ego and desire for results are not found in the knower of the Self.

gloss.en: in the knower of the Self

units.editionTranslation: The fault of omission belongs only to one who maintains the ego. For a knower of the Self there is no knowledge of an ego seeking results.

units.label: Verse I.1.25
units.deva: तस्माद् अज्ञानहानाय संसारविनिवृत्तये । ब्रह्मविद्याविधानाय प्रारब्धोपनिषत् त्व् इयम्
units.iast: tasmād ajñānahānāya saṃsāravinivṛttaye । brahmavidyāvidhānāya prārabdhopaniṣat tv iyam
units.translation: Therefore this Upaniṣad has been begun to remove ignorance, end saṃsāra, and teach the knowledge of Brahman.

gloss.en: for teaching the knowledge of Brahman

units.editionTranslation: Therefore this Upaniṣad begins, to remove ignorance and end worldly existence, teaching the knowledge of Brahman.

units.label: Verse I.1.26
units.deva: सदेर् उपनिपूर्वस्य क्विपि चोपनिषद् भवेत् । मन्दीकरणभावाच् च गर्भादेः शातनात् तथा
units.iast: sader upanipūrvasya kvipi copaniṣad bhavet । mandīkaraṇabhāvāc ca garbhādeḥ śātanāt tathā
units.translation: The word “Upaniṣad” is formed from the root sad, preceded by upa and ni, with the suffix kvip. It is so called because it weakens and destroys the bond beginning with the womb.

gloss.en: of the womb and the rest

units.editionTranslation: The word *upaniṣad* is derived from the root *sad* with the prefixes *upa* and *ni* and the suffix *kvip*. It is so called because it weakens bondage and loosens the cycle of birth, beginning with the womb.

units.label: Verse I.2.1
units.deva: प्रतिषेद्धुम् अशक्यत्वान् नेति नेतीति शेषितम् । इदं नाहम् इदं नाहम् इत्य् अद्धा प्रतिपद्यते
units.iast: pratiṣeddhum aśakyatvān neti netīti śeṣitam । idaṃ nāham idaṃ nāham ity addhā pratipadyate
units.translation: Because it cannot be denied, “not this, not this” is retained. One directly understands, “I am not this; I am not this.”
units.editionTranslation: Since it cannot be denied, the teaching ‘not this, not this’ is retained; one directly understands, ‘I am not this; I am not this.’

units.label: Verse I.2.2
units.deva: इदंधीर् इदमात्मोत्था वाचारम्भणगोचरा । निषिद्धात्मोद्भवत्वात् सा न पुनर् मानतां व्रजेत्
units.iast: idaṃdhīr idamātmotthā vācārambhaṇagocarā । niṣiddhātmodbhavatvāt sā na punar mānatāṃ vrajet
units.translation: The cognition “this” arises from this Self and is within the scope of speech. Because it arises from the Self that was denied, it does not again become a means of knowledge.

gloss.en: because it arises from the denied Self
validity as a means of knowledge

units.editionTranslation: The cognition ‘this’ arises from the Self and concerns what can be expressed in words. Since it arises from what has been denied as the Self, it cannot itself serve as a valid means of knowledge.

units.label: Verse I.2.3
units.deva: पूर्वबुद्धिम् अबाधित्वा नोत्तरा जायते मतिः । दृशिर् एकः स्वयंसिद्धः फलत्वात् स न बाध्यते
units.iast: pūrvabuddhim abādhitvā nottarā jāyate matiḥ । dṛśir ekaḥ svayaṃsiddhaḥ phalatvāt sa na bādhyate
units.translation: A later cognition does not arise without setting aside the earlier cognition. The Seer alone is self-established; because it is the result, it is not set aside.
units.editionTranslation: A later cognition does not arise without sublating the earlier one. The Seer alone is self-established; as the ground of every result, it cannot be sublated.

units.label: Verse I.2.4
units.deva: इदंवनम् अतिक्रम्य शोकमोहादिदूषितम् । वनाद् गान्धारको यद्वत् स्वम् आत्मानं प्रपद्यते
units.iast: idaṃvanam atikramya śokamohādidūṣitam । vanād gāndhārako yadvat svam ātmānaṃ prapadyate
units.translation: Just as a man from Gandhāra, crossing a forest tainted with grief, delusion, and the rest, reaches his own home, so one reaches the Self.

gloss.en: tainted by grief, delusion, and the rest

units.editionTranslation: “Just as the man from Gandhāra, leaving the forest of grief and delusion, finds his way back to himself,”

units.label: Verse I.3.1
units.deva: ईश्वरश् चेद् अनात्मा स्यान् नासाव् अस्मीति धारयेत् । आत्मा चेद् ईश्वरो ऽस्मीति विद्या सान्यनिवर्तिका
units.iast: īśvaraś ced anātmā syān nāsāv asmīti dhārayet । ātmā ced īśvaro 'smīti vidyā sānyanivartikā
units.translation: If the Lord were not the Self, one would not hold the thought, “I am that.” If the Self is the Lord, that knowledge removes the idea of another.

gloss.en: remover of the idea of another

units.editionTranslation: “if the Lord were not the Self, one could not hold the thought ‘I am He.’ If the Self is the Lord, knowledge of that fact removes all else.”

units.label: Verse I.3.2
units.deva: आत्मनो ऽन्यस्य चेद् धर्मा अस्थूलत्वादयो मताः । अज्ञेयत्वे ऽस्य किं तैः स्याद् आत्मत्वे त्व् अन्यधीह्नुतिः
units.iast: ātmano 'nyasya ced dharmā asthūlatvādayo matāḥ । ajñeyatve 'sya kiṃ taiḥ syād ātmatve tv anyadhīhnutiḥ
units.translation: If qualities such as “not gross” belong to something other than the Self, what use are they if that is unknowable? But if they belong to the Self, they remove the thought of another.

gloss.en: removal of the thought of another

units.editionTranslation: If qualities such as ‘not gross’ belong to something other than the Self, what use are they if that reality cannot be known? If they belong to the Self, they dispel the notion of another.

units.label: Verse I.3.3
units.deva: मिथ्याध्यासनिषेधार्थं ततो ऽस्थूलादि गृह्यताम् । परत्र चेन् निषेधार्थं शून्यतावर्णनं हि तत्
units.iast: mithyādhyāsaniṣedhārthaṃ tato 'sthūlādi gṛhyatām । paratra cen niṣedhārthaṃ śūnyatāvarṇanaṃ hi tat
units.translation: Therefore, let “not gross” and the rest be understood as denying false superimposition. If they are meant to deny something else, that is indeed a description of emptiness.

gloss.en: for the purpose of denying false superimposition

units.editionTranslation: To deny false superimposition, understand the teaching ‘not gross’ and the rest. If it were meant to deny some other thing, it would merely describe a void.

units.label: Verse I.3.4
units.deva: बुभुत्सोर् यदि चान्यत्र प्रत्यगात्मन इष्यते । अप्राणो ह्य् अमनाः शुभ्र इति चानर्थकं वचः
units.iast: bubhutsor yadi cānyatra pratyagātmana iṣyate । aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti cānarthakaṃ vacaḥ
units.translation: If what is to be known is held to be elsewhere than the innermost Self, the statement “without breath, without mind, pure” has no purpose.

gloss.en: of one who wishes to know

units.editionTranslation: If the object to be known were held to be elsewhere than the innermost Self, the words ‘without breath, without mind, pure’ would have no purpose.

units.label: Verse I.4.1
units.deva: अहंप्रत्ययबीजं यद् अहंप्रत्ययवत्स्थितम् । नाहंप्रत्ययवह्न्युष्टं कथं कर्म प्ररोहति
units.iast: ahaṃpratyayabījaṃ yad ahaṃpratyayavatsthitam । nāhaṃpratyayavahnyuṣṭaṃ kathaṃ karma prarohati
units.translation: That seed of the I-thought which stands like an I-thought, not burnt by the fire of the I-thought—how does action sprout?

gloss.en: burnt by the fire of the I-thought

units.editionTranslation: “If the seed of the thought ‘I’ remains, and stands as the source of that thought, how can action sprout when the fire of ‘I’-awareness has scorched it?”

units.label: Verse I.4.2
units.deva: दृष्टवच् चेत् प्ररोहः स्यान् नान्यकर्मा स इष्यते । तन्निरोधे कथं तत् स्यात् पृच्छामो वस् तद् उच्यताम्
units.iast: dṛṣṭavac cet prarohaḥ syān nānyakarmā sa iṣyate । tannirodhe kathaṃ tat syāt pṛcchāmo vas tad ucyatām
units.translation: If sprouting occurs as seen, it is held to be no other action. When that is stopped, how could it occur? We ask you; let that be explained.
units.editionTranslation: “If action sprouts, as it appears to, it is said to be some other action. How could it remain when that source is destroyed? We ask you: explain this.”

units.label: Verse I.4.3
units.deva: देहाद्यारम्भसामर्थ्याज् ज्ञानं सद्विषयं त्वयि । अभिभूय फलं कुर्यात् कर्मान्ते ज्ञानम् उद्भवेत्
units.iast: dehādyārambhasāmarthyāj jñānaṃ sadviṣayaṃ tvayi । abhibhūya phalaṃ kuryāt karmānte jñānam udbhavet
units.translation: Because knowledge in you has the real as its object and has the power to begin the body and the rest, it would overcome [the opposing force] and produce a result; knowledge would arise at the end of action.

gloss.en: because of the power to begin the body and the rest
having the real as its object

units.editionTranslation: “Because it has the capacity to produce a body and the rest, knowledge in you concerns what is real; it suppresses action and bears fruit, and when the action ends, knowledge arises.”

units.label: Verse I.4.4
units.deva: आरब्धस्य फले ह्य् एते भोगो ज्ञानं च कर्मणः । अविरोधस् तयोर् युक्तो वैधर्म्यं चेतरस्य तु
units.iast: ārabdhasya phale hy ete bhogo jñānaṃ ca karmaṇaḥ । avirodhas tayor yukto vaidharmyaṃ cetarasya tu
units.translation: For an action whose result has begun, experience and knowledge are these two [results]. It is reasonable that they do not conflict, but the other [action] is different.
units.editionTranslation: “For action already begun, both experience and knowledge are its results. Their coexistence is reasonable; other kinds of action differ.”

units.label: Verse I.4.5
units.deva: देहात्मज्ञानवज् ज्ञानं देहात्मज्ञानबाधकम् । आत्मन्य् एय भवेद् यस्य स नेच्छन्न् अपि मुच्यते
units.iast: dehātmajñānavaj jñānaṃ dehātmajñānabādhakam । ātmany eya bhaved yasya sa necchann api mucyate
units.translation: Knowledge that blocks the thought “the body is the Self” is like that thought. Whoever has it in the Self is freed even without wishing.

gloss.en: like knowledge that the body is the Self
that blocks knowledge that the body is the Self

units.editionTranslation: “Knowledge, like the knowledge ‘I am the body,’ can sublate the knowledge ‘I am the body.’ Whoever has this knowledge established in the Self is liberated, even without intending it.”

units.label: Verse I.5.1
units.deva: मूत्राशङ्को यथोदङ्को नाग्रहीद् अमृतं मुनिः । कर्मनाशभयाज् जन्तोर् आत्मज्ञानाग्रहस् तथा
units.iast: mūtrāśaṅko yathodaṅko nāgrahīd amṛtaṃ muniḥ । karmanāśabhayāj jantor ātmajñānāgrahas tathā
units.translation: Just as the sage Udaṅka did not take nectar, suspecting it to be urine, so a living being refuses Self-knowledge from fear that action will be lost.

gloss.en: from fear of loss of action

units.editionTranslation: “The sage Udaṅka, fearing the loss of ritual merit, would not accept nectar, mistaking it for urine; in the same way a person refuses knowledge of the Self for fear of losing the results of action.”

units.label: Verse I.5.2
units.deva: बुद्धिस्थश् चलतीवात्मा ध्यायतीव च दृश्यते । नौगतस्य यथा वृक्षास् तद्वत् संसारविभ्रमः
units.iast: buddhisthaś calatīvātmā dhyāyatīva ca dṛśyate । naugatasya yathā vṛkṣās tadvat saṃsāravibhramaḥ
units.translation: The Self, situated in the intellect, is seen as if moving and as if thinking, just as trees seem to move for one riding in a boat; this is the confusion of worldly life.

gloss.en: of one gone in a boat

units.editionTranslation: “The Self appears to move and think because it is reflected in the intellect, just as trees seem to move to one travelling in a boat.”

units.label: Verse I.5.3
units.deva: नौस्थस्य प्रातिलोम्येन नगानां गमनं यथा । आत्मनः संसृतिस् तद्वद् ध्यायतीवेति हि श्रुतिः
units.iast: nausthasya prātilomyena nagānāṃ gamanaṃ yathā । ātmanaḥ saṃsṛtis tadvad dhyāyatīveti hi śrutiḥ
units.translation: Just as trees move backward to one in a boat, so the Self’s worldly wandering [appears]; scripture indeed says, “as if thinking.”
units.editionTranslation: “As trees seem to move backward to someone in a boat, so the Self seems to undergo worldly change, says scripture, using ‘as if it thinks.’”

units.label: Verse I.5.4
units.deva: चैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बेन व्याप्तो बोधो हि जायते । बुद्धेः शब्दादिनिर्भासस् तेन मोमुह्यते जगत्
units.iast: caitanyapratibimbena vyāpto bodho hi jāyate । buddheḥ śabdādinirbhāsas tena momuhyate jagat
units.translation: Awareness pervaded by a reflection of consciousness indeed arises; through that, sound and the rest appear in the intellect, and the world is greatly deluded.

gloss.en: appearance of sound and the rest

units.editionTranslation: “Awareness, reflected in consciousness, pervades the intellect; through it, sounds and the rest appear there, and the world is deluded.”

units.label: Verse I.5.5
units.deva: चैतन्याभासताहमस् तादर्थ्यं च तद् अस्य यत् । इदमंशप्रहाणे न परः सो ऽनुभवो भवेत्
units.iast: caitanyābhāsatāhamas tādarthyaṃ ca tad asya yat । idamaṃśaprahāṇe na paraḥ so 'nubhavo bhavet
units.translation: The “I” is a reflection of consciousness and is related to that [consciousness]. When the “this” part is abandoned, there is no other experience than that.
units.editionTranslation: “The ‘I’-thought is a reflection of awareness and takes on its nature. When the ‘this’ aspect is relinquished, the supreme experience remains.”

units.label: Verse I.6.1
units.deva: छित्त्वा त्यक्तेन हस्तेन स्वयं नात्मा विशेष्यते । तथा शिष्टेन सर्वेण येन येन विशेष्यते
units.iast: chittvā tyaktena hastena svayaṃ nātmā viśeṣyate । tathā śiṣṭena sarveṇa yena yena viśeṣyate
units.translation: The Self itself is not qualified by a hand that has been cut off and discarded. In the same way, it is qualified by each thing that remains.
units.editionTranslation: “A person is not defined by a hand once it has been cut off and discarded; in the same way, by whatever remains, the Self is distinguished.”

units.label: Verse I.6.2
units.deva: तस्मात् त्यक्तेन हस्तेन तुल्यं सर्वं विशेषणम् । अनात्मत्वेन तस्माज् ज्ञो मुक्तः सर्वविशेषणैः
units.iast: tasmāt tyaktena hastena tulyaṃ sarvaṃ viśeṣaṇam । anātmatvena tasmāj jño muktaḥ sarvaviśeṣaṇaiḥ
units.translation: Therefore, every qualification is like the discarded hand. Because they are not-Self, the knower is free from all qualifications.
units.editionTranslation: “Every attribute is therefore like the discarded hand. Knowing it as not-Self, the knower is free of every attribute.”

units.label: Verse I.6.3
units.deva: विशेषणम् इदं सर्वं साध्वलंकरणं यथा । अविद्यास्तम् अतः सर्वं ज्ञात आत्मन्य् असद् भवेत्
units.iast: viśeṣaṇam idaṃ sarvaṃ sādhvalaṃkaraṇaṃ yathā । avidyāstam ataḥ sarvaṃ jñāta ātmany asad bhavet
units.translation: All these qualifications are like fine ornaments. Therefore, when ignorance ends, all that is known is unreal in the Self.
units.editionTranslation: “All these attributes are like ornaments; once ignorance has ended, everything known as an attribute is absent in the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.6.4
units.deva: ज्ञातैवात्मा सदा ग्राह्यो ज्ञेयम् उत्सृज्य केवलः । अहम् इत्य् अपि यद् ग्राह्यं व्यपेताङ्गसमं हि तत्
units.iast: jñātaivātmā sadā grāhyo jñeyam utsṛjya kevalaḥ । aham ity api yad grāhyaṃ vyapetāṅgasamaṃ hi tat
units.translation: The knower alone, after leaving aside what is to be known, is always to be grasped as the Self, alone. Even what is grasped as “I” is indeed like a removed limb.
units.editionTranslation: “The knower alone is always to be recognized as the Self, after setting aside what is known. Even what can be grasped as ‘I’ is like a limb that has been removed.”

units.label: Verse I.6.5
units.deva: यावान् स्याद् इदमंशो यः स स्वतो ऽन्यो विशेषणम् । विशेषप्रक्षयो यत्र सिद्धो ज्ञश् चित्रगुर् यथा
units.iast: yāvān syād idamaṃśo yaḥ sa svato 'nyo viśeṣaṇam । viśeṣaprakṣayo yatra siddho jñaś citragur yathā
units.translation: Whatever the “this” part may be, it is a qualification other than the Self. Where every distinction is destroyed, the knower is established, like one whose limbs are gone.
units.editionTranslation: “Whatever portion of ‘this’ there may be is an attribute, other than the Self; when every distinction is ended, the knower is established, like a person who has lost his limbs.”

units.label: Verse I.6.6
units.deva: इदम् अंशो ऽहम् इत्य् अत्र त्याज्यो नात्मेति पण्डितैः । अहं ब्रह्मेति शिष्टो ऽंशो भूतपूर्वगतेर् भवेत्
units.iast: idam aṃśo 'ham ity atra tyājyo nātmeti paṇḍitaiḥ । ahaṃ brahmeti śiṣṭo 'ṃśo bhūtapūrvagater bhavet
units.translation: Here the wise should abandon the “this” part as not-Self in the thought “I am this.” The remaining part, “I am Brahman,” comes from the prior course [of thought].
units.editionTranslation: “The wise should set aside the ‘this’ portion and the thought ‘I’ as not-Self; what remains is the portion expressed by ‘I am Brahman,’ grounded in the original Self.”

units.label: Verse I.7.1
units.deva: बुद्ध्यारूढं सदा सर्वं दृश्यते यत्र तत्र वा । मया तस्मात् परं ब्रह्म सर्वज्ञश् चास्मि सर्वगः
units.iast: buddhyārūḍhaṃ sadā sarvaṃ dṛśyate yatra tatra vā । mayā tasmāt paraṃ brahma sarvajñaś cāsmi sarvagaḥ
units.translation: Everything seen anywhere is always set in the intellect. Therefore I am the supreme Brahman, all-knowing and all-pervading.
units.editionTranslation: “Everything, everywhere, is seen in the intellect; therefore I am the supreme Brahman, all-knowing and all-pervading.”

units.label: Verse I.7.2
units.deva: यथात्मबुद्धिचाराणां साक्षी तद्वत् परेष्व् अपि । नैवापोढुं न वादातुं शक्यस् तस्मात् परो ह्य् अहम्
units.iast: yathātmabuddhicārāṇāṃ sākṣī tadvat pareṣv api । naivāpoḍhuṃ na vādātuṃ śakyas tasmāt paro hy aham
units.translation: As the witness of the movements of my own intellect, so too am I the witness in others. I cannot be removed or denied by argument; therefore I am supreme.

gloss.en: of the movements of one’s own intellect

units.editionTranslation: “I am the witness of the movements of my own intellect; likewise of the intellects of others. I cannot be set aside or denied by argument; therefore I am supreme.”

units.label: Verse I.7.3
units.deva: विकारित्वम् अशुद्धत्वं भौतिकत्वं न चात्मनः । अशेषबुद्धिसाक्षित्वाद् बुद्धिवच् चाल्पवेदना
units.iast: vikāritvam aśuddhatvaṃ bhautikatvaṃ na cātmanaḥ । aśeṣabuddhisākṣitvād buddhivac cālpavedanā
units.translation: Changefulness, impurity, and material nature do not belong to the Self. Because it witnesses all intellects, its awareness is not limited like the intellect’s.
units.editionTranslation: “The Self is not subject to change, impurity or material nature. As witness of every movement of the intellect, it knows no less than the intellect.”

units.label: Verse I.7.4
units.deva: मणौ प्रकाश्यते यद्वद् रक्ताद्याकारतातपे । मयि संदृश्यते सर्वम् आतपेनेव तन् मया
units.iast: maṇau prakāśyate yadvad raktādyākāratātape । mayi saṃdṛśyate sarvam ātapeneva tan mayā
units.translation: Just as red and other forms are made visible in a jewel by sunlight, all that is seen in me is seen through me, as by sunlight.

gloss.en: in sunlight that shows red forms and the rest

units.editionTranslation: “Just as red and other colors appear in a jewel when sunlight falls on it, everything appears in me, as objects appear in sunlight.”

units.label: Verse I.7.5
units.deva: बुद्धौ दृश्यं भवेद् बुद्धौ सत्यां नास्ति विपर्यये । द्रष्टा यस्मात् सदा द्रष्टा तस्माद् द्वैतं न विद्यते
units.iast: buddhau dṛśyaṃ bhaved buddhau satyāṃ nāsti viparyaye । draṣṭā yasmāt sadā draṣṭā tasmād dvaitaṃ na vidyate
units.translation: What is seen exists when the intellect is present; it does not exist in the opposite state. Because the seer is always the seer, duality is not found.
units.editionTranslation: “What is seen exists when the intellect exists and is absent when it does not. Since the Seer is always the Seer, duality does not exist.”

units.label: Verse I.7.6
units.deva: अविवेकात् पराभावं यथा बुद्धिर् अवेत् तथा । विवेकात् तु पराद् अन्यः स्वयं चापि न विद्यते
units.iast: avivekāt parābhāvaṃ yathā buddhir avet tathā । vivekāt tu parād anyaḥ svayaṃ cāpi na vidyate
units.translation: Just as through non-discrimination the intellect knows a separate existence, through discrimination no other than the supreme is found, nor anything separate itself.
units.editionTranslation: “Through lack of discrimination the intellect imagines another reality; through discrimination, no other than the supreme Self exists, nor does the Self become something else.”

units.label: Verse I.8.1
units.deva: चितिस्वरूपं स्वत एव मे मते रसादियोगस् तव मोहकारितः । अतो न किंचित् तव चेष्टितेन मे फलं भवेत् सर्वविशेषहानतः
units.iast: citisvarūpaṃ svata eva me mate rasādiyogas tava mohakāritaḥ । ato na kiṃcit tava ceṣṭitena me phalaṃ bhavet sarvaviśeṣahānataḥ
units.translation: My nature is consciousness alone. In my view, your connection with taste and the rest is made by delusion. Therefore nothing would be a result for me from your actions, because all distinctions have been given up.

gloss.en: connection with taste and the rest
because of giving up all distinctions

units.editionTranslation: “By nature I am pure consciousness; your connection with taste and the rest is caused by delusion. Since every distinction is relinquished, nothing you do can produce a result for me.”

units.label: Verse I.8.2
units.deva: विमुच्य मायामयकार्यताम् इह प्रशान्तिम् आयाह्य् असदीहितात् सदा । अहं परं ब्रह्म सदा विमुक्तवत् तथाजम् एकं द्वयवर्जितं यतः
units.iast: vimucya māyāmayakāryatām iha praśāntim āyāhy asadīhitāt sadā । ahaṃ paraṃ brahma sadā vimuktavat tathājam ekaṃ dvayavarjitaṃ yataḥ
units.translation: Release yourself here from being an effect of māyā; always come to peace, away from false desire. I am the supreme Brahman, always free, unborn, one, and without a second.

gloss.en: the state of being an effect made by māyā

units.editionTranslation: “Free yourself from the effects fashioned by māyā and always come to peace, away from false desires. I am ever-free, unborn, one and without a second—the supreme Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.8.3
units.deva: सदा च भूतेषु समो ऽस्मि केवलो यथा च खं सर्वगम् अक्षरं शिवम् । निरन्तरं निष्कलम् अक्रियं परं ततो न मे ऽस्तीह फलं तवेहितैः
units.iast: sadā ca bhūteṣu samo 'smi kevalo yathā ca khaṃ sarvagam akṣaraṃ śivam । nirantaraṃ niṣkalam akriyaṃ paraṃ tato na me 'stīha phalaṃ tavehitaiḥ
units.translation: I am always equal in beings, alone, like space, all-pervading, imperishable, pure, continuous, partless, actionless, and supreme. Therefore your efforts bring me no result here.
units.editionTranslation: “I am always equal in all beings, alone, all-pervading and imperishable like space, auspicious, without parts, actionless and supreme. Therefore your deeds bring me no result.”

units.label: Verse I.8.4
units.deva: अहं ममैको न तदन्यद् इष्यते तथा न कस्याप्य् अहम् अस्म्य् असङ्गतः । असङ्गरूपो ऽहम् अतो न मे त्वया कृतेन कार्यं तव चाद्वयत्वतः
units.iast: ahaṃ mamaiko na tadanyad iṣyate tathā na kasyāpy aham asmy asaṅgataḥ । asaṅgarūpo 'ham ato na me tvayā kṛtena kāryaṃ tava cādvayatvataḥ
units.translation: I am one, and nothing is accepted as other than what is mine. Likewise, I belong to no one; I am unattached. I am by nature unattached. Therefore what you have done gives me no task, because you and I are nondual.
units.editionTranslation: “I alone am; nothing else is desired. I belong to no one, being unattached. My nature is nonattachment, so nothing is to be done by what you do, for you and I are nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.8.5
units.deva: फले च हेतौ च जनो विषक्तवान् इति प्रचिन्त्याहम् अतो विमोक्षणे । जनस्य संवादम् इमं प्रकॢप्तवान् स्वरूपतत्त्वार्थविबोधकारणम्
units.iast: phale ca hetau ca jano viṣaktavān iti pracintyāham ato vimokṣaṇe । janasya saṃvādam imaṃ prakḷptavān svarūpatattvārthavibodhakāraṇam
units.translation: Having considered that people are attached to the result and the cause, I therefore composed this dialogue to free people, as a means for understanding the truth of their own nature.

gloss.en: a means for understanding the truth of one’s own nature

units.editionTranslation: “Seeing that people are attached to actions and their fruits, I have composed this dialogue to free them and reveal the truth of their own nature.”

units.label: Verse I.8.6
units.deva: संवादम् एतं यदि चिन्तयेन् नरो विमुच्यते ऽज्ञानमहाभयागमात् । विमुक्तकामश् च तथा जनः सदा चरत्य् अशोकः सम आत्मवित् सुखी
units.iast: saṃvādam etaṃ yadi cintayen naro vimucyate 'jñānamahābhayāgamāt । vimuktakāmaś ca tathā janaḥ sadā caraty aśokaḥ sama ātmavit sukhī
units.translation: If a person reflects on this dialogue, that person is freed from the arising of the great fear of ignorance. Thus freed from desire, a person always moves without sorrow, even-minded, a knower of the Self, and happy.

gloss.en: from the coming of great fear from ignorance

units.editionTranslation: “A person who reflects on this dialogue is freed from the great terror of ignorance. Released from desire, the knower of the Self lives always without sorrow, in equanimity and happiness.”

units.label: Verse I.9.1
units.deva: सूक्ष्मताव्यापिते ज्ञेये गन्धादेर् उत्तरोत्तरम् । प्रत्यगात्मावसानेषु पूर्वपूर्वप्रहाणतः
units.iast: sūkṣmatāvyāpite jñeye gandhāder uttarottaram । pratyagātmāvasāneṣu pūrvapūrvaprahāṇataḥ
units.translation: What is to be known becomes subtler and more pervasive, step by step from smell onward, by giving up each prior thing, ending in the innermost Self.

gloss.en: in what is to be known
in steps ending in the innermost Self
by giving up each prior thing

units.editionTranslation: “The knowable becomes progressively subtler and more pervasive, from smell onward; by giving up each earlier element, one comes to the innermost Self.”

units.label: Verse I.9.2
units.deva: शारीरा पृथिवी तावद् यावद् बाह्या प्रमाणतः । अबादीनि च तत्त्वानि तावज् ज्ञेयानि कृत्स्नशः
units.iast: śārīrā pṛthivī tāvad yāvad bāhyā pramāṇataḥ । abādīni ca tattvāni tāvaj jñeyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ
units.translation: The bodily earth extends only as far as external knowledge reaches. The elements beginning with water are likewise to be known completely, each in its proper extent.
units.editionTranslation: “The body made of earth extends only as far as external evidence reaches; in the same way, the elements beginning with water are each to be understood completely.”

units.label: Verse I.9.3
units.deva: वाय्वादीनां यथोत्पत्तेः पूर्वं खं सर्वगं तथा । अहम् एकः सदा सर्वश् चिन्मात्रः सर्वगो ऽद्वयः
units.iast: vāyvādīnāṃ yathotpatteḥ pūrvaṃ khaṃ sarvagaṃ tathā । aham ekaḥ sadā sarvaś cinmātraḥ sarvago 'dvayaḥ
units.translation: Just as space is all-pervading before air and the other elements arise, so I alone am always all: consciousness alone, all-pervading, and nondual.
units.editionTranslation: “As space pervades all before the emergence of air and the other elements, so I alone am always all: pure consciousness, all-pervading and nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.9.4
units.deva: ब्रह्माद्याः स्थावरान्ता ये प्राणिनो मम पूः स्मृताः । कामक्रोधादयो दोषा जायेरन् मे कुतो ऽन्यतः
units.iast: brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāntā ye prāṇino mama pūḥ smṛtāḥ । kāmakrodhādayo doṣā jāyeran me kuto 'nyataḥ
units.translation: All living beings, from Brahmā to the unmoving, are considered my dwelling. From what other source could defects such as desire and anger arise in me?
units.editionTranslation: “All beings, from Brahmā down to the motionless, are said to be my dwelling. From what other source could faults such as desire and anger arise in me?”

units.label: Verse I.9.5
units.deva: भूतदोषैः सदास्पृष्टं सर्वभूतस्थम् ईश्वरम् । नीलं व्योम यथा बालो दुष्टं मां वीक्षते जनः
units.iast: bhūtadoṣaiḥ sadāspṛṣṭaṃ sarvabhūtastham īśvaram । nīlaṃ vyoma yathā bālo duṣṭaṃ māṃ vīkṣate janaḥ
units.translation: As a child sees the sky as blue, so a person sees me, the Lord dwelling in all beings, as tainted by their defects, though I am always untouched by them.
units.editionTranslation: “Though untouched by the defects of beings, the Lord dwells in every being. Like a child who sees the clear sky as blue, a person sees me as tainted.”

units.label: Verse I.9.6
units.deva: मच्चैतन्यावभास्यत्वात् सर्वप्राणिधियां सदा । पूर् मम प्राणिनः सर्वे सर्वज्ञस्य विपाप्मनः
units.iast: maccaitanyāvabhāsyatvāt sarvaprāṇidhiyāṃ sadā । pūr mama prāṇinaḥ sarve sarvajñasya vipāpmanaḥ
units.translation: Because the intellects of all living beings are always illuminated by my consciousness, all beings are my dwelling; I am all-knowing and free from sin.

gloss.en: because they are illuminated by my consciousness

units.editionTranslation: “Because I am the awareness in which every living being’s intellect appears, all beings are my dwelling; I am all-knowing and free from evil.”

units.label: Verse I.9.7
units.deva: जनिमज् ज्ञानविज्ञेयं स्वप्नज्ञानवद् इष्यते । नित्यं निर्विषयं ज्ञानं तस्माद् द्वैतं न विद्यते
units.iast: janimaj jñānavijñeyaṃ svapnajñānavad iṣyate । nityaṃ nirviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tasmād dvaitaṃ na vidyate
units.translation: Knowledge that arises and is known is considered like dream-knowledge. Eternal knowledge has no object; therefore duality is not found.
units.editionTranslation: “Knowledge that arises and is known is like the knowledge of a dream. Knowledge that is eternal has no object; therefore duality does not exist.”

units.label: Verse I.9.8
units.deva: ज्ञातुर् ज्ञातिर् हि नित्योक्ता सुषुप्ते त्व् अन्यशून्यतः । जाग्रज्ज्ञातिस् त्व् अविद्यातस् तद् ग्राह्यं चासद् इष्यताम्
units.iast: jñātur jñātir hi nityoktā suṣupte tv anyaśūnyataḥ । jāgrajjñātis tv avidyātas tad grāhyaṃ cāsad iṣyatām
units.translation: The knower’s knowing is indeed said to be eternal, because in deep sleep there is no other. But waking cognition comes from ignorance; let its object be considered unreal.
units.editionTranslation: “The knower’s awareness is said to be eternal; in deep sleep there is no second thing. Waking awareness depends on ignorance, so what it grasps may be regarded as unreal.”

units.label: Verse I.9.9
units.deva: रूपवत्त्वाद्यसत्त्वान् न दृष्ट्यादेः कर्मता यथा । एवं विज्ञानकर्मत्वं भूम्नो नास्तीति गम्यते
units.iast: rūpavattvādyasattvān na dṛṣṭyādeḥ karmatā yathā । evaṃ vijñānakarmatvaṃ bhūmno nāstīti gamyate
units.translation: Just as sight and the rest are not objects because qualities such as form are absent, so it is understood that fullness is not an object of cognition.

gloss.en: because form and the rest are absent

units.editionTranslation: “Just as sight itself does not become an action because it lacks form and the other properties, so the fullness of awareness is not an object of cognition.”

units.label: Verse I.10.1
units.deva: दृशिस्वरूपं गगनोपमं परं सकृद्विभातं त्व् अजम् एकम् अक्षरम् । अलेपकं सर्वगतं यद् अद्वयं तद् एव चाहं सततं विमुक्त ओम्
units.iast: dṛśisvarūpaṃ gaganopamaṃ paraṃ sakṛdvibhātaṃ tv ajam ekam akṣaram । alepakaṃ sarvagataṃ yad advayaṃ tad eva cāhaṃ satataṃ vimukta om
units.translation: I am that very nondual, always-free reality: supreme, like space, the nature of seeing, shining all at once, unborn, one, imperishable, unstained, and all-pervading. Om.
units.editionTranslation: “I am the supreme witnessing nature, like space, shining all at once, unborn, one, imperishable, unstained and all-pervading. I am nondual and always free. Om.”

units.label: Verse I.10.2
units.deva: दृशिस् तु शुद्धो ऽहम् अविक्रियात्मको न मे ऽस्ति कश्चिद् विषयः स्वभावतः । पुरस् तिरश् चोर्ध्वम् अधश् च सर्वतः सुपूर्णभूमा त्व् अज आत्मनि स्थितः
units.iast: dṛśis tu śuddho 'ham avikriyātmako na me 'sti kaścid viṣayaḥ svabhāvataḥ । puras tiraś cordhvam adhaś ca sarvataḥ supūrṇabhūmā tv aja ātmani sthitaḥ
units.translation: I am pure seeing, unchanging in nature; by nature I have no object. In front, across, above, below—everywhere—I am the completely full, unborn reality, established in the Self.
units.editionTranslation: “I am pure awareness, unchanging by nature. No object is my nature. Before, behind, above, below and everywhere, I am the fullness, unborn and established in the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.10.3
units.deva: अजो ऽमरश् चैव तथाजरो ऽमृतः स्वयंप्रभः सर्वगतो ऽहम् अद्वयः । न कारणं कार्यम् अतीव निर्मलः सदैव तृप्तश् च ततो विमुक्त ओम्
units.iast: ajo 'maraś caiva tathājaro 'mṛtaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ sarvagato 'ham advayaḥ । na kāraṇaṃ kāryam atīva nirmalaḥ sadaiva tṛptaś ca tato vimukta om
units.translation: I am unborn, deathless, ageless, immortal, self-luminous, all-pervading, and nondual. I am no cause or effect, completely pure, always satisfied, and therefore free. Om.
units.editionTranslation: “I am unborn, undying, ageless, immortal, self-luminous, all-pervading and nondual; perfectly pure, beyond cause and effect, always fulfilled, and therefore free. Om.”

units.label: Verse I.10.4
units.deva: सुषुप्तजाग्रत्स्वपतश् च दर्शनं न मे ऽस्ति किंचित् स्वम् इवेह मोहनम् । स्वतश् च तेषां परतो ऽप्य् असत्त्वतस् तुरीय एवास्मि सदा दृग् अद्वयः
units.iast: suṣuptajāgratsvapataś ca darśanaṃ na me 'sti kiṃcit svam iveha mohanam । svataś ca teṣāṃ parato 'py asattvatas turīya evāsmi sadā dṛg advayaḥ
units.translation: I have no experience of anything as mine here in deep sleep, waking, or dreaming; they are delusion. Because they are unreal in themselves and through another, I am always the Fourth, the nondual Seer.
units.editionTranslation: “I have no experience of anything as my own in deep sleep, waking or dream, which are delusive. Since they are unreal in themselves and through something else, I am ever the Fourth: the nondual Seer.”

units.label: Verse I.10.5
units.deva: शरीरबुद्धीन्द्रियदुःखसंततिर् न मे न चाहं मम निर्विकारतः । असत्त्वहेतोश् च तथैव संततेर् असत्त्वम् अस्याः स्वपतो हि दृश्यवत्
units.iast: śarīrabuddhīndriyaduḥkhasaṃtatir na me na cāhaṃ mama nirvikārataḥ । asattvahetoś ca tathaiva saṃtater asattvam asyāḥ svapato hi dṛśyavat
units.translation: The body, intellect, senses, and series of suffering are not mine; because I am changeless, they are not “I” or “mine.” For the same reason this series is unreal, like things seen by one who sleeps.
units.editionTranslation: “The body, intellect, senses and stream of suffering are not mine; because I am changeless, I am not them. Like appearances in a dream, this stream is unreal because it has no real ground.”

units.label: Verse I.10.6
units.deva: इदं तु सत्यं मम नास्ति विक्रिया विकारहेतुर् न हि मे ऽद्वयत्वतः । न पुण्यपापे न च मोक्षबन्धने न चास्ति वर्णाश्रमताशरीरतः
units.iast: idaṃ tu satyaṃ mama nāsti vikriyā vikārahetur na hi me 'dvayatvataḥ । na puṇyapāpe na ca mokṣabandhane na cāsti varṇāśramatāśarīrataḥ
units.translation: This is true: no change exists in me, and no cause of change exists for me because I am nondual. I have no merit or demerit, no bondage or liberation, nor caste, life-stage, or body.
units.editionTranslation: “There is no change in me; this is true. Because I am nondual, I have no cause of change. I have neither merit nor demerit, bondage nor liberation, nor caste, stage of life or body.”

units.label: Verse I.10.7
units.deva: अनादितो निर्गुणतो न कर्म मे फलं च तस्मात् परमो ऽहम् अद्वयः । यथा नभः सर्वगतं न लिप्यते तथा ह्य् अहं देहगतो ऽपि सूक्ष्मतः
units.iast: anādito nirguṇato na karma me phalaṃ ca tasmāt paramo 'ham advayaḥ । yathā nabhaḥ sarvagataṃ na lipyate tathā hy ahaṃ dehagato 'pi sūkṣmataḥ
units.translation: Because I am beginningless and without qualities, I have neither action nor result. Therefore I am supreme and nondual. As all-pervading space is unstained, so I, though dwelling in the body, am subtle.
units.editionTranslation: “I am without beginning and without qualities; I have no action and therefore no result. I am supreme and nondual. Like space, I remain unstained though subtly present in the body.”

units.label: Verse I.10.8
units.deva: सदा च भूतेषु समो ऽहम् ईश्वरः क्षराक्षराभ्यां परमो ह्य् अथोत्तमः । परात्मतत्त्वश् च तथाद्वयो ऽपि सन् विपर्ययेणाभिवृतस् त्व् अविद्यया
units.iast: sadā ca bhūteṣu samo 'ham īśvaraḥ kṣarākṣarābhyāṃ paramo hy athottamaḥ । parātmatattvaś ca tathādvayo 'pi san viparyayeṇābhivṛtas tv avidyayā
units.translation: I am always equal in all beings, the Lord, beyond the perishable and imperishable, and highest. I am the nondual truth of the supreme Self, yet through error I seem covered by ignorance.

gloss.en: the truth of the supreme Self

units.editionTranslation: “I am the Lord, equal in all beings, beyond the perishable and the imperishable, highest, and the nondual truth of the supreme Self; yet ignorance covers me through a mistaken appearance.”

units.label: Verse I.10.9
units.deva: अविद्यया भावनया च कर्मभिर् विविक्त आत्माव्यवधिः सुनिर्मलः । दृगादिशक्तिप्रचितो ऽहम् अद्वयः स्थितः स्वरूपे गगनं यथाचलम्
units.iast: avidyayā bhāvanayā ca karmabhir vivikta ātmāvyavadhiḥ sunirmalaḥ । dṛgādiśaktipracito 'ham advayaḥ sthitaḥ svarūpe gaganaṃ yathācalam
units.translation: Separate from ignorance, thought, and actions, I am the Self, limitless and very pure. Filled with the power of seeing and the rest, I am nondual and remain in my own nature, unmoving like space.

gloss.en: filled with the power of seeing and the rest

units.editionTranslation: “Distinct, pure and without limit, I am awareness alone, filled with the power of seeing and the rest. Ignorance and its imaginings do not touch me; I remain in my own nature, unmoving like space.”

units.label: Verse I.10.10
units.deva: अहं परं ब्रह्म विनिश्चयात्मदृङ् न जायते भूय इति श्रुतेर् वचः । न चैव बीजे त्व् असति प्रजायते फलं न जन्मास्ति ततो ह्य् अमोहता
units.iast: ahaṃ paraṃ brahma viniścayātmadṛṅ na jāyate bhūya iti śruter vacaḥ । na caiva bīje tv asati prajāyate phalaṃ na janmāsti tato hy amohatā
units.translation: “I am the supreme Brahman” is a firm vision of the Self; scripture says one is not born again. When the seed is absent, no fruit arises. Therefore there is no delusion.

gloss.en: a firm vision of the Self

units.editionTranslation: “I am the supreme Brahman”—this is the Self’s decisive vision; scripture says one is not born again. Without a seed, no fruit arises, and so there is no rebirth when delusion is gone.”

units.label: Verse I.10.11
units.deva: ममेदम् इत्थं च तवाद ईदृशं तथाहम् एवं न परो ऽपि चान्यथा । विमूढतैवास्य जनस्य कल्पना सदा समे ब्रह्मणि वाद्वये शिवे
units.iast: mamedam itthaṃ ca tavāda īdṛśaṃ tathāham evaṃ na paro 'pi cānyathā । vimūḍhataivāsya janasya kalpanā sadā same brahmaṇi vādvaye śive
units.translation: “This is mine, this is so; that of yours is of such a kind; likewise I am so, and another is not otherwise”—this imagining belongs only to the deluded person, in always-equal, nondual, auspicious Brahman.
units.editionTranslation: “‘This is mine,’ ‘you are this,’ ‘I am this,’ and ‘another is otherwise’—such imaginings belong to the deluded person, in the equal, auspicious, nondual Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.10.12
units.deva: यद् अद्वयं ज्ञानम् अतीव निर्मलं महात्मनां तत्र न शोकमोहता । तयोर् अभावे न हि कर्म जन्म वा भवेद् अयं वेदविदां विनिश्चयः
units.iast: yad advayaṃ jñānam atīva nirmalaṃ mahātmanāṃ tatra na śokamohatā । tayor abhāve na hi karma janma vā bhaved ayaṃ vedavidāṃ viniścayaḥ
units.translation: In the very pure, nondual knowledge of the great ones, there is no grief or delusion. When those two are absent, action or birth cannot arise; this is the certain conclusion of Veda-knowers.

gloss.en: of the knowers of the Veda

units.editionTranslation: “In the perfectly pure, nondual knowledge of the great Self there is no grief or delusion. When both are absent, there can be no action or birth; this is the settled understanding of those who know the Veda.”

units.label: Verse I.10.13
units.deva: सुषुप्तवज् जाग्रति यो न पश्यति द्वयं तु पश्यन्न् अपि चाद्वयत्वतः । तथा च कुर्वन्न् अपि निष्क्रियश् च यः स आत्मविन् नान्य इतीह निश्चयः
units.iast: suṣuptavaj jāgrati yo na paśyati dvayaṃ tu paśyann api cādvayatvataḥ । tathā ca kurvann api niṣkriyaś ca yaḥ sa ātmavin nānya itīha niścayaḥ
units.translation: One who, while awake, sees no duality as in deep sleep, but even while seeing [knows] nonduality, and who acts yet is actionless—that one is a knower of the Self, none other: this is the certainty here.
units.editionTranslation: “One who, awake, sees no duality as in deep sleep, and who, even while seeing, sees nondually; who acts and yet is actionless—that one is a knower of the Self, none other.”

units.label: Verse I.10.14
units.deva: इतीदम् उक्तं परमार्थदर्शनं मया हि वेदान्तविनिश्चितं परम् । विमुच्यते ऽस्मिन् यदि निश्चितो भवेन् न लिप्यते व्योमवद् एव कर्मभिः
units.iast: itīdam uktaṃ paramārthadarśanaṃ mayā hi vedāntaviniścitaṃ param । vimucyate 'smin yadi niścito bhaven na lipyate vyomavad eva karmabhiḥ
units.translation: This highest vision of reality, determined by Vedānta, has thus been taught by me. If someone becomes certain in this, that person is freed and is not stained by actions, just as space is not stained.
units.editionTranslation: “This highest vision of reality, established by Vedānta, has been taught by me. Whoever becomes certain of it is freed and is not stained by actions, as space is unstained.”

units.label: Verse I.11.1
units.deva: ईक्षितृत्वं स्वतःसिद्धं जन्तूनां च ततो ऽन्यता । अज्ञानाद् इत्य् अतो ऽन्यत्वं सद् असीति निवर्त्यते
units.iast: īkṣitṛtvaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ jantūnāṃ ca tato 'nyatā । ajñānād ity ato 'nyatvaṃ sad asīti nivartyate
units.translation: The state of being the seer is established by itself, and the otherness of living beings from it comes from ignorance. Therefore, the words “You are existence” remove this otherness.

gloss.en: the state of being the seer

units.editionTranslation: “The sense of agency is self-established, and the distinction from other beings arises through ignorance. The words ‘You are that’ remove this apparent otherness.”

units.label: Verse I.11.2
units.deva: एतावद् ध्य् अमृतत्वं न किंचिद् अन्यत् सहायकम् । ज्ञानस्येति ब्रुवच् छास्त्रं सलिङ्गं कर्म बाधते
units.iast: etāvad dhy amṛtatvaṃ na kiṃcid anyat sahāyakam । jñānasyeti bruvac chāstraṃ saliṅgaṃ karma bādhate
units.translation: This alone is immortality; nothing else aids knowledge. Scripture says this and refutes action together with its marks.
units.editionTranslation: “This alone is immortality; nothing else assists it. Scripture, teaching that knowledge is sufficient, refutes action and its accompanying rites.”

units.label: Verse I.11.3
units.deva: सर्वेषां मनसो वृत्तम् अविशेषेण पश्यतः । तस्य मे निर्विकारस्य विशेषः स्यात् कथंचन
units.iast: sarveṣāṃ manaso vṛttam aviśeṣeṇa paśyataḥ । tasya me nirvikārasya viśeṣaḥ syāt kathaṃcana
units.translation: I see the activity of every mind without distinction. How could there be any difference in me, who am changeless?
units.editionTranslation: “I see without distinction the activity of every mind. How could there be any difference in me, who am changeless?”

units.label: Verse I.11.4
units.deva: मनोवृत्तं मनश् चैव स्वप्नवज् जाग्रतीक्षितुः । संप्रसादे द्वयासत्त्वाच् चिन्मात्रः सर्वगो ऽद्वयः
units.iast: manovṛttaṃ manaś caiva svapnavaj jāgratīkṣituḥ । saṃprasāde dvayāsattvāc cinmātraḥ sarvago 'dvayaḥ
units.translation: For the waking seer, the activity of mind and the mind itself are like a dream. In deep repose, because both are unreal, I am consciousness alone, all-pervading and nondual.
units.editionTranslation: “For the Seer in waking, the mind’s activity and the mind itself are like a dream. In deep repose, when neither is present, I am pure consciousness, all-pervading and nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.11.5
units.deva: स्वप्नः सत्यो यथाबोधाद् देहात्मत्वं तथैव च । प्रत्यक्षादेः प्रमाणत्वं जाग्रत् स्याद् आत्मवेदनात्
units.iast: svapnaḥ satyo yathābodhād dehātmatvaṃ tathaiva ca । pratyakṣādeḥ pramāṇatvaṃ jāgrat syād ātmavedanāt
units.translation: Just as a dream is real until awakening, so too is the body taken as the Self. Perception and the rest are valid in waking until knowledge of the Self.
units.editionTranslation: “A dream seems real until awakening; so too does identification of the Self with the body. Perception and the other means of knowledge seem valid in waking until knowledge of the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.11.6
units.deva: व्योमवत् सर्वभूतस्थो भूतदोषैर् विवर्जितः । साक्षी चेतागुणः शुद्धो ब्रह्मैवास्मीति केवलः
units.iast: vyomavat sarvabhūtastho bhūtadoṣair vivarjitaḥ । sākṣī cetāguṇaḥ śuddho brahmaivāsmīti kevalaḥ
units.translation: Like space, dwelling in all beings and free from their defects, I am the witness, conscious, without qualities, pure, and Brahman alone.
units.editionTranslation: “Like space, I dwell in all beings and am free of their defects. I am the witness, conscious, without qualities, pure, and none other than Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.11.7
units.deva: नामरूपक्रियाभ्यो ऽन्यो नित्यमुक्तस्वरूपवान् । अहम् आत्मा परं ब्रह्म चिन्मात्रो ऽहं सदाद्वयः
units.iast: nāmarūpakriyābhyo 'nyo nityamuktasvarūpavān । aham ātmā paraṃ brahma cinmātro 'haṃ sadādvayaḥ
units.translation: Other than name, form, and action, and having an eternally free nature, I am the Self, the supreme Brahman, consciousness alone, always nondual.
units.editionTranslation: “Beyond name, form and action, eternally free in nature, I am the Self, the supreme Brahman, pure consciousness, ever nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.11.8
units.deva: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि कर्ता च भोक्ता चास्मीति ये विदुः । ते नष्टा ज्ञानकर्मभ्यां नास्तिकाः स्युर् न संशयः
units.iast: ahaṃ brahmāsmi kartā ca bhoktā cāsmīti ye viduḥ । te naṣṭā jñanakarmabhyāṃ nāstikāḥ syur na saṃśayaḥ
units.translation: Those who know “I am Brahman” and also “I am the doer and experiencer” are ruined with respect to knowledge and action; they are deniers of the truth, without doubt.

gloss.en: with respect to knowledge and action

units.editionTranslation: “Those who think ‘I am Brahman’ and at the same time ‘I am the doer and enjoyer’ are lost to both knowledge and action; without doubt, they are nihilists.”

units.label: Verse I.11.9
units.deva: धर्माधर्मफलैर् योग इष्टो ऽदृष्टो यथात्मनः । शास्त्राद् ब्रह्मत्वम् अप्य् अस्य मोक्षो ज्ञानात् तथेष्यताम्
units.iast: dharmādharmaphalair yoga iṣṭo 'dṛṣṭo yathātmanaḥ । śāstrād brahmatvam apy asya mokṣo jñānāt tatheṣyatām
units.translation: As the Self’s connection with the unseen fruits of merit and demerit is accepted, so let this person’s being Brahman be accepted from scripture, and liberation from knowledge.

gloss.en: with the fruits of merit and demerit

units.editionTranslation: “As the Self is connected with the unseen fruits of merit and demerit, so let Brahmanhood be accepted on the authority of scripture and liberation on the authority of knowledge.”

units.label: Verse I.11.10
units.deva: या माहारजनाद्यास् ता वासनाः स्वप्नदर्शिभिः । अनुभूयन्त एवेह ततो ऽन्यः केवलो दृशिः
units.iast: yā māhārajanādyās tā vāsanāḥ svapnadarśibhiḥ । anubhūyanta eveha tato 'nyaḥ kevalo dṛśiḥ
units.translation: Whatever latent impressions, such as saffron-dyed garments and the rest, are experienced here by dream-seers, from those I am other: the Seer alone.
units.editionTranslation: “Those who dream experience impressions such as garlands and the rest; therefore I am the pure Seer, other than these.”

units.label: Verse I.11.11
units.deva: कोशाद् इव विनिष्कृष्टः कार्यकारणवर्जितः । यथासिर् दृश्यते स्वप्ने तद्वद् बोद्धा स्वयंप्रभः
units.iast: kośād iva viniṣkṛṣṭaḥ kāryakāraṇavarjitaḥ । yathāsir dṛśyate svapne tadvad boddhā svayaṃprabhaḥ
units.translation: Like a sword drawn from its sheath and free from effect and cause, the knower is seen in a dream, self-luminous.
units.editionTranslation: “Like a sword drawn out from its sheath, the knower is seen in a dream as free of cause and effect, self-luminous.”

units.label: Verse I.11.12
units.deva: आपेषात् प्रतिबुद्धस्य ज्ञस्य स्वाभाविकं पदम् । उक्तं नेत्यादिवाक्येन कल्पितस्यापनेतृणा
units.iast: āpeṣāt pratibuddhasya jñasya svābhāvikaṃ padam । uktaṃ netyādivākyena kalpitasyāpanetṛṇā
units.translation: The natural state of the awakened knower, from that moment onward, is taught by the words “not this” and the rest, which remove what was imagined.
units.editionTranslation: “The natural state of the awakened knower, from the moment of awakening onward, is taught by the words ‘not this, not this,’ which remove what was imagined.”

units.label: Verse I.11.13
units.deva: महाराजादयो लोका मयि यद्वत् प्रकल्पिताः । स्वप्ने तद्वद् द्वयं विद्याद् रूपं वासनया सह
units.iast: mahārājādayo lokā mayi yadvat prakalpitāḥ । svapne tadvad dvayaṃ vidyād rūpaṃ vāsanayā saha
units.translation: Just as great kings and worlds are imagined in me, so in a dream one should know the two: form together with its latent impression.
units.editionTranslation: “Just as great kings and other worlds are imagined in me, so in a dream one should understand the two—the visible form and its latent impression—as imagined.”

units.label: Verse I.11.14
units.deva: देहलिङ्गात्मना कार्या वासनारूपिणा क्रिया । नेतिनेत्यात्मरूपत्वान् न मे कार्या क्रिया क्वचित्
units.iast: dehaliṅgātmanā kāryā vāsanārūpiṇā kriyā । netinetyātmarūpatvān na me kāryā kriyā kvacit
units.translation: Action to be done belongs to the body and subtle body, taking the form of latent impressions. Because my nature is taught as “not this, not this,” I never have action to do.

gloss.en: in the form of body and subtle body
having the form of latent impressions
because of the nature of the Self

units.editionTranslation: “Action belongs to the body and subtle body, arising from impressions; I have no action at any time, for my nature is taught as ‘not this, not this.’”

units.label: Verse I.11.15
units.deva: न ततो ऽमृतताशास्ति कर्मणो ऽज्ञानहेतुतः । मोक्षस्य ज्ञानहेतुत्वान् न तदन्यद् अपेक्षते
units.iast: na tato 'mṛtatāśāsti karmaṇo 'jñānahetutaḥ । mokṣasya jñānahetutvān na tadanyad apekṣate
units.translation: Immortality is not expected from action, because ignorance is its cause. Since knowledge is the cause of liberation, liberation requires nothing else.
units.editionTranslation: “Action cannot bring immortality, since ignorance is its cause; liberation comes from knowledge and depends on nothing else.”

units.label: Verse I.11.16
units.deva: अमृतं चाभयं नार्तं नेतीत्यात्मा प्रियो मम । विपरीतम् अतो ऽन्यद् यत् त्यजेत् तत् सक्रियं ततः
units.iast: amṛtaṃ cābhayaṃ nārtaṃ netītyātmā priyo mama । viparītam ato 'nyad yat tyajet tat sakriyaṃ tataḥ
units.translation: The Self is immortal, fearless, and untroubled, taught by “not this, not this,” and dear to me. Whatever is its opposite one should abandon, since it is connected with action.
units.editionTranslation: “The Self, taught as immortal, fearless and free of sorrow by ‘not this, not this,’ is dear to me. Whatever is its opposite should be abandoned as bound to action.”

units.label: Verse I.12.1
units.deva: प्रकाशस्थं यथा देहं सालोकम् अभिमन्यते । द्रष्ट्राभासं तथा चित्तं द्रष्टाहम् इति मन्यते
units.iast: prakāśasthaṃ yathā dehaṃ sālokam abhimanyate । draṣṭrābhāsaṃ tathā cittaṃ draṣṭāham iti manyate
units.translation: Just as a body in light is thought to shine with that light, so the mind, reflecting the Seer, thinks, “I am the Seer.”
units.editionTranslation: “Just as a body in light is imagined to shine by its own light, so the mind, reflecting the Seer, imagines ‘I am the Seer.’”

units.label: Verse I.12.2
units.deva: यद् एव दृश्यते लोके तेनाभिन्नत्वम् आत्मनः । प्रपद्यते ततो मूढस् तेनात्मानं न विन्दति
units.iast: yad eva dṛṣyate loke tenābhinnatvam ātmanaḥ । prapadyate tato mūḍhas tenātmānaṃ na vindati
units.translation: The deluded person takes the Self to be non-different from whatever is seen in the world; because of that, the person does not find the Self.
units.editionTranslation: “The ignorant person identifies the Self with whatever is seen in the world; because of this, that person does not find the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.12.3
units.deva: दशमस्य नवात्मत्वप्रतिपत्तिवद् आत्मनः । दृश्येषु तद्वद् एवायं मूढो लोको न चान्यथा
units.iast: daśamasya navātmatvapratipattivad ātmanaḥ । dṛśyeṣu tadvad evāyaṃ mūḍho loko na cānyathā
units.translation: Like the tenth person who counts himself as the ninth, this deluded world likewise takes the Self to be among visible things, and not otherwise.

gloss.en: like the belief that he is the ninth

units.editionTranslation: “Just as someone who counts the tenth person among the nine mistakes him for someone else, so too this deluded world mistakes the Self among visible things.”

units.label: Verse I.12.4
units.deva: त्वं कुरु त्वं तद् एवेति प्रत्ययाव् एककालिकौ । एकनीडौ कथं स्यातां विरुद्धौ न्यायतो वद
units.iast: tvaṃ kuru tvaṃ tad eveti pratyayāv ekakālikau । ekanīḍau kathaṃ syātāṃ viruddhau nyāyato vada
units.translation: “You act” and “you are exactly that”—how could these two simultaneous thoughts, having one place and contradicting each other, both be logical? Tell me.
units.editionTranslation: “‘You act’ and ‘you are that’—how can these two judgments, contradictory yet belonging to the same person, be true at the same time? Explain the reasoning.”

units.label: Verse I.12.5
units.deva: देहाभिमानिनो दुःखं नादेहस्य स्वभावतः । स्वापवत् तत्प्रहाणाय तत् त्वम् इत्य् उच्यते दृशेः
units.iast: dehābhimānino duḥkhaṃ nādehasya svabhāvataḥ । svāpavat tatprahāṇāya tat tvam ity ucyate dṛśeḥ
units.translation: Sorrow belongs to one who identifies with the body; it is not natural to the bodiless Self. As in sleep, “You are that” is said to the Seer to remove that [sorrow].

gloss.en: of one identified with the body

units.editionTranslation: “Sorrow belongs to one who identifies with the body; it is not the nature of the bodiless Self. As in a dream, the teaching ‘you are that’ is given to the Seer to end that sorrow.”

units.label: Verse I.12.6
units.deva: दृशेश् छाया यदारूढा मुखच्छायेव दर्शने । पश्यंस् तं प्रत्ययं योगी दृष्ट आत्मेति मन्यते
units.iast: dṛśeś chāyā yadārūḍhā mukhacchāyeva darśane । paśyaṃs taṃ pratyayaṃ yogī dṛṣṭa atmeti manyate
units.translation: When the Seer’s shadow has arisen in the mirror, like a face’s reflection, the yogi sees that cognition and thinks, “The Self has been seen.”
units.editionTranslation: “When the shadow of the Seer has risen in the vision, like the reflection of a face in a mirror, the yogin sees that cognition and thinks, ‘I have seen the Self.’”

units.label: Verse I.12.7
units.deva: तं च मूढं च यद्य् अन्यं प्रत्ययं वेत्ति नो दृशेः । स एव योगिनां श्रेष्ठो नेतरः स्यान् न संशयः
units.iast: taṃ ca mūḍhaṃ ca yady anyaṃ pratyayaṃ vetti no dṛśeḥ । sa eva yogināṃ śreṣṭho netaraḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ
units.translation: If one knows that cognition as other than both the deluded person and the Seer, that one alone is the best of yogis; no other is so, without doubt.
units.editionTranslation: “If one knows that cognition as distinct from the deluded person and from the Seer, that one is the best of yogins; no other is so.”

units.label: Verse I.12.8
units.deva: विज्ञातेर् यस् तु विज्ञाता स त्वम् इत्य् उच्यते यतः । स स्याद् अनुभवस् तस्य ततो ऽन्यो ऽनुभवो मृषा
units.iast: vijñāter yas tu vijñātā sa tvam ity ucyate yataḥ । sa syād anubhavas tasya tato 'nyo 'nubhavo mṛṣā
units.translation: Because the knower of awareness itself is called “you,” that is the person’s experience; any other experience than that is false.
units.editionTranslation: “Since the knower of awareness itself is called ‘you,’ that is the person’s own experience; any other experience is false.”

units.label: Verse I.12.9
units.deva: दृशिरूपे सदा नित्ये दर्शनादर्शने मयि । कथं स्यातां ततो नान्य इष्यते ऽनुभवस् ततः
units.iast: dṛśirūpe sadā nitye darśanādarśane mayi । kathaṃ syātāṃ tato nānya iṣyate 'nubhavas tataḥ
units.translation: In me, whose nature is seeing and who am always eternal, how could seeing and not-seeing occur? Therefore no other experience is accepted.
units.editionTranslation: “In me, the eternal nature of seeing, how could seeing and not seeing occur? Therefore no other experience is admitted.”

units.label: Verse I.12.10
units.deva: यत्स्थस् तापो रवेर् देहे दृशेः स विषयो यथा । सत्त्वस्थस् तद्वद् एवेह दृशेः स विषयस् तथा
units.iast: yatsthas tāpo raver dehe dṛśeḥ sa viṣayo yathā । sattvasthas tadvad eveha dṛśeḥ sa viṣayas tathā
units.translation: Just as heat situated in the sun’s body is an object of sight, so what is situated in purity is an object for the Seer.
units.editionTranslation: “Just as the heat located in the sun’s body is an object of sight, so what is established in the quality of purity is an object for the Seer.”

units.label: Verse I.12.11
units.deva: प्रतिषिद्धेदमंशो ज्ञः खम् इवैकरसो ऽद्वयः । नित्यमुक्तस् तथा शुद्धः सो ऽहं ब्रह्मास्मि केवलः
units.iast: pratiṣiddhedamaṃśo jñaḥ kham ivaikaraso 'dvayaḥ । nityamuktas tathā śuddhaḥ so 'haṃ brahmāsmi kevalaḥ
units.translation: The knower, having rejected the “this” part, is of one essence like space, nondual, always free, and pure. I alone am that Brahman.

gloss.en: one who has rejected the “this” part

units.editionTranslation: “The wise one, having rejected the ‘this’ portion, is one in essence like space, nondual, ever-free and pure. I alone am that Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.12.12
units.deva: विज्ञातुर् नैव विज्ञाता परो ऽन्यः संभवत्य् अतः । विज्ञाताहं परो मुक्तः सर्वभूतेषु सर्वदा
units.iast: vijñātur naiva vijñātā paro 'nyaḥ saṃbhavaty ataḥ । vijñātāhaṃ paro muktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā
units.translation: No other knower of the knower exists. Therefore I am the supreme knower, free in all beings, always.
units.editionTranslation: “There can be no other knower of the knower. Therefore I am the supreme knower, free always and in all beings.”

units.label: Verse I.12.13
units.deva: यो वेदालुप्तदृष्टित्वम् आत्मनो ऽकर्तृतां तथा । ब्रह्मवित्त्वं तथा मुक्त्वा स आत्मज्ञो न चेतरः
units.iast: yo vedāluptadṛṣṭitvam ātmano 'kartṛtāṃ tathā । brahmavittvaṃ tathā muktvā sa ātmajño na cetaraḥ
units.translation: Whoever knows the Self’s undiminished seeing, non-agency, being a knower of Brahman, and freedom is a knower of the Self, and no other.
units.editionTranslation: “One who knows the Self’s seeing as undiminished, its non-agency, its being Brahman and its freedom is a knower of the Self; no other is.”

units.label: Verse I.12.14
units.deva: ज्ञातैवाहम् अविज्ञेयः शुद्धो मुक्तः सदेत्य् अपि । विवेकी प्रत्ययो बुद्धेर् दृश्यत्वान् नाशवत्त्वतः
units.iast: jñātaivāham avijñeyaḥ śuddho muktaḥ sadety api । vivekī pratyayo buddher dṛśyatvān nāśavattvataḥ
units.translation: Even “I alone am the knower, unknowable, pure, and always free” is a discerning thought of the intellect, because the intellect is seen and perishable.
units.editionTranslation: “‘I alone am the knower, unknowable, pure and ever free’—this discernment is a thought in the intellect, because the intellect is seen and perishable.”

units.label: Verse I.12.15
units.deva: अलुप्ता त्व् आत्मनो दृष्टिर् नोत्पाद्या कारकैर् यतः । दृश्यया चान्यया दृष्ट्या जन्यतास्याः प्रकल्पिता
units.iast: aluptā tv ātmano dṛṣṭir notpādyā kārakair yataḥ । dṛśyayā cānyayā dṛṣṭyā janyatāsyāḥ prakalpitā
units.translation: The Self’s seeing is undiminished and is not to be produced by action-factors, because its production by another, visible act of seeing is imagined.
units.editionTranslation: “The Self’s seeing is never diminished and need not be produced by factors of action; its being produced by another, visible act of seeing is only imagined.”

units.label: Verse I.12.16
units.deva: देहात्मबुद्ध्यपेक्षत्वाद् आत्मनः कर्तृता मृषा । नैव किंचित् करोमीति सत्या बुद्धिः प्रमाणजा
units.iast: dehātmabuddhyapekṣatvād ātmanaḥ kartṛtā mṛṣā । naiva kiṃcit karomīti satyā buddhiḥ pramāṇajā
units.translation: The Self’s agency is false because it depends on the thought “the body is the Self.” The true cognition “I do nothing” is born from a valid means of knowledge.

gloss.en: because it depends on the thought “the body is the Self”
born from a valid means of knowledge

units.editionTranslation: “The Self’s agency is false because it depends on identifying with the body. The valid cognition ‘I do nothing’ is true.”

units.label: Verse I.12.17
units.deva: कर्तृत्वं कारकापेक्षम् अकर्तृत्वं स्वभावतः । कर्ता भोक्तेति विज्ञानं मृषैवेति सुनिश्चितम्
units.iast: kartṛtvaṃ kārakāpekṣam akartṛtvaṃ svabhāvataḥ । kartā bhokteti vijñānaṃ mṛṣaiveti suniścitam
units.translation: Agency depends on action-factors; non-agency is natural. The thought “I am the doer and experiencer” is certainly false.
units.editionTranslation: “Agency depends on the factors of action; non-agency is natural. The thought ‘I am the doer and enjoyer’ is certainly false.”

units.label: Verse I.12.18
units.deva: एवं शास्त्रानुमानाभ्यां स्वरूपे ऽवगते सति । नियोज्यो ऽहम् इति ह्य् एषा सत्या बुद्धिः कथं भवेत्
units.iast: evaṃ śāstrānumānābhyāṃ svarūpe 'vagate sati । niyojyo 'ham iti hy eṣā satyā buddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet
units.translation: When one’s own nature has been understood through scripture and reasoning, how could the thought “I must be enjoined to act” be true?
units.editionTranslation: “When one’s true nature has been understood through scripture and reasoning, how could the thought ‘I am one who must act’ be true?”

units.label: Verse I.12.19
units.deva: यथा सर्वान्तरं व्योम व्योम्नो ऽप्य् अभ्यन्तरो ह्य् अहम् । निर्विकारो ऽचलः शुद्धो ऽजरो मुक्तः सदाद्वयः
units.iast: yathā sarvāntaraṃ vyoma vyomno 'py abhyantaro hy aham । nirvikāro 'calaḥ śuddho 'jaro muktaḥ sadādvayaḥ
units.translation: Just as space is within all things, I am within even space: changeless, unmoving, pure, ageless, free, and always nondual.
units.editionTranslation: “As space is within all things, I am within even space: changeless, unmoving, pure, ageless, free and ever nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.13.1
units.deva: अचक्षुष्ट्वान् न दृष्टिर् मे तथाश्रोत्रस्य का श्रुतिः । अवाक्त्वान् न तु वक्तिः स्याद् अमनस्त्वान् मतिः कुतः
units.iast: acakṣuṣṭvān na dṛṣṭir me tathāśrotrasya kā śrutiḥ । avāktvān na tu vaktiḥ syād amanastvān matiḥ kutaḥ
units.translation: Because I have no eyes, I have no sight; likewise, without ears, what hearing could there be? Because I have no speech, I do not speak; without a mind, where could thought come from?
units.editionTranslation: “I have no sight, since I have no eyes; what hearing could there be without ears? Since I have no speech, I do not speak; without a mind, how could there be thought?”

units.label: Verse I.13.2
units.deva: अप्राणस्य न कर्मास्ति बुद्ध्यभावे न वेदिता । विद्याविद्ये ततो न स्तश् चिन्मात्रज्योतिषो मम
units.iast: aprāṇasya na karmāsti buddhyabhāve na veditā । vidyāvidye tato na staś cinmātrajyotiṣo mama
units.translation: For one without breath there is no action; when intellect is absent there is no knower. Therefore knowledge and ignorance do not exist for me, whose light is consciousness alone.
units.editionTranslation: “Without breath, I have no action; without intellect, no knower. For me, whose light is pure consciousness alone, there is neither knowledge nor ignorance.”

units.label: Verse I.13.3
units.deva: नित्यमुक्तस्य शुद्धस्य कूटस्थस्याविचालिनः । अमृतस्याक्षरस्यैवम् अशरीरस्य सर्वदा
units.iast: nityamuktasya śuddhasya kūṭasthasyāvicālinaḥ । amṛtasyākṣarasyaivam aśarīrasya sarvadā
units.translation: Thus I am always free, pure, unchanging, unmoving, immortal, imperishable, and bodiless.
units.editionTranslation: “Thus I am ever-free, pure, changeless, unmoving, immortal, imperishable and always bodiless.”

units.label: Verse I.13.4
units.deva: जिघत्सा वा पिपासा वा शोकमोहौ जरामृती । न विद्यन्ते ऽशरीरत्वाद् व्योमवद् व्यापिनो मम
units.iast: jighatsā vā pipāsā vā śokamohau jarāmṛtī । na vidyante 'śarīratvād vyomavad vyāpino mama
units.translation: Hunger or thirst, grief and delusion, old age and death do not exist for me, because I am bodiless and all-pervading like space.
units.editionTranslation: “Hunger and thirst, grief and delusion, old age and death do not exist for me, who am bodiless and all-pervading like space.”

units.label: Verse I.13.5
units.deva: अस्पर्शत्वान् न मे स्पृष्टिर् नाजिह्वत्वाद् रसज्ञता । नित्यविज्ञानरूपस्य ज्ञानाज्ञाने न मे सदा
units.iast: asparśatvān na me spṛṣṭir nājihvatvād rasajñatā । nityavijñānarūpasya jñānājñāne na me sadā
units.translation: Because I cannot be touched, touch is not mine; because I have no tongue, tasting is not mine. For me, whose nature is eternal awareness, knowledge and ignorance never exist.
units.editionTranslation: “Since I cannot be touched, I have no sensation of touch; having no tongue, I do not taste. I am eternally the nature of awareness, so knowledge and ignorance are never mine.”

units.label: Verse I.13.6
units.deva: या तु स्यान् मानसी वृत्तिश् चाक्षुष्का रूपरञ्जना । नित्यम् एवात्मनो दृष्ट्या नित्यया दृश्यते हि सा
units.iast: yā tu syān mānasī vṛttiś cākṣuṣkā rūparañjanā । nityam evātmano dṛṣṭyā nityayā dṛśyate hi sā
units.translation: Whatever mental thought colors itself with visible form is always seen by the Self’s eternal vision.
units.editionTranslation: “The mental thought that colors itself with visible form is always seen by the Self’s eternal vision.”

units.label: Verse I.13.7
units.deva: तथान्येन्द्रिययुक्ता या वृत्तयो विषयाञ्जनाः । स्मृती रागादिरूप च केवलान्तर् मनस्य् अपि
