units.iast: tathānyendriyayuktā yā vṛttayo viṣayāñjanāḥ । smṛtī rāgādirūpa ca kevalāntar manasy api
units.translation: Likewise, thoughts joined with other senses and colored by objects, memory, desire and the rest—even when only within the mind—[are seen].

gloss.en: having the form of desire and the rest

units.editionTranslation: “Likewise thoughts joined with other senses and colored by their objects, and memory, attachment and the rest, even when they occur only within the mind—”

units.label: Verse I.13.8
units.deva: मानस्यस् तद्वद् अन्यस्य दृश्यन्ते स्वप्नवृत्तयः । द्रष्टुर् दृष्टिस् ततो नित्या शुद्धानन्ता च केवला
units.iast: mānasyas tadvad anyasya dṛśyante svapnavṛttayaḥ । draṣṭur dṛṣṭis tato nityā śuddhānantā ca kevalā
units.translation: Dream-thoughts in another are seen in the same way. Therefore the Seer’s vision is eternal, pure, limitless, and alone.
units.editionTranslation: “—are seen like dream-thoughts in another. The Seer’s vision is therefore eternal, pure, infinite and alone.”

units.label: Verse I.13.9
units.deva: अनित्या साविशुद्धेति गृह्यते ऽत्राविवेकतः । सुखी दुःखी तथा चाहं दृश्ययोपाधिभूतया
units.iast: anityā sāviśuddheti gṛhyate 'trāvivekataḥ । sukhī duḥkhī tathā cāhaṃ dṛśyayopādhibhūtayā
units.translation: Through lack of discrimination, that vision is taken as impermanent and impure. Thus I am thought happy or unhappy through what is seen, which has become a limiting adjunct.
units.editionTranslation: “Through lack of discrimination it is mistaken for impermanent and impure; the whole world thinks ‘I am happy’ or ‘I am unhappy’ because of the seen limiting adjunct.”

units.label: Verse I.13.10
units.deva: मूढया मूढ इत्य् एवं शुद्धया शुद्ध इत्य् अपि । मन्यते सर्वलोको ऽयं येन संसारम् ऋच्छति
units.iast: mūḍhayā mūḍha ity evaṃ śuddhayā śuddha ity api । manyate sarvaloko 'yaṃ yena saṃsāram ṛcchati
units.translation: Through a deluded mind, one thinks “I am deluded”; through a pure mind, “I am pure.” Everyone thinks this way and enters worldly existence through it.
units.editionTranslation: “Deluded by a confused understanding, the world thinks itself deluded or pure, and so enters worldly existence.”

units.label: Verse I.13.11
units.deva: अचक्षुष्ट्वादिशास्त्रोक्तं सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं ह्य् अजम् । नित्यमुक्तम् इहात्मानं मुमुक्षुश् चेत् सदा स्मरेत्
units.iast: acakṣuṣṭvādiśāstroktaṃ sabāhyābhyantaraṃ hy ajam । nityamuktam ihātmānaṃ mumukṣuś cet sadā smaret
units.translation: If a seeker of liberation always remembers the Self here—unborn within and without, always free, as taught by scripture beginning “without eyes”—[that is the teaching].
units.editionTranslation: “If a seeker would always remember the Self, unborn inside and out, as taught by scripture through ‘without eyes’ and the rest, one is eternally free.”

units.label: Verse I.13.12
units.deva: अचक्षुष्ट्वादिशास्त्राच् च नेन्द्रियाणि सदा मम । अप्राणो ह्य् अमनाः शुभ्र इति चाथर्वणे वचः
units.iast: acakṣuṣṭvādiśāstrāc ca nendriyāṇi sadā mama । aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti cātharvaṇe vacaḥ
units.translation: Scripture beginning “without eyes” also says the sense organs are never mine. The Atharvan text says, “without breath, without mind, pure.”
units.editionTranslation: “Scripture says I never have the sense organs, as taught by ‘without eyes’ and the rest; the Atharvan text says, ‘without breath, without mind, pure.’”

units.label: Verse I.13.13
units.deva: शब्दादीनाम् अभावश् च श्रूयते मम काठके । अप्राणो ह्य् अमना यस्माद् अविकारी सदा ह्य् अहम्
units.iast: śabdādīnām abhāvaś ca śrūyate mama kāṭhake । aprāṇo hy amanā yasmād avikārī sadā hy aham
units.translation: “The Kaṭha text also declares that sound and the rest do not belong to me. Since I am without breath or mind, I am always changeless.”

units.label: Verse I.13.14
units.deva: विक्षेपो नास्ति तस्मान् मे न समाधिस् ततो मम । विक्षेपो वा समाधिर् वा मनसः स्याद् विकारिणः
units.iast: vikṣepo nāsti tasmān me na samādhis tato mama । vikṣepo vā samādhir vā manasaḥ syād vikāriṇaḥ
units.translation: “Therefore distraction does not exist for me, nor does concentration. Distraction and concentration are states of a changing mind.”

units.label: Verse I.13.15
units.deva: अमनस्कस्य शुद्धस्य कथं तत् स्याद् द्वयं मम । अमनस्त्वाविकारित्वे विदेहव्यापिनो मम
units.iast: amanaskasya śuddhasya kathaṃ tat syād dvayaṃ mama । amanastvāvikāritve videhavyāpino mama
units.translation: “How could either state belong to me, who am mindless, pure and changeless, bodiless and all-pervading?”

units.label: Verse I.13.16
units.deva: इत्य् एतद् यावद् अज्ञानं तावत् कार्यं ममाभवत् । नित्यमुक्तस्य शुद्धस्य बुद्धस्य च सदा मम
units.iast: ity etad yāvad ajñānaṃ tāvat kāryaṃ mamābhavat । nityamuktasya śuddhasya buddhasya ca sadā mama
units.translation: “So long as ignorance remained, all this appeared to be my concern. But I am always free, pure and awakened.”

units.label: Verse I.13.17
units.deva: समाधिर् वासमाधिर् वा कार्यं वान्यत् कुतो भवेत् । मां हि ध्यात्वा च बुद्ध्वा च मन्यन्ते कृतकृत्यताम्
units.iast: samādhir vāsamādhir vā kāryaṃ vānyat kuto bhavet । maṃ hi dhyātvā ca buddhvā ca manyante kṛtakṛtyatām
units.translation: “How could concentration, lack of concentration or any other task belong to me? People think they have accomplished their purpose by meditating on me and knowing me.”

units.label: Verse I.13.18
units.deva: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि सर्वो ऽस्मि शुद्धो बुद्धो ऽसितः सदा । अजः सर्वग एवाहम् अजरश् चामृतो ऽक्षयः
units.iast: ahaṃ brahmāsmi sarvo 'smi śuddho buddho 'sitaḥ sadā । ajaḥ sarvaga evāham ajaraś cāmṛto 'kṣayaḥ
units.translation: “I am Brahman; I am all—pure, awakened, ever unstained. I am unborn, all-pervading, ageless, immortal and imperishable.”

units.label: Verse I.13.19
units.deva: मदन्यः सर्वभूतेषु बोद्धा कश्चिन् न विद्यते । कर्माध्यक्षश् च साक्षी च चेता नित्यो ऽगुणो ऽद्वयः
units.iast: madanyaḥ sarvabhūteṣu boddhā kaścin na vidyate । karmādhyakṣaś ca sākṣī ca cetā nityo 'guṇo 'dvayaḥ
units.translation: “There is no knower in all beings other than me. I am the overseer of action, the witness, conscious, eternal, without qualities and nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.13.20
units.deva: न सच् चाहं न चासच् च नोभयं केवलः शिवः । न मे संध्या न रात्रिर् वा नाहर् वा सर्वदा दृशेः
units.iast: na sac cāhaṃ na cāsac ca nobhayaṃ kevalaḥ śivaḥ । na me saṃdhyā na rātrir vā nāhar vā sarvadā dṛśeḥ
units.translation: “I am neither existent nor nonexistent, nor both; I am alone, auspicious. For my vision there is no twilight or night, no day, ever.”

units.label: Verse I.13.21
units.deva: सर्वमूर्तिवियुक्तं यद् यथा खं सूक्ष्मम् अद्वयम् । तेनाप्य् अस्मि विनाभूतं ब्रह्मैवाहं तथाद्वयम्
units.iast: sarvamūrtiviyuktaṃ yad yathā khaṃ sūkṣmam advayam । tenāpy asmi vinābhūtaṃ brahmaivāhaṃ tathādvayam
units.translation: “As space is subtle, nondual and free of every form, so too I am Brahman, untouched by anything, nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.13.22
units.deva: ममात्मास्य त आत्मेति भेदो व्योम्नो यथा भवेत् । एकस्य सुषिभेदेन तथा मम विकल्पितः
units.iast: mamātmāsya ta ātmeti bhedo vyomno yathā bhavet । ekasya suṣibhedena tathā mama vikalpitaḥ
units.translation: “The distinctions ‘my Self’ and ‘your Self’ are imagined in me, as divisions of space are imagined through the openings in a single space.”

units.label: Verse I.13.23
units.deva: भेदो ऽभेदस् तथा चैको नाना चेति विकल्पितम् । ज्ञेयं ज्ञाता गतिर् गन्ता मय्य् एकस्मिन् कुतो भवेत्
units.iast: bhedo 'bhedas tathā caiko nānā ceti vikalpitam । jñeyaṃ jñātā gatir gantā mayy ekasmin kuto bhavet
units.translation: “Difference and nondifference, oneness and multiplicity are all imagined. How could the known, the knower, the path and the traveler exist in me alone?”

units.label: Verse I.13.24
units.deva: न मे हेयं न चादेयम् अविकारी यतो ह्य् अहम् । सदा मुक्तस् तथा शुद्धः सदा बुद्धो ऽगुणो ऽद्वयः
units.iast: na me heyaṃ na cādeyam avikārī yato hy aham । sadā muktas tathā śuddhaḥ sadā buddho 'guṇo 'dvayaḥ
units.translation: “Nothing is to be given up or taken up by me, for I am changeless, ever-free, pure, awakened, without qualities and nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.13.25
units.deva: इत्य् एवं सर्वदात्मानं विद्यात् सर्वं समाहितः । विदित्वा मां स्वदेहस्थम् ऋषिर् मुक्तो ध्रुवो भवेत्
units.iast: ity evaṃ sarvadātmānaṃ vidyāt sarvaṃ samāhitaḥ । viditvā māṃ svadehastham ṛṣir mukto dhruvo bhavet
units.translation: “With a collected mind, know the Self in this way at all times. Knowing me, present in one’s own body, the sage surely becomes free.”

units.label: Verse I.13.26
units.deva: कृतकृत्यश् च सिद्धश् च योगी ब्राह्मण एव च । यदैवं वेद तत्त्वार्थम् अन्यथा ह्य् आत्महा भवेत्
units.iast: kṛtakṛtyaś ca siddhaś ca yogī brāhmaṇa eva ca । yadaivaṃ veda tattvārtham anyathā hy ātmahā bhavet
units.translation: “When one knows the truth in this way, one is accomplished, fulfilled, a yogin and a true knower of Brahman; otherwise one destroys one’s own Self.”

units.label: Verse I.13.27
units.deva: वेदार्थो निश्चितो ह्य् एष समासेन मयोदितः । संन्यासिभ्यः प्रवक्तव्यः शान्तेभ्यः शिष्टबुद्धिना
units.iast: vedārtho niścito hy eṣa samāsena mayoditaḥ । saṃnyāsibhyaḥ pravaktavyaḥ śāntebhyaḥ śiṣṭabuddhinā
units.translation: “In brief, I have stated this certain meaning of the Veda. It should be taught to renunciants who are peaceful and wise.”

units.label: Verse I.14.1
units.deva: स्वप्नस्मृत्योर् घटादेर् हि रूपाभासः प्रदृश्यते । पुरा नूनं तदाकरा धीर् दृष्टेत्य् अनुमीयते
units.iast: svapnasmṛtyor ghaṭāder hi rūpābhāsaḥ pradṛśyate । purā nūnaṃ tadākarā dhīr dṛṣṭety anumīyate
units.translation: “In a dream and in memory, the form of a pot and the like is seen; one infers that earlier there must have been a cognition shaped like it.”

units.label: Verse I.14.2
units.deva: भिक्षाम् अटन् यथा स्वप्ने दृष्टो देहो न स स्वयम् । जाग्रद्दृश्यात् तथा देहाद् द्रष्टृत्वाद् अन्य एव सः
units.iast: bhikṣām aṭan yathā svapne dṛṣṭo deho na sa svayam । jāgraddṛśyāt tathā dehād draṣṭṛtvād anya eva saḥ
units.translation: “The body seen in a dream while begging is not the dreamer himself; likewise, because the waking body is seen, the Seer is other than it.”

units.label: Verse I.14.3
units.deva: मूषासिक्तं यथा ताम्रं तन्निभं जायते तथा । रूपादीन् व्याप्नुवच् चित्तं तन्निभं दृश्यते ध्रुवम्
units.iast: mūṣāsiktaṃ yathā tāmraṃ tannibhaṃ jāyate tathā । rūpādīn vyāpnuvac cittaṃ tannibhaṃ dṛśyate dhruvam
units.translation: “As copper poured into a mold takes its form, so the mind, pervading visible forms and the rest, surely appears to take their shape.”

units.label: Verse I.14.4
units.deva: व्यञ्जको वा यथालोको व्यङ्ग्यस्याकारताम् इयात् । सर्वार्थव्यञ्जकत्वाद् धीर् अर्थाकरा प्रदृश्यते
units.iast: vyañjako vā yathāloko vyaṅgyasyākāratām iyāt । sarvārthavyañjakatvād dhīr arthākarā pradṛśyate
units.translation: “As light takes the form of what it reveals, the intellect appears shaped like its objects because it reveals them all.”

units.label: Verse I.14.5
units.deva: धिर् एवार्थस्वरूपा हि पुंसा दृष्टा पुरापि च । न चेत् स्वप्ने कथं पश्येत् स्मरतो वाकृतिः कुतः
units.iast: dhir evārthasvarūpā hi puṃsā dṛṣṭā purāpi ca । na cet svapne kathaṃ paśyet smarato vākṛtiḥ kutaḥ
units.translation: “The intellect has already been seen to take the form of its object. If not, how would one see in a dream, and how could memory have a form?”

units.label: Verse I.14.6
units.deva: व्यञ्जकत्वं तद् एवास्य रूपाद्याकारदृश्यता । द्रष्टृत्वं च दृशेस् तद्वद् व्याप्तिः स्याद् धिय उद्भवे
units.iast: vyañjakatvaṃ tad evāsya rūpādyākāradṛśyatā । draṣṭṛtvaṃ ca dṛśes tadvad vyāptiḥ syād dhiya udbhave
units.translation: “Its revealing power is just this appearance as the forms of color and the rest. The Seer’s vision likewise pervades the intellect as it arises.”

units.label: Verse I.14.7
units.deva: चिन्मात्रज्योतिषा सर्वः सर्वदेहेषु बुद्धयः । मया यस्मात् प्रकाश्यन्ते सर्वस्यात्मा ततो ह्य् अहम्
units.iast: cinmātrajyotiṣā sarvaḥ sarvadeheṣu buddhayaḥ । mayā yasmāt prakāśyante sarvasyātmā tato hy aham
units.translation: “Because I illumine the intellects in every body by the light of pure consciousness, I am therefore the Self of all.”

units.label: Verse I.14.8
units.deva: करणं कर्म कर्ता च क्रिया स्वप्ने फलं च धीः । जाग्रत्य् एवं यतो दृष्टा द्रष्टा तस्मात् ततो ऽन्यथा
units.iast: karaṇaṃ karma kartā ca kriyā svapne phalaṃ ca dhīḥ । jāgraty evaṃ yato dṛṣṭā draṣṭā tasmāt tato 'nyathā
units.translation: “In a dream, the instrument, action, agent and result are all seen as intellect; the waking world is seen in the same way. The Seer is different from them.”

units.label: Verse I.14.9
units.deva: बुद्ध्यादीनाम् अनात्मत्वं हेयोपादेयरूपतः । हानोपादानकर्तात्मा न त्याज्यो न च गृह्यते
units.iast: buddhyādīnām anātmatvaṃ heyopādeyarūpataḥ । hānopādānakartātmā na tyājyo na ca gṛhyate
units.translation: “The intellect and the rest are not-Self, to be relinquished or taken up; the Self is the one who relinquishes and takes up, but is itself neither abandoned nor grasped.”

units.label: Verse I.14.10
units.deva: सबाह्याभ्यन्तरे शुद्धे प्रज्ञानैकरसे घने । बाह्यम् आभ्यन्तरं चान्यत् कथं हेयं प्रकल्प्यते
units.iast: sabāhyābhyantare śuddhe prajñānaikarase ghane । bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ cānyat kathaṃ heyaṃ prakalpyate
units.translation: “Within and without, all is a single mass of pure awareness; how could anything outside or inside be imagined as separate and rejected?”

units.label: Verse I.14.11
units.deva: य आत्मा नेति नेतीति परापोहेन शेषितः । स चेद् ब्रह्मविदात्मेष्टो यतेतातः परं कथम्
units.iast: ya ātmā neti netīti parāpohena śeṣitaḥ । sa ced brahmavidātmeṣṭo yatetātaḥ paraṃ katham
units.translation: “If the Self, retained after every other thing is excluded, is held to be Brahman by the knower, what further effort could be required?”

units.label: Verse I.14.12
units.deva: अशनायाद्यतिक्रान्तं ब्रह्मैवास्मि निरन्तरम् । कार्यवान् स्यां कथं चाहं विमृशेद् एवम् अञ्जसा
units.iast: aśanāyādyatikrāntaṃ brahmaivāsmi nirantaram । kāryavān syāṃ kathaṃ cāhaṃ vimṛśed evam añjasā
units.translation: “I am Brahman, without interruption, beyond hunger and the rest. How could I, in truth, think that I have any task to do?”

units.label: Verse I.14.13
units.deva: पारगस् तु यथा नद्यास् तत्स्थः परं यियासति । आत्मज्ञश् चेत् तथा कार्यं कर्तुम् अन्यद् इहेच्छति
units.iast: pāragas tu yathā nadyās tatsthaḥ paraṃ yiyāsati । ātmajñaś cet tathā kāryaṃ kartum anyad ihecchati
units.translation: “Just as one who has crossed to the far bank of a river would not wish to do some other work there, so too a knower of the Self has no further task to seek here.”

units.label: Verse I.14.14
units.deva: आत्मज्ञस्यापि यस्य स्याद् धानोपादानता यदि । न मोक्षार्हः स विज्ञेयो वान्तो ऽसौ ब्रह्मणा ध्रुवम्
units.iast: ātmajñasyāpi yasya syād dhānopādānatā yadi । na mokṣārhaḥ sa vijñeyo vānto 'sau brahmaṇā dhruvam
units.translation: “If a knower of the Self still accepts and rejects things, know that person is not fit for liberation; that person has surely been overcome by the world of Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.14.15
units.deva: सादित्यं हि जगत् प्राणस् तस्मान् नाहर् निशैव वा । प्राणज्ञस्यापि न स्यातां कुतो ब्रह्मविदो ऽद्वये
units.iast: sādityaṃ hi jagat prāṇas tasmān nāhar niśaiva vā । prāṇajñasyāpi na syātāṃ kuto brahmavido 'dvaye
units.translation: “The world, with its sun and the rest, is life-breath itself; for the knower of breath there is neither day nor night. How much less could these exist for the knower of nondual Brahman?”

units.label: Verse I.14.16
units.deva: न स्मरत्य् आत्मनो ह्य् आत्मा विस्मरेद् वाप्य् अलुप्तचित् । मनो ऽपि स्मरतीत्य् एतज् ज्ञानम् अज्ञानहेतुजम्
units.iast: na smaraty ātmano hy ātmā vismared vāpy aluptacit । mano 'pi smaratīty etaj jñānam ajñānahetujam
units.translation: “The Self does not remember itself, nor does it forget itself, for awareness is never lost. The mind remembers; this knowledge and ignorance arise from a cause.”

units.label: Verse I.14.17
units.deva: ज्ञातुर् ज्ञेयः परो ह्य् आत्मा सो ऽविद्याकल्पितः स्मृतः । अपोढे विद्यया तस्मिन् रज्ज्वां सर्प इवाद्वयः
units.iast: jñātur jñeyaḥ paro hy ātmā so 'vidyākalpitaḥ smṛtaḥ । apoḍhe vidyayā tasmin rajjvāṃ sarpa ivādvayaḥ
units.translation: “A second Self, beyond the knower, is imagined through ignorance. When it is removed by knowledge, the Self is nondual, like the rope mistaken for a snake.”

units.label: Verse I.14.18
units.deva: कर्तृकर्मफलाभावात् सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं ह्य् अजम् । ममाहं चेति यो भावस् तस्मिन् कस्य कुतो भवेत्
units.iast: kartṛkarmaphalābhāvāt sabāhyābhyantaraṃ hy ajam । mamāhaṃ ceti yo bhāvas tasmin kasya kuto bhavet
units.translation: “Since there is no agent, action or result, and the Self is unborn within and without, for whom and how could the thought ‘I’ or ‘mine’ arise?”

units.label: Verse I.14.19
units.deva: आत्मा ह्य् आत्मीय इत्य् एष भावो ऽविद्याप्रकल्पितः । आत्मैकत्वे ह्य् असौ नास्ति बीजभावे कुतः फलम्
units.iast: ātmā hy ātmīya ity eṣa bhāvo 'vidyāprakalpitaḥ । ātmaikatve hy asau nāsti bījabhāve kutaḥ phalam
units.translation: “The notion ‘the Self is mine’ is imagined through ignorance. When the Self is one, it does not exist; without a seed, how could there be a fruit?”

units.label: Verse I.14.20
units.deva: द्रष्टृ स्रोतृ तथा मन्तृ विज्ञातृ एव तद् अक्षरम् । द्रष्ट्राद्यन्यन् न तद् यस्मात् तस्माद् द्रष्टाहम् अक्षरम्
units.iast: draṣṭṛ srotṛ tathā mantṛ vijñātṛ eva tad akṣaram । draṣṭrādyanyan na tad yasmāt tasmād draṣṭāham akṣaram
units.translation: “The one who sees, hears, thinks and knows is the Imperishable. Since no one is other than the Seer and the rest, I am that Seer, the Imperishable.”

units.label: Verse I.14.21
units.deva: स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव द्रष्टृत्वादिक्रियायुतम् । सर्वम् अक्षरम् एवातः सर्वस्यात्माक्षरं त्व् अहम्
units.iast: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva draṣṭṛtvādikriyāyutam । sarvam akṣaram evātaḥ sarvasyātmākṣaraṃ tv aham
units.translation: “All beings, moving and unmoving, endowed with acts such as seeing, are the Imperishable; therefore I am the Imperishable Self of all.”

units.label: Verse I.14.22
units.deva: अकार्यशेषम् आत्मानम् अक्रियात्मक्रियाफलम् । निर्ममं निरहंकारं यः पश्यति स पश्यति
units.iast: akāryaśeṣam ātmānam akriyātmakriyāphalam । nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
units.translation: “One who sees the Self as free of every object and action, with no remainder of agency or result, and without ‘mine’ or ego, truly sees.”

units.label: Verse I.14.23
units.deva: ममाहंकारयत्नेच्छाः शून्या एव स्वभावतः । आत्मनीति यदि ज्ञातम् आध्वं स्वस्थाः किम् ईहितैः
units.iast: mamāhaṃkārayatnecchāḥ śūnyā eva svabhāvataḥ । ātmanīti yadi jñātam ādhvaṃ svasthāḥ kim īhitaiḥ
units.translation: “The thoughts ‘mine’ and ‘I,’ effort and desire, are empty by nature. If this is known to be in the Self, why strive? Be at peace.”

units.label: Verse I.14.24
units.deva: यो ऽहंकर्तारम् आत्मानं तथा वेत्तारम् एव यः । वेत्त्य् अनात्मज्ञ एवासौ यो ऽन्यथाज्ञः स आत्मवित्
units.iast: yo 'haṃkartāram ātmānaṃ tathā vettāram eva yaḥ । vetty anātmajña evāsau yo 'nyathājñaḥ sa ātmavit
units.translation: “Whoever knows the Self as the doer, and also as the knower, is not a knower of the Self; the one who knows it otherwise is the knower.”

units.label: Verse I.14.25
units.deva: यथान्यत्वे ऽपि तादात्म्यं देहादिष्व् आत्मनो मतम् । तथाकर्तुर् अविज्ञानात् फलकर्मात्मतात्मनः
units.iast: yathānyatve 'pi tādātmyaṃ dehādiṣv ātmano matam । tathākartur avijñānāt phalakarmātmatātmanaḥ
units.translation: “As the Self is thought to be identical with the body and the rest, though distinct from them, so through ignorance the Self is identified with agency, knowledge and the fruits of action.”

units.label: Verse I.14.26
units.deva: दृष्टिः श्रुतिर् मतिर् ज्ञातिः स्वप्ने दृष्टा जनैः सदा । तासाम् आत्मस्वरूपत्वाद् अतः प्रत्यक्षतात्मनः
units.iast: dṛṣṭiḥ śrutir matir jñātiḥ svapne dṛṣṭā janaiḥ sadā । tāsām ātmasvarūpatvād ataḥ pratyakṣatātmanaḥ
units.translation: “Seeing, hearing, thinking and knowing are experienced by people in dreams; since they belong to the Self, the Self is directly evident.”

units.label: Verse I.14.27
units.deva: परलोकभयं यस्य नास्ति मृत्युभयं तथा । तस्यात्मज्ञस्य शोच्यः स्युः सब्रह्मेन्द्रा अपीश्वराः
units.iast: paralokabhayaṃ yasya nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ tathā । tasyātmajñasya śocyaḥ syuḥ sabrahmendrā apīśvarāḥ
units.translation: “For the knower of the Self, who fears neither the next world nor death, even the gods, including Brahmā and Indra, are objects of pity.”

units.label: Verse I.14.28
units.deva: ईश्वरत्वेन किं तस्य ब्रह्मेन्द्रत्वेन वा पुनः । तृष्णा चेत् सर्वतश् छिन्ना सर्वदैन्योद्भवाशुभा
units.iast: īśvaratvena kiṃ tasya brahmendratvena vā punaḥ । tṛṣṇā cet sarvataś chinnā sarvadainyodbhavāśubhā
units.translation: “What need has that person of lordship or the rank of Indra, when craving is cut off everywhere, along with the source of all misery?”

units.label: Verse I.14.29
units.deva: अहम् इत्य् आत्मधीर् या च ममेत्य् आत्मीयधीर् अपि । अर्थशून्ये यदा यस्य स आत्मज्ञो भवेत् तदा
units.iast: aham ity ātmadhīr yā ca mamety ātmīyadhīr api । arthaśūnye yadā yasya sa ātmajño bhavet tadā
units.translation: “When a person’s notions ‘I’ and ‘mine’ have no object at all, that person is then a knower of the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.14.30
units.deva: बुद्ध्यादौ सत्य् उपाधौ च तथासत्य् अविशेषता । यस्य चेद् आत्मनो ज्ञाता तस्य कार्यं कथं भवेत्
units.iast: buddhyādau saty upādhau ca tathāsaty aviśeṣatā । yasya ced ātmano jñātā tasya kāryaṃ kathaṃ bhavet
units.translation: “When the intellect and its limiting adjunct are present, or when they are absent, the knower of the Self remains without distinction. How could any task belong to that one?”

units.label: Verse I.14.31
units.deva: प्रसन्ने विमले व्योम्नि प्रज्ञानैकरसे ऽद्वये । उत्पन्नात्मधियो ब्रूत किम् अन्यत् कार्यम् इष्यते
units.iast: prasanne vimale vyomni prajñānaikarase 'dvaye । utpannātmadhiyo brūta kim anyat kāryam iṣyate
units.translation: “Tell me what further task is desired when knowledge of the Self has arisen in the clear, stainless, nondual sky of pure consciousness.”

units.label: Verse I.14.32
units.deva: आत्मानं सर्वभूतस्थम् अमित्रं चात्मनो ऽपि यः । पश्यन्न् इच्छत्य् असौ नूनं शीतीकर्तुं विभावसुम्
units.iast: ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtastham amitraṃ cātmano 'pi yaḥ । paśyann icchaty asau nūnaṃ śītīkartuṃ vibhāvasum
units.translation: “One who sees the Self dwelling in all beings, and even as an enemy to oneself, surely wishes to cool the blazing fire.”

units.label: Verse I.14.33
units.deva: प्रज्ञाप्राणानुकार्य् आत्मा छायेवाक्षादिगोचरः । ध्यायतीवेति चोक्तो हि शुद्धो मुक्तः स्वतो हि सः
units.iast: prajñāprāṇānukāry ātmā chāyevākṣādigocaraḥ । dhyāyatīveti cokto hi śuddho muktaḥ svato hi saḥ
units.translation: “The Self appears to follow the intellect and life-breath, like a shadow appearing within the range of the eye; scripture says it ‘seems to think.’ Yet by nature it is pure and free.”

units.label: Verse I.14.34
units.deva: अप्राणस्यामनस्कस्य तथासंसर्गिणो दृशेः । व्योमवद् व्यापिनो ह्य् अस्य कथं कार्यं भवेन् मम
units.iast: aprāṇasyāmanaskasya tathāsaṃsargiṇo dṛśeḥ । vyomavad vyāpino hy asya kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhaven mama
units.translation: “For me, the Seer without breath or mind, unattached and all-pervading like space, how could there be any task?”

units.label: Verse I.14.35
units.deva: असमाधिं न पश्यामि निर्विकारस्य सर्वदा । ब्रह्मणो मे विशुद्धस्य शोध्यं चान्यद् विपाप्मनः
units.iast: asamādhiṃ na paśyāmi nirvikārasya sarvadā । brahmaṇo me viśuddhasya śodhyaṃ cānyad vipāpmanaḥ
units.translation: “For me, the changeless, ever-pure Brahman, I see no lack of concentration or anything else that needs purification, since I am free from evil.”

units.label: Verse I.14.36
units.deva: गन्तव्यं च तथैवाहं सर्वगस्याचलस्य च । नोर्ध्वं नाधस् तिरो वापि निष्कलस्यागुणत्वतः
units.iast: gantavyaṃ ca tathaivāhaṃ sarvagasyācalasya ca । nordhvaṃ nādhas tiro vāpi niṣkalasyāguṇatvataḥ
units.translation: “I am indeed what is to be reached, all-pervading and unmoving; I am neither above, below nor across, because I am without parts or qualities.”

units.label: Verse I.14.37
units.deva: चिन्मात्रज्योतिषो नित्यं तमस् तस्मिन् न विद्यते । कथं कार्यं ममैवाद्य नित्यमुक्तस्य शिष्यते
units.iast: cinmātrajyotiṣo nityaṃ tamas tasmin na vidyate । kathaṃ kāryaṃ mamaivādya nityamuktasya śiṣyate
units.translation: “There is no darkness for me, whose light is pure consciousness alone. What task could remain for me, eternally free even now?”

units.label: Verse I.14.38
units.deva: अमनस्कस्य का चिन्ता क्रिया वानिन्द्रियस्य का । अप्राणो ह्य् अमनाः शुभ्र इति सत्यं श्रुतेर् वचः
units.iast: amanaskasya kā cintā kriyā vānindriyasya kā । aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhra iti satyaṃ śruter vacaḥ
units.translation: “What thought can there be for one without a mind? What action for one without senses? Scripture truly says: ‘without breath, without mind, pure.’”

units.label: Verse I.14.39
units.deva: अकालत्वाद् अदेशत्वाद् अदिक्त्वाद् अनिमित्ततः । आत्मनो नैव कालादेर् अपेक्षा ध्यायतः सदा
units.iast: akālatvād adeśatvād adiktvād animittataḥ । ātmano naiva kālāder apekṣā dhyāyataḥ sadā
units.translation: “Because the Self is beyond time, place, direction and cause, it has no need of time or the rest, even for one who meditates on it always.”

units.label: Verse I.14.40
units.deva: यस्मिन् देवाश् च वेदाश् च पवित्रं कृत्स्नम् एकताम् । व्रजेत् तन् मानसं तीर्थं यस्मिन् स्नात्वामृतो भवेत्
units.iast: yasmin devāś ca vedāś ca pavitraṃ kṛtsnam ekatām । vrajet tan mānasaṃ tīrthaṃ yasmin snātvāmṛto bhavet
units.translation: “That in which the gods, the Vedas and all that is pure attain unity is the sacred ford of the mind; bathing in it, one becomes immortal.”

units.label: Verse I.14.41
units.deva: न चास्ति शब्दादिर् अनन्यवेदनः परस्परेणापि न चैव दृश्यते । परेण दृश्यास् तु यथा रसादयस् तथैव दृश्यत्वत एव दैहिकाः
units.iast: na cāsti śabdādir ananyavedanaḥ paraspareṇāpi na caiva dṛśyate । pareṇa dṛśyās tu yathā rasādayas tathaiva dṛśyatvata eva daihikāḥ
units.translation: “Sound and the rest do not know one another, nor do they appear to one another; they are seen by another, as taste and the rest are. The bodily senses and their objects are likewise seen.”

units.label: Verse I.14.42
units.deva: अहं ममेत्य् एषणयत्नविक्रियाः सुखादयस् तद्वद् इह प्रदृश्यतः । दृश्यत्वयोगाच् च परस्परेण ते न दृश्यतां यान्ति ततः परो भवेत्
units.iast: ahaṃ mamety eṣaṇayatnavikriyāḥ sukhādayas tadvad iha pradṛśyataḥ । dṛśyatvayogāc ca paraspareṇa te na dṛśyatāṃ yānti tataḥ paro bhavet
units.translation: “The thoughts ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ desire, effort, change and happiness are all seen here; because they are seen, they do not see one another. The Seer is beyond them.”

units.label: Verse I.14.43
units.deva: अहंक्रियाद्या हि समस्तविक्रिया सकर्तृका कर्मफलेन संहिता । चितिस्वरूपेण समन्ततो ऽर्कवत् प्रकाश्यमानासिततात्मनो ह्य् अतः
units.iast: ahaṃkriyādyā hi samastavikriyā sakartṛkā karmaphalena saṃhitā । citisvarūpeṇa samantato 'rkavat prakāśyamānāsitatātmano hy ataḥ
units.translation: “All changes, beginning with ego, are joined to an agent, action and result, and are illuminated on every side by the light of consciousness; therefore the Self is pure and beyond them.”

units.label: Verse I.14.44
units.deva: दृशिस्वरूपेण हि सर्वदेहिनां वियद् यथा व्याप्य मनांस्य् अवस्थितः । अतो न तस्माद् अपरो ऽस्ति वेदिता परो ऽपि तस्माद् अत एक ईश्वरः
units.iast: dṛśisvarūpeṇa hi sarvadehināṃ viyad yathā vyāpya manāṃsy avasthitaḥ । ato na tasmād aparo 'sti veditā paro 'pi tasmād ata eka īśvaraḥ
units.translation: “As space pervades the minds of all embodied beings, the Seer abides in all as their seeing nature. There is no knower apart from it; the supreme Lord is therefore one.”

units.label: Verse I.14.45
units.deva: शरीरबुद्ध्योर् यदि चान्यदृश्यता निरात्मवादाः सुनिराकृटा मया । परश् च सिद्धो ह्य् अविशुद्धिकर्मतः सुनिर्मलः सर्वगतो ऽसितो ऽद्वयः
units.iast: śarīrabuddhyor yadi cānyadṛśyatā nirātmavādāḥ sunirākṛṭā mayā । paraś ca siddho hy aviśuddhikarmataḥ sunirmalaḥ sarvagato 'sito 'dvayaḥ
units.translation: “If the body and intellect are seen as other, I have fully refuted the doctrines that deny the Self. The supreme Self is established as pure, all-pervading, unstained and nondual.”

units.label: Verse I.14.46
units.deva: घटादिरूपं यदि ते न गृह्यते मनः प्रवृत्तं बहुधा स्ववृत्तिभिः । अशुद्ध्यचिद्रूपविकारदोषता मतेर् यथा वारयितुं न पार्यते
units.iast: ghaṭādirūpaṃ yadi te na gṛhyate manaḥ pravṛttaṃ bahudhā svavṛttibhiḥ । aśuddhyacidrūpavikāradoṣatā mater yathā vārayituṃ na pāryate
units.translation: “Even if you do not grasp the forms of pots and the rest, the mind is active in its many thoughts; its defects of impurity, insentience and change cannot thereby be prevented.”

units.label: Verse I.14.47
units.deva: यथा विशुद्धं गगनं निरन्तरं न सज्जते नापि च लिप्यते तथा । समस्तभूतेषु सदैव तेष्व् अयं समः सदात्मा ह्य् अजरो ऽमरो ऽभयः
units.iast: yathā viśuddhaṃ gaganaṃ nirantaraṃ na sajjate nāpi ca lipyate tathā । samastabhūteṣu sadaiva teṣv ayaṃ samaḥ sadātmā hy ajaro 'maro 'bhayaḥ
units.translation: “As the stainless, unbroken sky neither clings nor is stained, so this eternal Self is always equal in all beings, ageless, deathless and fearless.”

units.label: Verse I.14.48
units.deva: अमूर्तमूर्तानि च कर्मवासना दृशिस्वरूपस्य बहिः प्रकल्पिताः । अविद्यया ह्य् आत्मनि मूढदृष्टिभिर् अपोह्य नेतीत्य् अवशेषितो दृशिः
units.iast: amūrtamūrtāni ca karmavāsanā dṛśisvarūpasya bahiḥ prakalpitāḥ । avidyayā hy ātmani mūḍhadṛṣṭibhir apohya netīty avaśeṣito dṛśiḥ
units.translation: “Immaterial and material forms, together with the latent impressions of action, are imagined outside the nature of the Seer. Through ignorance the deluded project them on the Self; when they are set aside as ‘not this,’ the Seer alone remains.”

units.label: Verse I.14.49
units.deva: प्रबोधरूपं मनसो ऽर्थयोगजं स्मृतौ च सुप्तस्य च दृश्यते ऽर्थवत् । तथैव देहप्रतिमानतः पृथग् दृशेः शरीरं च मनश् च दृश्यतः
units.iast: prabodharūpaṃ manaso 'rthayogajaṃ smṛtau ca suptasya ca dṛśyate 'rthavat । tathaiva dehapratimānataḥ pṛthag dṛśeḥ śarīraṃ ca manaś ca dṛśyataḥ
units.translation: “The mind’s waking awareness, arising from contact with an object, is seen; the sleeping person’s memory is seen too, as are the body and mind, distinct from the Seer.”

units.label: Verse I.14.50
units.deva: स्वभावशुद्धे गगने घनादिके मले ऽपयाते सति चाविशेषता । यथा च तद्वच् छ्रुतिवारितद्वये सदाविशेषो गगनोपमे दृशौ
units.iast: svabhāvaśuddhe gagane ghanādike male 'payāte sati cāviśeṣatā । yathā ca tadvac chrutivāritadvaye sadāviśeṣo gaganopame dṛśau
units.translation: “When clouds and other stains depart, the naturally pure sky has no division. Likewise, once scripture has removed duality, the Seer remains ever undivided, like space.”

units.label: Verse I.15.1
units.deva: नान्यद् अन्यद् भवेद् यस्मान् नान्यत् किंचिद् विचिन्तयेत् । अन्यस्यान्यत्वभावे हि नाशस् तस्य ध्रुवो भवेत्
units.iast: nānyad anyad bhaved yasmān nānyat kiṃcid vicintayet । anyasyānyatvabhāve hi nāśas tasya dhruvo bhavet
units.translation: “Nothing becomes something other than itself; one should therefore not imagine anything as other. If one thing truly became another, it would surely perish.”

units.label: Verse I.15.2
units.deva: स्मरतो दृश्यते दृष्टं पटे चित्रम् इवार्पितम् । यत्र येन च तौ ज्ञेयौ सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञसंज्ञकौ
units.iast: smarato dṛśyate dṛṣṭaṃ paṭe citram ivārpitam । yatra yena ca tau jñeyau sattvakṣetrajñasaṃjñakau
units.translation: “What is remembered appears as an image painted on a cloth. In that, both the existent and the knower of the field are to be understood—where and by what are they known?”

units.label: Verse I.15.3
units.deva: फलान्तं चानुभूतं यद् युक्तं कर्त्रादिकारकैः । स्मर्यमाणं हि कर्मस्थं पूर्वं कर्मैव तत् ततः
units.iast: phalāntaṃ cānubhūtaṃ yad yuktaṃ kartrādikārakaiḥ । smaryamāṇaṃ hi karmasthaṃ pūrvaṃ karmaiva tat tataḥ
units.translation: “What has been experienced through agent, action and other factors, up to its result, is remembered as belonging to action; that, then, is the earlier action itself.”

units.label: Verse I.15.4
units.deva: द्रष्टुश् चान्यद् भवेद् दृश्यं दृश्यत्वाद् घटवत् सदा । दृश्याद् द्रष्टासजातीयो न धीवत् साक्षितान्यथा
units.iast: draṣṭuś cānyad bhaved dṛśyaṃ dṛśyatvād ghaṭavat sadā । dṛśyād draṣṭāsajātīyo na dhīvat sākṣitānyathā
units.translation: “The seen is always different from the Seer, like a pot. The Seer is of a different kind from what is seen, unlike the intellect; otherwise there could be no witnessing.”

units.label: Verse I.15.5
units.deva: स्वात्मबुद्धिम् अपेक्ष्यासौ विधीनां स्यात् प्रयोजकः । जात्यादिः शववत् तेन तद्वन् नानात्मतान्यथा
units.iast: svātmabuddhim apekṣyāsau vidhīnāṃ syāt prayojakaḥ । jātyādiḥ śavavat tena tadvan nānātmatānyathā
units.translation: “If the Seer depended on self-knowledge as an object, ritual injunctions could apply to it; but, like a corpse, it has no such qualities. Therefore it cannot be not-Self.”

units.label: Verse I.15.6
units.deva: न प्रियाप्रिय इत्य् उक्तेर् नादेहत्वं क्रियाफलम् । देहयोगः क्रियाहेतुस् तस्माद् विद्वान् क्रियास् त्यजेत्
units.iast: na priyāpriya ity ukter nādehatvaṃ kriyāphalam । dehayogaḥ kriyāhetus tasmād vidvān kriyās tyajet
units.translation: “The statement that pleasure and pain do not belong to the Self does not mean that bodilessness is a result of action. Embodiment is the cause of action; therefore the wise should relinquish actions.”

units.label: Verse I.15.7
units.deva: कर्मस्व् आत्मा स्वतन्त्रश् चेन् निवृत्तौ च तथेष्यताम् । अदेहत्वे फले ऽकार्ये ज्ञाते कुर्यात् कथं क्रियाः
units.iast: karmasv ātmā svatantraś cen nivṛttau ca tatheṣyatām । adehatve phale 'kārye jñāte kuryāt kathaṃ kriyāḥ
units.translation: “If the Self is independent with respect to action, it should be so with respect to cessation as well. When the result is known to be bodilessness, how could one perform action?”

units.label: Verse I.15.8
units.deva: जात्यादिन् संपरित्यज्य निमित्तं कर्मणां बुधः । कर्महेतुविरुद्धं यत् स्वरूपं शास्त्रतः स्मरेत्
units.iast: jātyādin saṃparityajya nimittaṃ karmaṇāṃ budhaḥ । karmahetuviruddhaṃ yat svarūpaṃ śāstrataḥ smaret
units.translation: “Having set aside birth, caste and the rest, the wise should remember through scripture the Self’s nature, which is contrary to the cause of action.”

units.label: Verse I.15.9
units.deva: आत्मैकः सर्वभूतेषु तानि तस्मिंश् च खे यथा । पर्यगाद् व्योमवत् सर्वं शुक्रं दीप्तिमद् इष्यते
units.iast: ātmaikaḥ sarvabhūteṣu tāni tasmiṃś ca khe yathā । paryagād vyomavat sarvaṃ śukraṃ dīptimad iṣyate
units.translation: “The Self is one in all beings and pervades them, as space pervades all. It is pure and radiant; I am that.”

units.label: Verse I.15.10
units.deva: व्रणस्नाय्वोर् अभावेन स्थूलं देहं निवारयेत् । शुद्धापापतया लेपं लिङ्गं चाकायम् इत्य् उत
units.iast: vraṇasnāyvor abhāvena sthūlaṃ dehaṃ nivārayet । śuddhāpāpatayā lepaṃ liṅgaṃ cākāyam ity uta
units.translation: “One should set aside the gross body, which has wounds, tendons and the rest; its stain does not touch the pure and sinless Self, which is subtle and bodiless.”

units.label: Verse I.15.11
units.deva: वासुदेवो यथाश्वत्थे स्वदेहे चाब्रवित् समम् । तद्वद् वेत्ति य आत्मानं समं स ब्रह्मवित्तमः
units.iast: vāsudevo yathāśvatthe svadehe cābravit samam । tadvad vetti ya ātmānaṃ samaṃ sa brahmavittamaḥ
units.translation: “As Vāsudeva declared himself equal in the aśvattha tree and in his own body, so one who knows the Self equally in all is the highest knower of Brahman.”

units.label: Verse I.15.12
units.deva: यथा ह्य् अन्यशरीरेषु ममाहन्ता न चेष्यते । अस्मिंश् चापि तथा देहे धीसाक्षित्वाविशेषतः
units.iast: yathā hy anyaśarīreṣu mamāhantā na ceṣyate । asmiṃś cāpi tathā dehe dhīsākṣitvāviśeṣataḥ
units.translation: “Just as I do not identify with other bodies, neither should I identify with this body, since I equally witness the intellect in all.”

units.label: Verse I.15.13
units.deva: रूपसंस्कारतुल्याधि रागद्वेषौ भयं च यत् । गृह्यते धीश्रयं तस्माज् ज्ञाता शुद्धो ऽभयः सदा
units.iast: rūpasaṃskāratulyādhi rāgadveṣau bhayaṃ ca yat । gṛhyate dhīśrayaṃ tasmāj jñātā śuddho 'bhayaḥ sadā
units.translation: “Color and impressions, attachment, aversion and fear are grasped as belonging to the intellect; therefore the knower is always pure and fearless.”

units.label: Verse I.15.14
units.deva: यन्मनास् तन्मयो ऽन्यत्वे नात्मत्वाप्तौ क्रियात्मनि । आत्मत्वे चानपेक्षत्वात् सापेक्षं हि न तत् स्वयम्
units.iast: yanmanās tanmayo 'nyatve nātmatvāptau kriyātmani । ātmatve cānapekṣatvāt sāpekṣaṃ hi na tat svayam
units.translation: “The mind becomes what it attends to, but that does not make it the Self; reaching the Self is not an action. Since the Self is always itself, it depends on nothing.”

units.label: Verse I.15.15
units.deva: खम् इवैकरसा ज्ञप्तिर् अविभक्ताजरामला । चक्षुराद्युपधानात् सा विपरीता विभाव्यते
units.iast: kham ivaikarasā jñaptir avibhaktājarāmalā । cakṣurādyupadhānāt sā viparītā vibhāvyate
units.translation: “Awareness is undivided and of one nature, like space, ageless and unstained; the sense organs as limiting adjuncts make it appear otherwise.”

units.label: Verse I.15.16
units.deva: दृश्यत्वाद् अहम् इत्य् एष नात्मधर्मो घटादिवत् । तथान्ये प्रत्यया ज्ञेया दोषाश् चात्मामलो ह्य् अतः
units.iast: dṛśyatvād aham ity eṣa nātmadharmo ghaṭādivat । tathānye pratyayā jñeyā doṣāś cātmāmalo hy ataḥ
units.translation: “Because it is seen, the thought ‘I’ is not a property of the Self, like a pot; the other thoughts are likewise known, and their defects do not stain the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.15.17
units.deva: सर्वप्रत्ययसाक्षित्वाद् अविकारी च सर्वगः । विक्रियेत यदि द्रष्टा बुद्ध्यादीवाल्पविद् भवेत्
units.iast: sarvapratyayasākṣitvād avikārī ca sarvagaḥ । vikriyeta yadi draṣṭā buddhyādīvālpavid bhavet
units.translation: “Because the Self witnesses every thought, it is changeless and all-pervading. If the Seer changed, it would become a limited knower like the intellect.”

units.label: Verse I.15.18
units.deva: न दृष्टिर् लुप्यते द्रष्टुश् चक्षुरादेर् यथैव तु । नहि द्रष्टुर् इति ह्य् उक्तं तस्माद् द्रष्टा सदैव भुक्
units.iast: na dṛṣṭir lupyate draṣṭuś cakṣurāder yathaiva tu । nahi draṣṭur iti hy uktaṃ tasmād draṣṭā sadaiva bhuk
units.translation: “The Seer’s vision is never destroyed, even as the eye and the other senses are; scripture says the Seer itself is never destroyed, and thus is always the experiencer.”

units.label: Verse I.15.19
units.deva: संघातो वास्मि भूतानां करणानां तथैव च । व्यस्तं वान्यतमो वास्मि को आस्मीति विचारयेत्
units.iast: saṃghāto vāsmi bhūtānāṃ karaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca । vyastaṃ vānyatamo vāsmi ko āsmīti vicārayet
units.translation: “Am I an aggregate of elements and senses, or each of them separately? One should inquire: ‘What am I?’”

units.label: Verse I.15.20
units.deva: व्यस्तं नाहं समस्तं वा भूतम् इन्द्रियम् एव वा । ज्ञेयत्वात् करणत्वाच् च ज्ञातान्यो ऽस्माद् घटादिवत्
units.iast: vyastaṃ nāhaṃ samastaṃ vā bhūtam indriyam eva vā । jñeyatvāt karaṇatvāc ca jñātānyo 'smād ghaṭādivat
units.translation: “I am neither an individual element nor their aggregate, nor any single sense. Because they are known and serve as instruments, I am distinct from them, like a pot.”

units.label: Verse I.15.21
units.deva: आत्माग्नेर् इन्धना बुद्धिर् अविद्याकामकर्मभिः । दीपिता प्रज्वलत्य् एष द्वारैः श्रोत्रादिभिः सदा
units.iast: ātmāgner indhanā buddhir avidyākāmakarmabhiḥ । dīpitā prajvalaty eṣa dvāraiḥ śrotrādibhiḥ sadā
units.translation: “The intellect is fuel for the fire of the Self. Ignorance, desire and action kindle it; it blazes continually through the openings of hearing and the other senses.”

units.label: Verse I.15.22
units.deva: दक्षिणाक्षिप्रधानेषु यदा बुद्धिर् विचेष्टते । विषयैर् हविषा दीप्ता आत्माग्निः स्थूलभुक् तदा
units.iast: dakṣiṇākṣipradhāneṣu yadā buddhir viceṣṭate । viṣayair haviṣā dīptā ātmāgniḥ sthūlabhuk tadā
units.translation: “When the intellect operates chiefly through the right eye, the fire of the Self, kindled by the offerings of sense objects, then consumes the gross world.”

units.label: Verse I.15.23
units.deva: हूयन्ते तु हवींषीति रूपादिग्रहणे स्मरन् । अरागद्वेष आत्माग्नौ जाग्रद्दोषैर् न लिप्यते
units.iast: hūyante tu havīṃṣīti rūpādigrahaṇe smaran । arāgadveṣa ātmāgnau jāgraddoṣair na lipyate
units.translation: “Remembering that forms and the rest are offered as oblations, the Self-fire, free of attachment and aversion, is not stained by the defects of waking.”

units.label: Verse I.15.24
units.deva: मानसे तु गृहे व्यक्ता अविद्याकर्मवासनाः । पश्यंस् तैजस आत्मोक्तः स्वयंज्योतिःप्रकाशिताः
units.iast: mānase tu gṛhe vyaktā avidyākarmavāsanāḥ । paśyaṃs taijasa ātmoktaḥ svayaṃjyotiḥprakāśitāḥ
units.translation: “When impressions of ignorance and action appear in the house of the mind, the Self is called Taijasa, seeing them illumined by its own light.”

units.label: Verse I.15.25
units.deva: विषया वासना वापि चोद्यन्ते नैव कर्मभिः । यदा बुद्धौ तदा ज्ञेयः प्राज्ञ आत्मा ह्य् अनन्यदृक्
units.iast: viṣayā vāsanā vāpi codyante naiva karmabhiḥ । yadā buddhau tadā jñeyaḥ prājña ātmā hy ananyadṛk
units.translation: “When objects or impressions are projected in the intellect, the Self is to be known as Prājña, seeing no other.”

units.label: Verse I.15.26
units.deva: मनोबुद्धीन्द्रियाणां या अवस्थाः कर्मचोदिताः । चैतन्येनैव भास्यन्ते रविणेव घटादयः
units.iast: manobuddhīndriyāṇāṃ yā avasthāḥ karmacoditāḥ । caitanyenaiva bhāsyante raviṇeva ghaṭādayaḥ
units.translation: “The states of mind, intellect and senses, prompted by action, are all illumined by consciousness alone, as pots and the rest are by the sun.”

units.label: Verse I.15.27
units.deva: तत्रैवं सति बुद्धीर् ज्ञ आत्मभासावभासयन् । कर्ता तासां यदर्थास् ता मूढैर् एवाभिधीयते
units.iast: tatraivaṃ sati buddhīr jña ātmabhāsāvabhāsayan । kartā tāsāṃ yadarthās tā mūḍhair evābhidhīyate
units.translation: “The knower, illuminating the intellects by the light of the Self, is called their agent by the deluded, because they are the objects those intellects attend to.”

units.label: Verse I.15.28
units.deva: सर्वज्ञो ऽप्य् अत एव स्यात् स्वेन भासावभासयन् । सर्वं सर्वक्रियाहेतोः सर्वकृत्त्वं तथात्मनः
units.iast: sarvajño 'py ata eva syāt svena bhāsāvabhāsayan । sarvaṃ sarvakriyāhetoḥ sarvakṛttvaṃ tathātmanaḥ
units.translation: “For this very reason the Self is all-knowing: illuminating everything by its own light, it is the cause of every action and is called the doer of all.”

units.label: Verse I.15.29
units.deva: सोपाधिश् चैवम् आत्मोक्तो निरुपाख्यो ऽनुपाधिकः । निष्कलो निर्गुणः शुद्धस् तं मनो वाक् च नाप्नुतः
units.iast: sopādhiś caivam ātmokto nirupākhyo 'nupādhikaḥ । niṣkalo nirguṇaḥ śuddhas taṃ mano vāk ca nāpnutaḥ
units.translation: “The Self is described with limiting adjuncts, but without them it is beyond description, partless, qualityless and pure; mind and speech do not reach it.”

units.label: Verse I.15.30
units.deva: चेतनो ऽचेतनो वापि कर्ताकर्ता गतो ऽगतः । बद्धो मुक्तस् तथा चैको नैकः शुद्धो ऽन्यथेति वा
units.iast: cetano 'cetano vāpi kartākartā gato 'gataḥ । baddho muktas tathā caiko naikaḥ śuddho 'nyatheti vā
units.translation: “Conscious or unconscious, agent or non-agent, moving or unmoving, bound or free, one or many, pure or otherwise—these are all [ways it is spoken of].”

units.label: Verse I.15.31
units.deva: अप्राप्यैव निवर्तन्ते वाचो धीभिः सहैव तु । निर्गुणत्वात् क्रियाभावाद् विशेषाणां ह्य् अभावतः
units.iast: aprāpyaiva nivartante vāco dhībhiḥ sahaiva tu । nirguṇatvāt kriyābhāvād viśeṣāṇāṃ hy abhāvataḥ
units.translation: “Words, along with the intellect, turn back without reaching it, because it has no qualities, action or distinctions.”

units.label: Verse I.15.32
units.deva: व्यापकं सर्वतो व्योम मूर्तैः सर्वैर् वियोजितम् । यथा तद्वद् इहात्मानं विद्याच् छुद्धं परं पदम्
units.iast: vyāpakaṃ sarvato vyoma mūrtaiḥ sarvair viyojitam । yathā tadvad ihātmānaṃ vidyāc chuddhaṃ paraṃ padam
units.translation: “As space is all-pervading and separate from every material form, so should one know the Self here as the pure, supreme reality.”

units.label: Verse I.15.33
units.deva: दृष्टं हित्वा स्मृतिं तस्मिन् सर्वग्रश् च तमस् त्यजेत् । सर्वदृग् ज्योतिषा युक्तो दिनकृच् छार्वरं यथा
units.iast: dṛṣṭaṃ hitvā smṛtiṃ tasmin sarvagraś ca tamas tyajet । sarvadṛg jyotiṣā yukto dinakṛc chārvaraṃ yathā
units.translation: “Set aside what is seen, memory and darkness; joined with the light of the all-seeing, be like the sun that dispels the night.”

units.label: Verse I.15.34
units.deva: रूपस्मृत्यन्धकारार्थाः प्रत्यया यस्य गोचराः । स एवात्मा समो द्रष्टा सर्वभूतेषु सर्वगः
units.iast: rūpasmṛtyandhakārārthāḥ pratyayā yasya gocarāḥ । sa evātmā samo draṣṭā sarvabhūteṣu sarvagaḥ
units.translation: “The Self is that which has thoughts of form, memory and darkness as its objects—the equal Seer, all-pervading in all beings.”

units.label: Verse I.15.35
units.deva: आत्मबुद्धिमनश्चक्षुर्विषयालोकसंगमात् । विचित्रो जायते बुद्धेः प्रत्ययो ऽज्ञानलक्षणः
units.iast: ātmabuddhimanaścakṣurviṣayālokasaṃgamāt । vicitro jāyate buddheḥ pratyayo 'jñānalakṣaṇaḥ
units.translation: “When the thought of Self, the mind, the eye, objects and light come together, the intellect produces diverse cognitions marked by ignorance.”

units.label: Verse I.15.36
units.deva: विविच्यास्मात् स्वम् आत्मानं विद्याच् छुद्धं परं पदम् । द्रष्टारं सर्वभूतस्थं समं सर्वभयातिगम्
units.iast: vivicyāsmāt svam ātmānaṃ vidyāc chuddhaṃ paraṃ padam । draṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtasthaṃ samaṃ sarvabhayātigam
units.translation: “Discerning one’s true Self from these, know it as the pure, supreme reality, the Seer dwelling in all beings, equal and beyond every fear.”

units.label: Verse I.15.37
units.deva: समस्तं सर्वगं शान्तं विमलं व्योमवत् स्थितम् । निष्कलं निष्क्रियं सर्वं नित्यं द्वन्द्वैर् विवर्जितम्
units.iast: samastaṃ sarvagaṃ śāntaṃ vimalaṃ vyomavat sthitam । niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ sarvaṃ nityaṃ dvandvair vivarjitam
units.translation: “It is complete, all-pervading, peaceful, pure and established like space; partless, actionless, all, eternal and free from every pair of opposites.”

units.label: Verse I.15.38
units.deva: सर्वप्रत्ययसाक्षी ज्ञः कथं ज्ञेयो मयेत्य् उत । विमृश्यैवं विजानीयाज् ज्ञातं ब्रह्म न वेति वा
units.iast: sarvapratyayasākṣī jñaḥ kathaṃ jñeyo mayety uta । vimṛśyaivaṃ vijānīyāj jñātaṃ brahma na veti vā
units.translation: “How could the knower, witness of every cognition, be known by me?” Having examined this, one should discern whether Brahman has been understood or not.

units.label: Verse I.15.39
units.deva: अदृष्टं द्रष्ट्र् अविज्ञातं दभ्रम् इत्यादिशासनात् । नैव ज्ञेयं मयान्यैर् वा परं ब्रह्म कथंचन
units.iast: adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭr avijñātaṃ dabhram ityādiśāsanāt । naiva jñeyaṃ mayānyair vā paraṃ brahma kathaṃcana
units.translation: “The supreme Brahman cannot in any way be known by me or another, as scripture says: ‘unseen, yet the Seer; unknown, yet the Knower; subtle…’”

units.label: Verse I.15.40
units.deva: स्वरूपाव्यवधानाभ्यां ज्ञानालोकस्वभावतः । अन्यज्ञानानपेक्षत्वाज् ज्ञातं चैव सदा मया
units.iast: svarūpāvyavadhānābhyāṃ jñānālokasvabhāvataḥ । anyajñānānapekṣatvāj jñātaṃ caiva sadā mayā
units.translation: “Because it is not separated from its own nature, because its nature is the light of knowledge, and because it depends on no other cognition, it is always known by me.”

units.label: Verse I.15.41
units.deva: नान्येन ज्योतिषा कार्यं रवेर् आत्मप्रकाशने । स्वबोधान् नान्यबोधेच्छा बोधस्यात्मप्रकाशने
units.iast: nānyena jyotiṣā kāryaṃ raver ātmaprakāśane । svabodhān nānyabodhecchā bodhasyātmaprakāśane
units.translation: “The sun needs no other light in order to illumine itself; awareness, by its own light, has no wish for another awareness to illumine it.”

units.label: Verse I.15.42
units.deva: न तस्यैवान्यतो ऽपेक्षा स्वरूपं यस्य यद् भवेत् । प्रकाशान्तरदृश्यो न प्रकाशो ह्य् अस्ति कश्चन
units.iast: na tasyaivānyato 'pekṣā svarūpaṃ yasya yad bhavet । prakāśāntaradṛśyo na prakāśo hy asti kaścana
units.translation: “Nothing whose nature is light depends on another to reveal that nature; no light exists that must itself be seen by a different light.”

units.label: Verse I.15.43
units.deva: व्यक्तिः स्याद् अप्रकाशस्य प्रकाशात्मसमागमात् । प्रकाशस् त्व् अर्ककार्यः स्याद् इति मिथ्य वचो ह्य् अतः
units.iast: vyaktiḥ syād aprakāśasya prakāśātmasamāgamāt । prakāśas tv arkakāryaḥ syād iti mithya vaco hy ataḥ
units.translation: “An unmanifest thing becomes manifest when it meets what is luminous; the claim that light is an effect of the sun is therefore false.”

units.label: Verse I.15.44
units.deva: यतो ऽभूत्वा भवेद् यच् च तस्य तत् कार्यम् इष्यते । स्वरूपत्वाद् अभूत्वा न प्रकाशो जायते रवेः
units.iast: yato 'bhūtvā bhaved yac ca tasya tat kāryam iṣyate । svarūpatvād abhūtvā na prakāśo jāyate raveḥ
units.translation: “What was not manifest and becomes manifest is regarded as an effect; but light does not arise from nonexistence, because light is the sun’s very nature.”

units.label: Verse I.15.45
units.deva: सत्तामात्रे प्रकाशस्य कर्तादित्यादिर् इष्यते । घटादिव्यक्तितो यद्वत् तद्वद् बोधात्मनीष्यताम्
units.iast: sattāmātre prakāśasya kartādityādir iṣyate । ghaṭādivyaktito yadvat tadvad bodhātmanīṣyatām
units.translation: “The sun is called the maker only of light’s manifestation, not of its existence; in the same way, awareness is the nature of the Self and is said to manifest things such as pots.”

units.label: Verse I.15.46
units.deva: बिलात् सर्पस्य निर्याणे सूर्यो यद्वत् प्रकाशकः । प्रयत्नेन विना तद्वज् ज्ञातात्मा बोधरूपतः
units.iast: bilāt sarpasya niryāṇe sūryo yadvat prakāśakaḥ । prayatnena vinā tadvaj jñātātmā bodharūpataḥ
units.translation: “As the sun illumines a snake emerging from a hole without effort, so the knower of the Self, by the nature of awareness, illumines without effort.”

units.label: Verse I.15.47
units.deva: दग्धैवम् उष्णः सत्तायां तद्वद् बोधात्मनीष्यताम् । सत्य् एव यद् उपाधौ तु ज्ञाते सर्प इवोत्थिते
units.iast: dagdhaivam uṣṇaḥ sattāyāṃ tadvad bodhātmanīṣyatām । saty eva yad upādhau tu jñāte sarpa ivotthite
units.translation: “Just as heat is inseparable from fire, awareness is inseparable from the Self. The adjunct may appear as a real snake, but once it is known, it is seen as it is.”

units.label: Verse I.15.48
units.deva: ज्ञातायत्नो ऽपि तद्वज् ज्ञः कर्ता भ्रामकवद् भवेत् । स्वरूपेण स्वयं नात्मा ज्ञेयो ऽज्ञेयो ऽथवा ततः
units.iast: jñātāyatno 'pi tadvaj jñaḥ kartā bhrāmakavad bhavet । svarūpeṇa svayaṃ nātmā jñeyo 'jñeyo 'thavā tataḥ
units.translation: “Though knowledge seems to require effort, the knower seems to become an agent, as in an illusion. By its own nature the Self is neither an object to be known nor something unknowable.”

units.label: Verse I.15.49
units.deva: विदिताविदिताभ्यां तद् अन्यद् एवेति शासनात् । बन्धमोक्षादयो भावास् तद्वद् आत्मनि कल्पिताः
units.iast: viditāviditābhyāṃ tad anyad eveti śāsanāt । bandhamokṣādayo bhāvās tadvad ātmani kalpitāḥ
units.translation: “Scripture says the Self is other than both the known and the unknown; bondage, liberation and the rest are likewise imagined in it.”

units.label: Verse I.15.50
units.deva: नाहोरात्रे यथा सूर्ये प्रभारूपाविशेषतः । बोधरूपाविशेषान् न बोधाबोधौ तथात्मनि
units.iast: nāhorātre yathā sūrye prabhārūpāviśeṣataḥ । bodharūpāviśeṣān na bodhābodhau tathātmani
units.translation: “As day and night do not belong to the sun, which is simply light, neither awareness nor its absence belongs to the Self, whose nature is awareness.”

units.label: Verse I.15.51
units.deva: यथोक्तं ब्रह्म यो वेद हानोपादानवर्जितम् । यथोक्तेन विधानेन स सत्यं नैव जायते
units.iast: yathoktaṃ brahma yo veda hānopādānavarjitam । yathoktena vidhānena sa satyaṃ naiva jāyate
units.translation: “One who knows Brahman as taught here, free of taking up and laying down, truly does not undergo birth.”

units.label: Verse I.15.52
units.deva: जन्ममृत्युप्रवाहेषु पतितो नैव शक्नुयात् । इत उद्धर्तुम् आत्मानं ज्ञानाद् अन्येन केनचित्
units.iast: janmamṛtyupravāheṣu patito naiva śaknuyāt । ita uddhartum ātmānaṃ jñānād anyena kenacit
units.translation: “Caught in the stream of births and deaths, no one can lift oneself out of it by anything other than knowledge.”

units.label: Verse I.15.53
units.deva: "भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश् छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्ट" इति श्रुतेः
units.iast: "bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ । kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭa" iti śruteḥ
units.translation: “When that is seen, the knot of the heart is severed, all doubts are cut, and one’s actions are exhausted,” says scripture.

units.label: Verse I.15.54
units.deva: ममाहम् इत्य् एतद् अपोह्य सर्वतो विमुक्तदेहं पदम् अम्बरोपमम् । सुदृष्टशास्त्रानुमितिभ्य ईरितं विमुच्यते ऽस्मिन् यदि निश्चितो नरः
units.iast: mamāham ity etad apohya sarvato vimuktadehaṃ padam ambaropamam । sudṛṣṭaśāstrānumitibhya īritaṃ vimucyate 'smin yadi niścito naraḥ
units.translation: “Setting aside ‘I’ and ‘mine’ entirely, one reaches the bodiless state like space. This is taught by scripture and sound reasoning; a person who is certain of it is freed.”

units.label: Verse I.16.1
units.deva: पार्थिवः कठिनो धातुर् द्रवो देहे स्मृतो ऽम्मयः । पक्तिचेष्टावकाशाः स्युर् वह्निवाय्वम्बरोद्भवाः
units.iast: pārthivaḥ kaṭhino dhātur dravo dehe smṛto 'mmayaḥ । pakticeṣṭāvakāśāḥ syur vahnivāyvambarodbhavāḥ
units.translation: “The earth element in the body is hard; the water element is fluid. Digestion and movement arise from fire and air; space provides room.”

units.label: Verse I.16.2
units.deva: घ्राणादीनि तदर्थाश् च पृथिव्यादिगुणाः क्रमात् । रूपालोकवद् इष्टं हि सजातीयार्थम् इन्द्रियम्
units.iast: ghrāṇādīni tadarthāś ca pṛthivyādiguṇāḥ kramāt । rūpālokavad iṣṭaṃ hi sajātīyārtham indriyam
units.translation: “Smell and the other senses, together with their objects, correspond in turn to the qualities of earth and the rest; a sense is suited to an object of its own kind, as sight is to form and light.”

units.label: Verse I.16.3
units.deva: बुद्ध्यर्थान्य् आहुर् एतानि वाक्पाण्यादीनि कर्मणे । तद्विकल्पार्थम् अन्तस्थं मन एकादशं भवेत्
units.iast: buddhyarthāny āhur etāni vākpāṇyādīni karmaṇe । tadvikalpārtham antasthaṃ mana ekādaśaṃ bhavet
units.translation: “Speech, the hands and the other organs of action serve action; the senses serve cognition. The mind within, the eleventh, organizes their different functions.”

units.label: Verse I.16.4
units.deva: निश्चयार्था भवेद् बुद्धिस् तां सर्वार्थानुभाविनीम् । ज्ञातात्मोक्तः स्वरूपेण ज्योतिषा व्यञ्जयन् सदा
units.iast: niścayārthā bhaved buddhis tāṃ sarvārthānubhāvinīm । jñātātmoktaḥ svarūpeṇa jyotiṣā vyañjayan sadā
units.translation: “The intellect determines; it experiences all objects. The knower of the Self is said to reveal it continually by the light of its own nature.”

units.label: Verse I.16.5
units.deva: व्यञ्जकस् तु यथालोको व्यङ्ग्यस्याकारतां गतः । व्यतिकीर्णो ऽप्य् असंकीर्णस् तद्वज् ज्ञः प्रत्ययैः सदा
units.iast: vyañjakas tu yathāloko vyaṅgyasyākāratāṃ gataḥ । vyatikīrṇo 'py asaṃkīrṇas tadvaj jñaḥ pratyayaiḥ sadā
units.translation: “As light, though mixed with what it reveals, appears to take on that thing’s form, yet remains unmixed, so the knower is always distinct from the thoughts.”

units.label: Verse I.16.6
units.deva: स्थितो दीपो यथायत्नः प्राप्तं सर्वं प्रकाशयेत् । शब्दाद्याकारबुद्धीर् ज्ञः प्राप्तास् तद्वत् प्रपश्यति
units.iast: sthito dīpo yathāyatnaḥ prāptaṃ sarvaṃ prakāśayet । śabdādyākārabuddhīr jñaḥ prāptās tadvat prapaśyati
units.translation: “As a lamp standing still without effort illuminates everything brought before it, the knower sees the cognitions of sound and the rest as they arise.”

units.label: Verse I.16.7
units.deva: शरीरेन्द्रियसंघात आत्मत्वेन गतां धियम् । नित्यात्मज्योतिषा दीप्तां विशिंषन्ति सुखादयः
units.iast: śarīrendriyasaṃghāta ātmatvena gatāṃ dhiyam । nityātmajyotiṣā dīptāṃ viśiṃṣanti sukhādayaḥ
units.translation: “Happiness and the rest distinguish the cognition identified with the body and senses; that cognition is lit by the eternal light of the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.16.8
units.deva: शिरोदुःखादिनात्मानं दुःख्य् अस्मीति हि पश्यति । द्रष्टान्यो दुःखिनो दृश्याद् द्रष्टृत्वच् च न दुःख्य् असौ
units.iast: śiroduḥkhādinātmānaṃ duḥkhy asmīti hi paśyati । draṣṭānyo duḥkhino dṛśyād draṣṭṛtvac ca na duḥkhy asau
units.translation: “Because of a headache and the like, one thinks ‘I am suffering.’ The witness is other than the suffering that is seen, and, as Seer, does not suffer.”

units.label: Verse I.16.9
units.deva: दुःखी स्याद् दुःख्यहंमानाद् दुःखिनो दर्शनान् न वा । संहते ऽङ्गादिभिर् द्रष्टा दुःखी दुःखस्य नैव सः
units.iast: duḥkhī syād duḥkhyahaṃmānād duḥkhino darśanān na vā । saṃhate 'ṅgādibhir draṣṭā duḥkhī duḥkhasya naiva saḥ
units.translation: “Does one suffer because of the thought ‘I am suffering,’ or because one sees someone suffering? The Seer is joined to body and limbs, but is not itself the sufferer.”

units.label: Verse I.16.10
units.deva: चक्षुर्वत् कर्मकर्तृत्वं स्याच् चेन् नानेकम् एव तत् । संहतं च ततो नात्मा द्रष्टृत्वात् कर्मतां व्रजेत्
units.iast: cakṣurvat karmakartṛtvaṃ syāc cen nānekam eva tat । saṃhataṃ ca tato nātmā draṣṭṛtvāt karmatāṃ vrajet
units.translation: “If the Self were agent and object of action like the eye, it would be many; because it is a composite, it is not the Self. The witness does not become an object of action.”

units.label: Verse I.16.11
units.deva: ज्ञानयत्नाद्यनेकत्वम् आत्मनो ऽपि मतं यदि । नैकज्ञानगुणत्वात् तु ज्योतिर्वत् तस्य कर्मता
units.iast: jñānayatnādyanekatvam ātmano 'pi mataṃ yadi । naikajñānaguṇatvāt tu jyotirvat tasya karmatā
units.translation: “If many acts of knowing and effort belonged to the Self, it would be many; but the Self has one nature of awareness, like light, and is not an agent.”

units.label: Verse I.16.12
units.deva: ज्योतिषो द्योतकत्वे ऽपि यद्वन् नात्मप्रकाशनम् । भेदे ऽप्य् एवं समत्वाज् ज्ञ आत्मानं नैव पश्यति
units.iast: jyotiṣo dyotakatve 'pi yadvan nātmaprakāśanam । bhede 'py evaṃ samatvāj jña ātmānaṃ naiva paśyati
units.translation: “Although light illumines things, it does not illumine itself as an object; so too the knower, though distinct from objects, does not see itself as an object.”

units.label: Verse I.16.13
units.deva: यद्धर्मा यः पदार्थो न तस्यैवेयात् स कर्मताम् । न ह्य् आत्मानं दहत्य् अग्निस् तथा नैव प्रकाशयेत्
units.iast: yaddharmā yaḥ padārtho na tasyaiveyāt sa karmatām । na hy ātmānaṃ dahaty agnis tathā naiva prakāśayet
units.translation: “A thing cannot become an object of action for what has the same nature; fire does not burn itself. So the Self does not illumine itself as an object.”

units.label: Verse I.16.14
units.deva: एतेनैवात्मनात्मनो ग्रहो बुद्धेर् निराकृतः । अंशो ऽप्य् एवं समत्वाद् धि निर्भेदत्वान् न युज्यते
units.iast: etenaivātmanātmano graho buddher nirākṛtaḥ । aṃśo 'py evaṃ samatvād dhi nirbhedatvān na yujyate
units.translation: “By this reasoning the intellect cannot grasp the Self as an object. A part of the Self cannot do so either, for it is not divided from the whole.”

units.label: Verse I.16.15
units.deva: शून्यतापि न युक्तैवं बुद्धेर् अन्येन दृश्यता । उक्तातो घटवत् तस्याः प्राक् सिद्धेश् च विकल्पतः
units.iast: śūnyatāpi na yuktaivaṃ buddher anyena dṛśyatā । uktāto ghaṭavat tasyāḥ prāk siddheś ca vikalpataḥ
units.translation: “Nor is it reasonable to say the Self is void. The intellect is seen by another, like a pot; before it is established, one can posit many alternatives.”

units.label: Verse I.16.16
units.deva: अविकल्पं तद् अस्त्य् एव यत् पूर्वं स्याद् विकल्पतः । विकल्पोत्पत्तिहेतुत्वाद् यद्य् अस्यैव च कारणम्
units.iast: avikalpaṃ tad asty eva yat pūrvaṃ syād vikalpataḥ । vikalpotpattihetutvād yady asyaiva ca kāraṇam
units.translation: “That which is free of conceptual thought exists before thought arises, since it is the cause from which those thoughts arise.”

units.label: Verse I.16.17
units.deva: अज्ञानं कल्पनामूलं संसारस्य नियामकम् । हित्वात्मानं परं ब्रह्म विद्यान् मुक्तं सदाभयम्
units.iast: ajñānaṃ kalpanāmūlaṃ saṃsārasya niyāmakam । hitvātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma vidyān muktaṃ sadābhayam
units.translation: “Ignorance is the root of imagination and governs worldly bondage. Setting it aside, know yourself as the supreme Brahman, ever free and fearless.”

units.label: Verse I.16.18
units.deva: जाग्रत्स्वप्नौ तयोर् बीजं सुषुप्ताख्यं तमोमयम् । अन्योन्यस्मिन्न् असत्त्वाच् च नास्तीत्य् एतत् त्रयं त्यजेत्
units.iast: jāgratsvapnau tayor bījaṃ suṣuptākhyaṃ tamomayam । anyonyasminn asattvāc ca nāstīty etat trayaṃ tyajet
units.translation: “Wakefulness and dream, and the darkness called deep sleep that is their seed, are mutually absent; one should relinquish all three.”

units.label: Verse I.16.19
units.deva: आत्मबुद्धिमनश्चक्षुरालोकार्थादिसंकरात् भ्रान्तिः स्याद् आत्मकर्मेति क्रियाणां संनिपाततः
units.iast: ātmabuddhimanaścakṣurālokārthādisaṃkarāt bhrāntiḥ syād ātmakarmeti kriyāṇāṃ saṃnipātataḥ
units.translation: “When the thought of Self is mixed with mind, intellect, eye, light and objects, confusion arises and actions are wrongly attributed to the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.16.20
units.deva: निमीलोन्मीलने स्थाने वायव्ये ते न चक्षुषः । प्रकाशत्वान् मनस्य् एवं बुद्धौ न स्तः प्रकाशतः
units.iast: nimīlonmīlane sthāne vāyavye te na cakṣuṣaḥ । prakāśatvān manasy evaṃ buddhau na staḥ prakāśataḥ
units.translation: “Opening and closing the eyelids are functions of air, not of the eye. Likewise the mind’s and intellect’s activity is not the light of awareness.”

units.label: Verse I.16.21
units.deva: संकल्पाध्यवसायौ तु मनोबुद्ध्योर् यथाक्रमात् । नेतरेतरधर्मत्वं सर्वं चात्मनि कल्पितम्
units.iast: saṃkalpādhyavasāyau tu manobuddhyor yathākramāt । netaretaradharmatvaṃ sarvaṃ cātmani kalpitam
units.translation: “Conception and determination belong respectively to the mind and intellect; they are not each other’s properties. Everything is imagined in the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.16.22
units.deva: स्थानावच्छेददृष्टिः स्याद् इन्द्रियाणां तदात्मताम् । गता धीस् तं हि पश्यञ् ज्ञो देहमात्र इवेक्ष्यते
units.iast: sthānāvacchedadṛṣṭiḥ syād indriyāṇāṃ tadātmatām । gatā dhīs taṃ hi paśyañ jño dehamātra ivekṣyate
units.translation: “Because the senses see only from their limited locations, the intellect identifies with them; the knower, seeing this, is regarded as nothing more than the body.”

units.label: Verse I.16.23
units.deva: क्षणिकं हि तद् अत्यर्थं धर्ममात्रं निरन्तरम् । सादृश्याद् दीपवत् तद्धीस् तच्छान्तिः पुरुषार्थता
units.iast: kṣaṇikaṃ hi tad atyarthaṃ dharmamātraṃ nirantaram । sādṛśyād dīpavat taddhīs tacchāntiḥ puruṣārthatā
units.translation: “That [mental state] is extremely fleeting, only a quality, momentary; because of similarity it seems continuous, like a lamp. Its cessation is held to be the human goal.”

units.label: Verse I.16.24
units.deva: स्वाकारान्यावभासं च येषां रूपादि विद्यते । येषां नास्ति ततश् चान्यत् पूर्वासंगतिर् उच्यते
units.iast: svākārānyāvabhāsaṃ ca yeṣāṃ rūpādi vidyate । yeṣāṃ nāsti tataś cānyat pūrvāsaṃgatir ucyate
units.translation: “Some things have color and other forms that appear in cognition as their own; things without such forms are said to be different, with no connection to the former.”

units.label: Verse I.16.25
units.deva: बाह्याकारत्वतो ज्ञप्तेः स्मृत्यभावः सदा क्षणात् । क्षणिकत्वाच् च संस्कारं नैवाधत्ते क्वचित् तु धिः
units.iast: bāhyākāratvato jñapteḥ smṛtyabhāvaḥ sadā kṣaṇāt । kṣaṇikatvāc ca saṃskāraṃ naivādhatte kvacit tu dhiḥ
units.translation: “If cognition always takes an external form, it disappears in an instant and cannot yield memory; being momentary, it leaves no impression anywhere.”

units.label: Verse I.16.26
units.deva: आधारस्याप्य् असत्त्वाच् च तुल्यतानिर्निमित्ततः । स्थाने वा क्षणिकत्वस्य हानं स्यान् न तद् इष्यते
units.iast: ādhārasyāpy asattvāc ca tulyatānirnimittataḥ । sthāne vā kṣaṇikatvasya hānaṃ syān na tad iṣyate
units.translation: “There is no support for such an impression, and no reason to treat it as equal to the cognition. If it were located in a lasting basis, momentariness would be lost, which is not accepted.”

units.label: Verse I.16.27
units.deva: शान्तेश् चायत्नसिद्धत्वात् साधनोक्तिर् अनर्थिका । एकैकस्मिन् समाप्तत्वाच् छान्तेर् अन्यानपेक्षता
units.iast: śānteś cāyatnasiddhatvāt sādhanoktir anarthikā । ekaikasmin samāptatvāc chānter anyānapekṣatā
units.translation: “Since cessation is accomplished without effort, the teaching of a means is pointless; if each moment has already ended, cessation cannot depend on anything else.”

units.label: Verse I.16.28
units.deva: अपेक्षा यदि भिन्ने ऽपि परसंतान इष्यताम् । सर्वार्थे क्षणिके कस्मिंस् तथाप्य् अन्यानपेक्षता
units.iast: apekṣā yadi bhinne 'pi parasaṃtāna iṣyatām । sarvārthe kṣaṇike kasmiṃs tathāpy anyānapekṣatā
units.translation: “If one allows relation even with another stream of moments, why would a momentary thing in every respect not depend on another?”

units.label: Verse I.16.29
units.deva: तुल्यकालसमुद्भूताव् इतरेतरयोगिनौ । योगाच् च संस्कृतो यस् तु सो ऽन्यं हीक्षितुम् अर्हति
units.iast: tulyakālasamudbhūtāv itaretarayoginau । yogāc ca saṃskṛto yas tu so 'nyaṃ hīkṣitum arhati
units.translation: “Two things arise at the same time and are connected with one another; whatever is conditioned by that connection ought to be able to perceive the other.”

units.label: Verse I.16.30
units.deva: मृषाध्यासस् तु यत्र स्यात् तन्नाशस् तत्र नो मतः । सर्वनाशो भवेद् यस्य मोक्षः कस्य फलं वद
units.iast: mṛṣādhyāsas tu yatra syāt tannāśas tatra no mataḥ । sarvanāśo bhaved yasya mokṣaḥ kasya phalaṃ vada
units.translation: “Where there is a false superimposition, we do not say that it is destroyed in this way. If everything were annihilated, tell me: for whom would liberation be the fruit?”

units.label: Verse I.16.31
units.deva: अस्ति तावत् स्वयं नाम ज्ञानं वात्मान्यद् एव वा । भावाभावज्ञतस् तस्य नाभावस् त्व् अधिगम्यते
units.iast: asti tāvat svayaṃ nāma jñānaṃ vātmānyad eva vā । bhāvābhāvajñatas tasya nābhāvas tv adhigamyate
units.translation: “Knowledge exists in itself, or as something other than the Self. Since it knows what exists and what does not, the absence of knowledge cannot itself be known.”

units.label: Verse I.16.32
units.deva: येनाधिगम्यते ऽभावस् तत् सत् स्यात् तन् न चेद् भवेत् । भावाभावानभिज्ञत्वं लोकस्य स्यान् न चेष्यते
units.iast: yenādhigamyate 'bhāvas tat sat syāt tan na ced bhavet । bhāvābhāvānabhijñatvaṃ lokasya syān na ceṣyate
units.translation: “That by which absence is known must exist; if it did not, the world could not know existence and nonexistence. That is not accepted.”

units.label: Verse I.16.33
units.deva: सद् असत् सदसच् चेति विकल्पात् प्राग् यद् इष्यते । तद् अद्वैतं समत्वात् तु नित्यं चान्यद् विकल्पितात्
units.iast: sad asat sadasac ceti vikalpāt prāg yad iṣyate । tad advaitaṃ samatvāt tu nityaṃ cānyad vikalpitāt
units.translation: “Before the alternatives ‘existent,’ ‘nonexistent’ and ‘both’ arise, what is held to be is nondual and equal, eternal; difference is only imagined.”

units.label: Verse I.16.34
units.deva: विकल्पोद्भवतो ऽसत्त्वं स्वप्नदृश्यवद् इष्यताम् । द्वैतस्य प्राग् असत्त्वाच् च सदसत्त्वादिकल्पनात्
units.iast: vikalpodbhavato 'sattvaṃ svapnadṛśyavad iṣyatām । dvaitasya prāg asattvāc ca sadasattvādikalpanāt
units.translation: “Since concepts arise, their objects are unreal, like what is seen in a dream. Duality was absent before; the ideas of existence and nonexistence are therefore imagined.”

units.label: Verse I.16.35
units.deva: वाचारम्भणशास्त्राच् च विकाराणां ह्य् अभावता । मृत्योः स मृत्युम् इत्यादेर् मम मायेति च स्मृतेः
units.iast: vācārambhaṇaśāstrāc ca vikārāṇāṃ hy abhāvatā । mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum ityāder mama māyeti ca smṛteḥ
units.translation: “Scripture teaches that change is only a matter of words; it says ‘from death to death’ and ‘this is my māyā,’ and the like.”

units.label: Verse I.16.36
units.deva: विशुद्धिश् चात एवास्य विकल्पाच् च विलक्षणात् । उपादेयो न हेयो ऽत आत्मा नान्यैर् अकल्पितः
units.iast: viśuddhiś cāta evāsya vikalpāc ca vilakṣaṇāt । upādeyo na heyo 'ta ātmā nānyair akalpitaḥ
units.translation: “The Self is pure because it is distinct from every imagined notion. Therefore it is not something to be taken up or abandoned; it is not imagined by anything else.”

units.label: Verse I.16.37
units.deva: अप्रकाशो यथादित्ये नास्ति ज्योतिःस्वभावतः । नित्यबोधस्वरूपत्वान् नाज्ञानं तद्वद् आत्मनि
units.iast: aprakāśo yathāditye nāsti jyotiḥsvabhāvataḥ । nityabodhasvarūpatvān nājñānaṃ tadvad ātmani
units.translation: “Just as there is no darkness in the sun, whose nature is light, so there is no ignorance in the Self, whose nature is eternal awareness.”

units.label: Verse I.16.38
units.deva: तथाविक्रियरूपत्वान् नावस्थान्तरम् आत्मनः । अवस्थान्तरवत्त्वे हि नाशो ऽस्य स्यान् न संशयः
units.iast: tathāvikriyarūpatvān nāvasthāntaram ātmanaḥ । avasthāntaravattve hi nāśo 'sya syān na saṃśayaḥ
units.translation: “The Self does not pass into another state, because it is changeless; if it could change states, it would surely perish.”

units.label: Verse I.16.39
units.deva: मोक्षो ऽवस्थान्तरं यस्य कृतकः स चलो ह्य् अतः । न संयोगो वियोगो वा मोक्षो युक्तः कथंचन
units.iast: mokṣo 'vasthāntaraṃ yasya kṛtakaḥ sa calo hy ataḥ । na saṃyogo viyogo vā mokṣo yuktaḥ kathaṃcana
units.translation: “If liberation were a different state, it would be made and therefore transient. Liberation cannot reasonably be union or separation.”

units.label: Verse I.16.40
units.deva: संयोगस्याप्य् अनित्यत्वाद् वियोगस्य तथैव च । गमनागमने चैव स्वरूपं तु न हीयते
units.iast: saṃyogasyāpy anityatvād viyogasya tathaiva ca । gamanāgamane caiva svarūpaṃ tu na hīyate
units.translation: “Union and separation are both impermanent, as are coming and going; one’s own nature, however, is never lost.”

units.label: Verse I.16.41
units.deva: स्वरूपस्यानिमित्तत्वात् सनिमित्ता हि चापरे । अनुपात्तं स्वरूपं हि स्वेनात्यक्तं तथैव च
units.iast: svarūpasyānimittatvāt sanimittā hi cāpare । anupāttaṃ svarūpaṃ hi svenātyaktaṃ tathaiva ca
units.translation: “One’s own nature has no cause, while other things have causes; it is neither acquired nor relinquished by oneself.”

units.label: Verse I.16.42
units.deva: स्वरूपत्वान् न सर्वस्य त्यक्तुं शक्यो ह्य् अनन्यतः । गृहीतुं वा ततो नित्यो ऽविषयत्वापृथक्त्वतः
units.iast: svarūpatvān na sarvasya tyaktuṃ śakyo hy ananyataḥ । gṛhītuṃ vā tato nityo 'viṣayatvāpṛthaktvataḥ
units.translation: “One cannot relinquish what is one’s own nature, since it is not separate; nor can one take it up. It is eternal, not an object, and never apart.”

units.label: Verse I.16.43
units.deva: आत्मार्थत्वाच् च सर्वस्य नित्य आत्मैव केवलः । त्यजेत् तस्मात् क्रियाः सर्वाः साधनैः सह मोक्षवित्
units.iast: ātmārthatvāc ca sarvasya nitya ātmaiva kevalaḥ । tyajet tasmāt kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sādhanaiḥ saha mokṣavit
units.translation: “Everything is for the sake of the Self; the Self alone is eternal. Therefore the knower of liberation should give up all actions and their means.”

units.label: Verse I.16.44
units.deva: आत्मलाभः परो लाभ इति शास्त्रोपपत्तयः । अलाभो ऽन्यात्मलाभस् तु त्यजेत् तस्माद् अनात्मताम्
units.iast: ātmalābhaḥ paro lābha iti śāstropapattayaḥ । alābho 'nyātmalābhas tu tyajet tasmād anātmatām
units.translation: “Attainment of the Self is the highest attainment taught by scripture and reason. Attainment of another self is no attainment; therefore give up the not-Self.”

units.label: Verse I.16.45
units.deva: गुणानां समभावस्य भ्रंशो न ह्य् उपपद्यते । अविद्यादेः प्रसुप्तत्वान् न चान्यो हेतुर् इष्यते
units.iast: guṇānāṃ samabhāvasya bhraṃśo na hy upapadyate । avidyādeḥ prasuptatvān na cānyo hetur iṣyate
units.translation: “A disturbance in the equilibrium of the qualities cannot be accounted for; ignorance is dormant, and no other cause is accepted.”

units.label: Verse I.16.46
units.deva: इतरेतरहेतुत्वे प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् सदा न वा । नियमो न प्रवृत्तीनां गुणेष्व् आत्मनि वा भवेत्
units.iast: itaretarahetutve pravṛttiḥ syāt sadā na vā । niyamo na pravṛttīnāṃ guṇeṣv ātmani vā bhavet
units.translation: “If the qualities caused one another, they would be either always active or never active; there could be no rule governing activity in the qualities or the Self.”

units.label: Verse I.16.47
units.deva: विशेषो मुक्तबद्धानां तादर्थ्ये च न युज्यते । अर्थार्थिनोश् च संबन्धो नार्थी ज्ञो नेतरो ऽपि वा
units.iast: viśeṣo muktabaddhānāṃ tādarthye ca na yujyate । arthārthinoś ca saṃbandho nārthī jño netaro 'pi vā
units.translation: “If that were so, there could be no real distinction between the bound and the liberated; nor would the relation between a seeker and the sought make sense. The knower is not a seeker, nor is anyone else.”

units.label: Verse I.16.48
units.deva: प्रधानस्य च पारार्थ्यं पुरुषस्याविकारतः । न युक्तं सांख्यशास्त्रे ऽपि विकारे ऽपि न युज्यते
units.iast: pradhānasya ca pārārthyaṃ puruṣasyāvikārataḥ । na yuktaṃ sāṃkhyaśāstre 'pi vikāre 'pi na yujyate
units.translation: “Even in the Sāṅkhya teaching, the unconscious Pradhāna’s existence for the sake of the unchanging Puruṣa makes no sense; even if it changed, it would not be reasonable.”

units.label: Verse I.16.49
units.deva: संबन्धानुपपत्तेश् च प्रकृतेः पुरुषस्य च । मिथो ऽयुक्तं तदर्थत्वं प्रधानस्याचितित्वतः
units.iast: saṃbandhānupapatteś ca prakṛteḥ puruṣasya ca । mitho 'yuktaṃ tadarthatvaṃ pradhānasyācititvataḥ
units.translation: “Since no relation between Prakṛti and Puruṣa can be established, it is not reasonable to say that Pradhāna acts for the sake of Puruṣa, for Pradhāna is unconscious.”

units.label: Verse I.16.50
units.deva: क्रियोत्पत्तौ विनाशित्वं ज्ञानमात्रे च पूर्ववत् । निर्निमित्ते त्व् अनिर्मोक्षः प्रधानस्य प्रसज्यते
units.iast: kriyotpattau vināśitvaṃ jñānamātre ca pūrvavat । nirnimitte tv anirmokṣaḥ pradhānasya prasajyate
units.translation: “Action arises and perishes; mere cognition is subject to the same difficulty as before. If liberation had no cause, then no liberation would follow for Pradhāna.”

units.label: Verse I.16.51
units.deva: न प्रकाश्यं यथोष्णत्वं ज्ञानेनैवं सुखादयः । एकनीडत्वतो ऽग्राह्याः स्युः कणादादिवर्त्मनाम्
units.iast: na prakāśyaṃ yathoṣṇatvaṃ jñānenaivaṃ sukhādayaḥ । ekanīḍatvato 'grāhyāḥ syuḥ kaṇādādivartmanām
units.translation: “Heat is not made manifest by cognition; likewise, happiness and the rest cannot be perceived as qualities inhering in one thing, as in the systems of Kaṇāda and others.”

units.label: Verse I.16.52
units.deva: युगपच् चासमेतत्वात् सुखविज्ञानयोर् अपि । मनोयोगैकहेतुत्वाद् अग्राह्यत्वं सुखस्य च
units.iast: yugapac cāsametatvāt sukhavijñānayor api । manoyogaikahetutvād agrāhyatvaṃ sukhasya ca
units.translation: “Happiness and cognition do not arise together, because they are not conjoined; and happiness cannot be grasped when the mind’s connection is its only cause.”

units.label: Verse I.16.53
units.deva: तथान्येषां च भिन्नत्वाद् युगपज्जन्म नेष्यते । गुणानां समवेतत्वं ज्ञानं चेन् न विशेषणात्
units.iast: tathānyeṣāṃ ca bhinnatvād yugapajjanma neṣyate । guṇānāṃ samavetatvaṃ jñānaṃ cen na viśeṣaṇāt
units.translation: “The other qualities are distinct, so simultaneous arising is not accepted. If cognition inheres in them as their qualifier, they are still not distinct in that way.”

units.label: Verse I.16.54
units.deva: ज्ञानेनैव विशेष्यत्वाज् ज्ञानाप्यत्वं स्मृतेस् तथा । सुखं ज्ञातं मयेत्य् एवं तवाज्ञानात्मकत्वतः
units.iast: jñānenaiva viśeṣyatvāj jñānāpyatvaṃ smṛtes tathā । sukhaṃ jñātaṃ mayety evaṃ tavājñānātmakatvataḥ
units.translation: “Because it is qualified by cognition, it is known through cognition and remembered as such: ‘I knew happiness.’ Thus your own view makes happiness an object of awareness.”

units.label: Verse I.16.55
units.deva: सुखादेर् नात्मधर्मत्वम् आत्मनस् ते ऽविकारतः । भेदाद् अन्यस्य कस्मान् न मनसो वाविशेषतः
units.iast: sukhāder nātmadharmatvam ātmanas te 'vikārataḥ । bhedād anyasya kasmān na manaso vāviśeṣataḥ
units.translation: “Happiness and the rest are not properties of the Self, because the Self is changeless. If they are different from it, why should they not be properties of the mind?”

units.label: Verse I.16.56
units.deva: स्यान् मालापरिहार्या तु ज्ञानं चेज् ज्ञेयतां व्रजेत् । युगपद् वापि चोत्पत्तिर् अभ्युपेते ऽन्त इष्यते
units.iast: syān mālāparihāryā tu jñānaṃ cej jñeyatāṃ vrajet । yugapad vāpi cotpattir abhyupete 'nta iṣyate
units.translation: “If cognition itself becomes an object of cognition, there would be an endless chain. Or, at the end, you must admit that they arise together.”

units.label: Verse I.16.57
units.deva: अनवस्थान्तरत्वाच् च बन्धो नात्मनि विद्यते । नाशुद्धिश् चाप्य् असङ्गत्वाद् असङ्गो हीति च श्रुतेः
units.iast: anavasthāntaratvāc ca bandho nātmani vidyate । nāśuddhiś cāpy asaṅgatvād asaṅgo hīti ca śruteḥ
units.translation: “The Self has no other state, so there is no bondage in it; being unattached, it has no impurity, as scripture says, ‘unattached indeed.’”

units.label: Verse I.16.58
units.deva: सूक्ष्मैकागोचरेभ्यश् च न लिप्यत इति श्रुतेः । एवं तर्हि न मोक्षो ऽस्ति बन्धाभावात् कथंचन
units.iast: sūkṣmaikāgocarebhyaś ca na lipyata iti śruteḥ । evaṃ tarhi na mokṣo 'sti bandhābhāvāt kathaṃcana
units.translation: “Scripture says it is unstained even by the subtle [body and its states]. If so, one might object, there can be no liberation, since there is no bondage at all.”

units.label: Verse I.16.59
units.deva: शास्त्रानर्थक्यम् एवं स्यान् न बुद्धेर् भ्रान्तिर् इष्यते । बन्धो मोक्षश् च तन्नाशः स यथोक्तो न चान्यथा
units.iast: śāstrānarthakyam evaṃ syān na buddher bhrāntir iṣyate । bandho mokṣaś ca tannāśaḥ sa yathokto na cānyathā
units.translation: “Then scripture would be pointless. But we accept the intellect’s delusion. Bondage, liberation and the ending of bondage are as explained, and not otherwise.”

units.label: Verse I.16.60
units.deva: बोधात्मज्योतिषा दीप्ता बोधम् आत्मनि मन्यते । बुद्धिर् नान्यो ऽस्ति बोद्धेति सेयं भ्रान्तिर् हि धीगता
units.iast: bodhātmajyotiṣā dīptā bodham ātmani manyate । buddhir nānyo 'sti boddheti seyaṃ bhrāntir hi dhīgatā
units.translation: “The intellect, lit by the light of awareness, thinks that awareness is within itself; it imagines, ‘There is no knower other than me.’ This delusion belongs to the intellect.”

units.label: Verse I.16.61
units.deva: बोधस्यात्मस्वरूपत्वान् नित्यं तत्रोपचर्यते । अविवेको ऽप्य् अनाद्यो ऽयं संसारो नान्य इष्यते
units.iast: bodhasyātmasvarūpatvān nityaṃ tatropacaryate । aviveko 'py anādyo 'yaṃ saṃsāro nānya iṣyate
units.translation: “Because awareness is the Self’s nature, it is always spoken of as belonging to the Self. This beginningless lack of discrimination alone is called worldly bondage.”

units.label: Verse I.16.62
units.deva: मोक्षस् तन्नाश एव स्यान् नान्यथानुपपत्तितः । येषां वस्त्वन्तरापत्तिर् मोक्षो नाशस् तु तैर् मतः
units.iast: mokṣas tannāśa eva syān nānyathānupapattitaḥ । yeṣāṃ vastvantarāpattir mokṣo nāśas tu tair mataḥ
units.translation: “Liberation is only the ending of that [ignorance], since no other account is possible. Those who say liberation is attainment of another reality hold that it is destruction.”

units.label: Verse I.16.63
units.deva: अवस्थान्तरम् अप्य् एवम् अविकारान् न युज्यते । विकारे ऽवयवित्वं स्यात् ततो नाशो घटादिवत्
units.iast: avasthāntaram apy evam avikārān na yujyate । vikāre 'vayavitvaṃ syāt tato nāśo ghaṭādivat
units.translation: “A different state is likewise impossible for what is changeless. Change would imply parts and therefore destruction, as with a pot.”

units.label: Verse I.16.64
units.deva: तस्माद् भ्रान्तिर् अतो ऽन्या हि बन्धमोक्षादिकल्पनाः । सांख्यकाणादबौद्धानां मीमांसाहतकल्पनाः
units.iast: tasmād bhrāntir ato 'nyā hi bandhamokṣādikalpanāḥ । sāṃkhyakāṇādabauddhānāṃ mīmāṃsāhatakalpanāḥ
units.translation: “Therefore bondage, liberation and the rest, other than delusion, are only imagined. These are the confused doctrines of Sāṅkhya, Kaṇāda, Buddhists and Mīmāṃsakas.”

units.label: Verse I.16.65
units.deva: शास्त्रयुक्तिविरोधात् ता नादर्तव्याः कदाचन । शक्यन्ते शतशो वक्तुं दोषास् तासां सहस्रशः
units.iast: śāstrayuktivirodhāt tā nādartavyāḥ kadācana । śakyante śataśo vaktuṃ doṣās tāsāṃ sahasraśaḥ
units.translation: “Because they conflict with scripture and reasoning, those views should never be accepted; hundreds and thousands of their faults can be stated.”

units.label: Verse I.16.66
units.deva: अपि निन्दोपपत्तेश् च यान्य् अतो ऽन्यानि चेत्य् अतः । त्यक्त्वातो ह्य् अन्यशास्त्रोक्तीर् मतिं कुर्याद् दृढां बुधः
units.iast: api nindopapatteś ca yāny ato 'nyāni cety ataḥ । tyaktvāto hy anyaśāstroktīr matiṃ kuryād dṛḍhāṃ budhaḥ
