units.deva: आचार्यो ब्रूयद् -- इहैव ते सोम्य मृतस्य शरीरं वयोभिर् अद्यते मृद्भावं वापद्यते, तत्र कथं संसारसागराद् उत्तर्तुम् इच्छसीति । नहि नद्या अवरे कूले भस्मीभूतो नद्याः पारं तरिष्यसीति
units.iast: ācāryo brūyad -- ihaiva te somya mṛtasya śarīraṃ vayobhir adyate mṛdbhāvaṃ vāpadyate, tatra kathaṃ saṃsārasāgarād uttartum icchasīti । nahi nadyā avare kūle bhasmībhūto nadyāḥ pāraṃ tariṣyasīti
units.translation: The teacher says: “Dear one, even here your dead body will be eaten by birds or turn to dust. How do you hope to cross the ocean of worldly life? One whose body has been burned on this bank of a river cannot cross to the other bank.”

units.label: Prose II.1.12
units.deva: स यदि ब्रूयात् -- अन्यो ऽहं शरीरात् । शरीरं तु जायते म्रियते, वयोभिर् अद्यते मृद्भावम् आपद्यते, शस्त्राग्न्यादिभिश् च विनाश्यते, व्याध्यादिभिश् च युज्यते । तस्मिन्न् अहं स्वकृतधर्माधर्मवशात् पक्षी नीडम् इव प्रविष्टः पुनः पुनः शरीरविनाशे धर्माधर्मवशाच् छरीरान्तरं यास्यामि, पूर्वनीडविनाशे पक्षीव नीडान्तरम् । एवम् एवाहम् अनादौ संसारे देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्यनिरयस्थानेषु स्वकर्मवशाद् उपात्तम् उपात्तं शरीरं त्यजन्, नवं नवं चान्यद् उपाददानो, जन्ममरणप्रबन्धचक्रे घटीयन्त्रवत् स्वकर्मणा भ्राम्यमाणः क्रमेणेदं शरीरम् आसाद्य संसारचक्रभ्रमणाद् अस्मान् निर्विण्णो भगवन्तम् उपसन्नो ऽस्मि संसारचक्रभ्रमणप्रशमायेति । तस्मान् नित्य एवाहं शरीराद् अन्यः । शरीराण्य् आगच्छन्त्य् अपगच्छन्ति च वासांषीव पुरुषस्येति
units.iast: sa yadi brūyāt -- anyo 'haṃ śarīrāt । śarīraṃ tu jāyate mriyate, vayobhir adyate mṛdbhāvam āpadyate, śastrāgnyādibhiś ca vināśyate, vyādhyādibhiś ca yujyate । tasminn ahaṃ svakṛtadharmādharmavaśāt pakṣī nīḍam iva praviṣṭaḥ punaḥ punaḥ śarīravināśe dharmādharmavaśāc charīrāntaraṃ yāsyāmi, pūrvanīḍavināśe pakṣīva nīḍāntaram । evam evāham anādau saṃsāre devatiryaṅmanuṣyanirayasthāneṣu svakarmavaśād upāttam upāttaṃ śarīraṃ tyajan, navaṃ navaṃ cānyad upādadāno, janmamaraṇaprabandhacakre ghaṭīyantravat svakarmaṇā bhrāmyamāṇaḥ krameṇedaṃ śarīram āsādya saṃsāracakrabhramaṇād asmān nirviṇṇo bhagavantam upasanno 'smi saṃsāracakrabhramaṇapraśamāyeti । tasmān nitya evāhaṃ śarīrād anyaḥ । śarīrāṇy āgacchanty apagacchanti ca vāsāṃṣīva puruṣasyeti
units.translation: The student says: “I am other than the body. The body is born and dies, is eaten by birds, turns to dust, is destroyed by weapons and fire, and is subject to disease. I have entered it like a bird entering a nest, through my own merit and demerit. When this body is destroyed, I will go to another body through merit and demerit, as a bird goes to another nest when its old one is destroyed. Thus, in beginningless worldly existence, I have repeatedly taken and left bodies among gods, animals, humans and hell-dwellers according to my actions, taking up one new body after another and being driven by my actions through the wheel of birth and death like a waterwheel. Wearied by this cycle, I have approached the revered teacher to end its turning. I am therefore eternal and other than the body, which comes and goes like clothes on a person.”

units.label: Prose II.1.13
units.deva: आचार्यो ब्रूयत् -- साध्व् अवादिः सम्यक् पश्यसि । कथं मृषावादीर् ब्राह्मणपुत्रो ऽदोन्वयो ब्रह्मचार्य् आसम्, गृहस्थो वा, इदानीम् अस्मि परमहंसपरिव्राड् इति
units.iast: ācāryo brūyat -- sādhv avādiḥ samyak paśyasi । kathaṃ mṛṣāvādīr brāhmaṇaputro 'donvayo brahmacāry āsam, gṛhastho vā, idānīm asmi paramahaṃsaparivrāḍ iti
units.translation: The teacher says: “Well said; you see correctly. But how then were you mistaken when you said, ‘I am the son of a Brahmin of such-and-such family; I was a student, then a householder, and now I am a supreme wandering renunciant’?”

units.label: Prose II.1.14
units.deva: स यदि ब्रूयात् -- भगवन्, कथम् अहं मृषावादिषम् इति
units.iast: sa yadi brūyāt -- bhagavan, katham ahaṃ mṛṣāvādiṣam iti
units.translation: The student asks: “Revered one, how was I mistaken?”

units.label: Prose II.1.15
units.deva: तं प्रति ब्रूयाद् आचार्यः -- यतस् त्वं भिन्नजात्यन्वयसंस्कारं शरीरं जात्यन्वयसंस्कारवर्जितस्यात्मनः प्रत्यज्ञासीर् ब्राह्मणपुत्रो ऽदोन्वय इत्यादिना वाक्येनेति
units.iast: taṃ prati brūyād ācāryaḥ -- yatas tvaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīraṃ jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjitasyātmanaḥ pratyajñāsīr brāhmaṇaputro 'donvaya ityādinā vākyeneti
units.translation: The teacher replies: “You identified the body, which has a particular birth, family and conditioning, with the Self, which is free from birth, family and conditioning, by saying ‘I am the son of a Brahmin of such-and-such family’ and the like.”

units.label: Prose II.1.16
units.deva: स यदि पृच्छेत् -- कथं भिन्नजात्यन्वयसंस्कारं शरीरम्, कथं वाहं जात्यन्वयसंस्कारवर्जित इति
units.iast: sa yadi pṛcchet -- kathaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīram, kathaṃ vāhaṃ jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita iti
units.translation: The student asks: “How is the body marked by birth, family and conditioning different from me? How am I free from those marks?”

units.label: Prose II.1.17
units.deva: आचार्यो ब्रूयत् -- शृणु सोम्य यथेदं शरीरं त्वत्तो भिन्नं भिन्नजात्यन्वयसंस्कारं त्वं च जात्यन्वयसंस्कारवर्जित इत्य् उक्त्वा तं स्मारयेत् -- स्मर्तुम् अर्हसि सोम्य, परमात्मानं सर्वात्मानं यथोक्तलक्षणं श्रावितो ऽसि "सद् एव सोम्येदम्" इत्यादि[भिः] श्रुतिभिः स्मृतिभिश् च । लक्षणं च तस्य श्रुतिभिः स्मृतिभिश् च
units.iast: ācāryo brūyat -- śṛṇu somya yathedaṃ śarīraṃ tvatto bhinnaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ tvaṃ ca jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita ity uktvā taṃ smārayet -- smartum arhasi somya, paramātmānaṃ sarvātmānaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ śrāvito 'si "sad eva somyedam" ityādi[bhiḥ] śrutibhiḥ smṛtibhiś ca । lakṣaṇaṃ ca tasya śrutibhiḥ smṛtibhiś ca
units.translation: The teacher says: “Listen, dear one. I have told you that this body is different from you: it bears birth, family and conditioning, while you are free of them. You should remember the Supreme Self, the Self of all, whose nature has been explained to you through scripture beginning ‘Being alone was this in the beginning.’ Its nature is taught by scripture and tradition.”

units.label: Prose II.1.18
units.deva: लब्धपरमात्मलक्षणस्मृतये ब्रूयात् -- यो ऽसाव् आकाशनामा नामरूपाभ्याम् अर्थान्तरभूतो ऽशरीरो ऽस्थूलादिलक्षणो ऽपहतपाप्मत्वादिलक्षणश् च सर्वैः संसारधर्मैर् अनागन्धितः "यत् साक्षाद् अपरोक्षाद् ब्रह्म ... एष त आत्मा सर्वान्तरः", "अदृष्टो द्रष्टा, अश्रुतः श्रोता, अमतो मन्ता, अविज्ञातो विज्ञात" नित्यविज्ञानस्वरूपो ऽनन्तरो ऽबाह्यः, "विज्ञानघन एव", परिपूर्ण आकाशवत्, अनन्तशक्तिः, आत्मा सर्वस्य, अशनायादिवर्जितः, आविर्भावतिरोभाववर्जितश् च स्वात्मविलक्षणयोर् नामरूपयोर् जगद्बीजभूतयोः स्वात्मस्थयोः तत्त्वान्यत्वाभ्याम् अनिर्वचनीययोः स्वसंवेद्ययोः सद्भावमात्रेणाचिन्त्यशक्तित्वाद् व्याकर्ताव्याकृतयोः
units.iast: labdhaparamātmalakṣaṇasmṛtaye brūyāt -- yo 'sāv ākāśanāmā nāmarūpābhyām arthāntarabhūto 'śarīro 'sthūlādilakṣaṇo 'pahatapāpmatvādilakṣaṇaś ca sarvaiḥ saṃsāradharmair anāgandhitaḥ "yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ... eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ", "adṛṣṭo draṣṭā, aśrutaḥ śrotā, amato mantā, avijñāto vijñāta" nityavijñānasvarūpo 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ, "vijñānaghana eva", paripūrṇa ākāśavat, anantaśaktiḥ, ātmā sarvasya, aśanāyādivarjitaḥ, āvirbhāvatirobhāvavarjitaś ca svātmavilakṣaṇayor nāmarūpayor jagadbījabhūtayoḥ svātmasthayoḥ tattvānyatvābhyām anirvacanīyayoḥ svasaṃvedyayoḥ sadbhāvamātreṇācintyaśaktitvād vyākartāvyākṛtayoḥ
units.translation: To help him remember the nature of the Supreme Self, the teacher says: “That which is called space, other than objects by name and form, bodiless, neither gross nor subtle, free from evil and every other mark, untouched by all the conditions of worldly life, is immediate and direct Brahman, ‘this Self of yours, the innermost Self of all.’ It is the unseen Seer, the unheard Hearer, the unthought Thinker and the unknown Knower; its nature is eternal awareness, without inner or outer, a mass of awareness alone, complete like space, of infinite power, the Self of all, free from hunger and the rest, and free from arising and disappearing. The names and forms that are distinct from it are the seed of the world, abiding in the Self, neither identical with it nor other than it, indescribable, known only through themselves, and manifest or unmanifest by an inconceivable power.”

units.label: Prose II.1.19
units.deva: ते नामरूपे ऽव्याकृते सती व्याक्रियमाणे तस्माद् एतस्माद् आत्मन आकाशनामाकृती संवृत्ते । तच् चाकाशख्यं भूतम् अनेन प्रकारेण परमात्मनः सम्भूतं प्रसन्नात् सलिलान् मलम् इव फेनम् । न सलिलं न च सलिलाद् अत्यन्तभिन्नं फेनम् । सलिलव्यतिरेकेणादर्शनात् । सलिलं तु स्वच्छम् अन्यत् फेनान् मलरूपात् । एवं परमात्मा नामरूपाभ्याम् अन्यः फेनस्थानीयाभ्यां शुद्धः प्रसन्नस् तद्विलक्षणः । ते नामरूपे ऽव्याकृते सती व्याक्रियमाणे फेनस्थानीये आकाशनामाकृती संवृत्ते
units.iast: te nāmarūpe 'vyākṛte satī vyākriyamāṇe tasmād etasmād ātmana ākāśanāmākṛtī saṃvṛtte । tac cākāśakhyaṃ bhūtam anena prakāreṇa paramātmanaḥ sambhūtaṃ prasannāt salilān malam iva phenam । na salilaṃ na ca salilād atyantabhinnaṃ phenam । salilavyatirekeṇādarśanāt । salilaṃ tu svaccham anyat phenān malarūpāt । evaṃ paramātmā nāmarūpābhyām anyaḥ phenasthānīyābhyāṃ śuddhaḥ prasannas tadvilakṣaṇaḥ । te nāmarūpe 'vyākṛte satī vyākriyamāṇe phenasthānīye ākāśanāmākṛtī saṃvṛtte
units.translation: “Those names and forms, while unmanifest, become manifest; from this very Self they take on the name and form of space. This element called space thus arises from the Supreme Self, like foam from clear water. Foam is not water, yet it is not completely different from water, since it cannot be seen apart from it. Water itself is clear and distinct from foam, which is like a stain. In the same way the Supreme Self is distinct from names and forms, which are like foam; it is pure and clear, unlike them. The unmanifest names and forms, when manifest, become space in name and appearance, like foam.”

units.label: Prose II.1.20
units.deva: ततो ऽपि स्थूलभावम् आपद्यमाने नामरूपे व्याक्रियमाणे वायुभावम् आपद्येते, ततो ऽप्य् अग्निभावम्, अग्नेर् अभावम्, ततः पृथ्वीभावम् इत्य् एवंक्रमेण पूर्वपूर्वो[त्तरो]त्तरानुप्रवेशेन पञ्चमहाभूतानि पृथिव्यन्तान्य् उत्पन्नानि । ततः पञ्चमहाभूतगुणविशिष्टा पृथ्[इ]वी । पृथ्[इ]व्याश् च पञ्चात्मक्यो व्रीहियवाद्या ओषधयो जायन्ते । ताभ्यो भक्षिताभ्यो लोहितं शुक्रं च स्त्रीपुंसशरीरसंबन्धि जायते । तद् उभयम् ऋतुकाले ऽविद्याप्रयुक्तकामखजनिर्मथनोद्भूतं मन्त्रसंस्कृतं गर्भाशये निषिच्यते । तत् स्वयोनिरसानुप्रवेशेन विवर्धमानं गर्भीभूतं दशमे नवमे वा मासि सञ्जायते
units.iast: tato 'pi sthūlabhāvam āpadyamāne nāmarūpe vyākriyamāṇe vāyubhāvam āpadyete, tato 'py agnibhāvam, agner abhāvam, tataḥ pṛthvībhāvam ity evaṃkrameṇa pūrvapūrvo[ttaro]ttarānupraveśena pañcamahābhūtāni pṛthivyantāny utpannāni । tataḥ pañcamahābhūtaguṇaviśiṣṭā pṛth[i]vī । pṛth[i]vyāś ca pañcātmakyo vrīhiyavādyā oṣadhayo jāyante । tābhyo bhakṣitābhyo lohitaṃ śukraṃ ca strīpuṃsaśarīrasaṃbandhi jāyate । tad ubhayam ṛtukāle 'vidyāprayuktakāmakhajanirmathanodbhūtaṃ mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ garbhāśaye niṣicyate । tat svayonirasānupraveśena vivardhamānaṃ garbhībhūtaṃ daśame navame vā māsi sañjāyate
units.translation: “As these names and forms become gross, they manifest successively as air, then fire, then water, and then earth; in this order, each later element enters into the earlier ones. Thus the five great elements arise, ending with earth. Earth, with the qualities of all five elements, gives rise to plants such as rice and barley. From the food they eat, male and female bodies produce blood and semen. At the proper time, driven by ignorance and desire and consecrated by ritual, these are joined and placed in the womb. Entering its source, growing and becoming an embryo, it is born in the ninth or tenth month.”

units.label: Prose II.1.21
units.deva: तज् जातं लब्धनामाकृतिकं जातकर्मादिभिर् मन्त्रसंस्कृतं पुनर् उपनयनसंस्कारयोगेन ब्रह्मचारिसंज्ञं भवति । तद् एव शरीरं पत्नीसंयोगसंस्कारयोगेन गृहस्थसंज्ञं भवति । तद् एव वनस्थसंस्कारेण तापससंज्ञं भवति । तद् एव क्रियाविनिवृत्तिनिमित्तसंस्कारेण परिव्राट्संज्ञं भवति । इत्य् एवं त्वत्तो भिन्नं भिन्नजात्यन्वयसंस्कारं शरीरम्
units.iast: taj jātaṃ labdhanāmākṛtikaṃ jātakarmādibhir mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ punar upanayanasaṃskārayogena brahmacārisaṃjñaṃ bhavati । tad eva śarīraṃ patnīsaṃyogasaṃskārayogena gṛhasthasaṃjñaṃ bhavati । tad eva vanasthasaṃskāreṇa tāpasasaṃjñaṃ bhavati । tad eva kriyāvinivṛttinimittasaṃskāreṇa parivrāṭsaṃjñaṃ bhavati । ity evaṃ tvatto bhinnaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāraṃ śarīram
units.translation: “Once born, given a name and form, and consecrated by rites such as the birth ceremony, that same body becomes known as a student through the initiation rite; through marriage it becomes known as a householder; through the forest-dweller’s rite it becomes an ascetic; and through the rites marking withdrawal from action it becomes a wandering renunciant. This body, bearing birth, family and conditioning, is different from you.”

units.label: Prose II.1.22
units.deva: मनश् चेन्द्रियाणि च नामरूपात्मकान्य् एव "अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः" इत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः
units.iast: manaś cendriyāṇi ca nāmarūpātmakāny eva "annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ" ityādiśrutibhyaḥ
units.translation: “The mind and the senses, too, are made of name and form, as scripture says, ‘The mind, dear one, is made of food,’ and the like.”

units.label: Prose II.1.23
units.deva: कथं चाहं भिन्नजात्यन्वयसंस्कारवर्जित इत्य् एतच् छृणु । यो ऽसौ नामरूपयोर् व्याकर्ता नामरूपधर्मविलक्षणः स एव नामरूपे व्याकुर्वन् सृष्ट्वेदं शरीरं स्वयं संस्कारधर्मवर्जितो नामरूप इह प्रविष्टो ऽन्यैर् अदृष्टः स्वयं पश्यंस् तथाश्रुतः शृण्वन्न् अमतो मन्वानो ऽविज्ञातो विजानन् -- "सर्वाणि रूपाणि विचित्य धीरो नामानि कृत्वाभिवदन् यद् आस्ते" इति । अस्मिन्न् अर्थे श्रुतयः सहस्रशः "तत् सृष्ट्वा तद् एवानुप्राविषत्". "अन्तः प्रविष्टः शास्ता जनानाम्", "स एष इह प्रविष्टः", "एष त आत्मा", "स एतम् एव सीमानं विदार्यैतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत", "एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढो ऽत्मा", "सेयं देवतैक्षत हन्ताहम् इमास् तिस्रो देवताः", "अशरीरं शरीरेषु" इत्याद्याः
units.iast: kathaṃ cāhaṃ bhinnajātyanvayasaṃskāravarjita ity etac chṛṇu । yo 'sau nāmarūpayor vyākartā nāmarūpadharmavilakṣaṇaḥ sa eva nāmarūpe vyākurvan sṛṣṭvedaṃ śarīraṃ svayaṃ saṃskāradharmavarjito nāmarūpa iha praviṣṭo 'nyair adṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ paśyaṃs tathāśrutaḥ śṛṇvann amato manvāno 'vijñāto vijānan -- "sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadan yad āste" iti । asminn arthe śrutayaḥ sahasraśaḥ "tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviṣat". "antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānām", "sa eṣa iha praviṣṭaḥ", "eṣa ta ātmā", "sa etam eva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata", "eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā", "seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāham imās tisro devatāḥ", "aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu" ityādyāḥ
units.translation: “Now listen to how you are free from birth, family and conditioning. That which manifests names and forms, distinct from their properties, creates them and this body, yet remains free of their conditions; it enters here without name or form. It is unseen by others, yet itself sees; unheard, yet itself hears; unthought, yet itself thinks; unknown, yet itself knows. As scripture says, ‘The wise one, forming all shapes and giving them names, sits calling them forth.’ There are thousands of passages on this: ‘Having created it, he entered into it’; ‘the ruler who entered within’; ‘he entered here’; ‘this is your Self’; ‘having split open the crown of the head, he entered by this door’; ‘the Self is hidden in all beings’; ‘the deity thought, “Let me enter these three deities”’; ‘bodiless among bodies’; and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.24
units.deva: स्मृतयो ऽपि "आत्मैव देवताः सर्वाः", "नवद्वारे पुरे देही", "क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि", "समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु", "उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च", "उत्तमः पुरुषस् त्व् अन्यः" इत्याद्याः । तस्माज् जात्यन्वयसंस्कारवर्जितस् त्वम् इति सिद्धम्
units.iast: smṛtayo 'pi "ātmaiva devatāḥ sarvāḥ", "navadvāre pure dehī", "kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi", "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu", "upadraṣṭānumantā ca", "uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ" ityādyāḥ । tasmāj jātyanvayasaṃskāravarjitas tvam iti siddham
units.translation: “Tradition likewise says: ‘All the gods are the Self’; ‘the embodied one in the city of nine gates’; ‘know me too as the knower of the field’; ‘equal in all beings’; ‘in one who has knowledge and humility’; ‘undivided among the divided’; ‘Vāsudeva is all’; and the rest. Thus you are established as the one Self, Supreme Brahman, free from every condition of worldly existence.”

units.label: Prose II.1.25
units.deva: स यदि ब्रूयात् -- अन्य एवाहम् अज्ञः सुखी दुःखी बद्धः संसारी, अन्यो ऽसौ मद्विलक्षणो ऽसंसारी देवः, तम् अहं बल्युपहारनमस्कारादिभिर् वर्णाश्रमकर्मभिश् चाराध्य संसारसागराद् उत्तितीर्षुर् अस्मि, कथम् अहं स एवेति
units.iast: sa yadi brūyāt -- anya evāham ajñaḥ sukhī duḥkhī baddhaḥ saṃsārī, anyo 'sau madvilakṣaṇo 'saṃsārī devaḥ, tam ahaṃ balyupahāranamaskārādibhir varṇāśramakarmabhiś cārādhya saṃsārasāgarād uttitīrṣur asmi, katham ahaṃ sa eveti
units.translation: The student says: “I am one person, ignorant, happy or unhappy, bound and in worldly existence; that God is another, different from me and free from it. I will worship him with offerings, reverence and rites appropriate to my caste and stage of life, and thereby cross the ocean of worldly existence. How can I be that very Self?”

units.label: Prose II.1.26
units.deva: आचार्यो ब्रूयत् -- नैवं सोम्य प्रतिपत्तुम् अर्हसि, प्रतिषिद्धत्वाद् भेदप्रतिपत्तेः । कथं प्रतिषिद्धा भेदप्रतिपत्तिर् इत्य् अत आह -- "अन्यो ऽसाव् अन्यो ऽहम् अस्मीति न स वेद", "ब्रह्म तं परादाद् यो ऽन्यत्रात्मनो ब्रह्म वेद", मृत्योः स मृत्युम् आप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति" इत्येवमाद्याः
units.iast: ācāryo brūyat -- naivaṃ somya pratipattum arhasi, pratiṣiddhatvād bhedapratipatteḥ । kathaṃ pratiṣiddhā bhedapratipattir ity ata āha -- "anyo 'sāv anyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda", "brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano brahma veda", mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati" ityevamādyāḥ
units.translation: The teacher says: “Dear one, you must not understand it in that way, for scripture forbids the understanding of difference.” How is it forbidden? The teacher cites: “‘He does not know, thinking, “He is one and I am another”’; ‘Brahman rejects the one who knows Brahman as other than the Self’; ‘whoever sees here as though there were multiplicity goes from death to death’; and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.27
units.deva: एता एव श्रुतयो भेदप्रतिपत्तेः संसारगमनं दर्शयन्ति
units.iast: etā eva śrutayo bhedapratipatteḥ saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti
units.translation: These same passages show that seeing difference leads into worldly existence.

units.label: Prose II.1.28
units.deva: अभेदप्रतिपत्तेश् च मोक्षं दर्शयन्ति सहस्रशः -- "स आत्मा तत् त्वम् असि" इति परमात्मभावं विधाय "आचार्यवान् पुरुषो वेद" इत्य् उक्त्वा "तस्य तावद् एव चिरम्" इति मोक्षं दर्शयन्त्य् अभेदविज्ञानाद् एव सत्यसन्धस्यातस्करस्येव दाहाद्यभावदृष्टान्तेन संसाराभावं दर्शयन्ति, भेददर्शनाद् असत्याभिसन्धस्य संसारगमनं दर्शयन्ति तस्करस्येव दाहादिदृष्टान्तेन
units.iast: abhedapratipatteś ca mokṣaṃ darśayanti sahasraśaḥ -- "sa ātmā tat tvam asi" iti paramātmabhāvaṃ vidhāya "ācāryavān puruṣo veda" ity uktvā "tasya tāvad eva ciram" iti mokṣaṃ darśayanty abhedavijñānād eva satyasandhasyātaskarasyeva dāhādyabhāvadṛṣṭāntena saṃsārābhāvaṃ darśayanti, bhedadarśanād asatyābhisandhasya saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti taskarasyeva dāhādidṛṣṭāntena
units.translation: Thousands of passages show that knowing non-difference leads to liberation: scripture establishes identity with the Supreme Self through ‘That is the Self; you are that,’ then says ‘a person with a teacher knows’ and ‘for him there is delay only until the body falls.’ Through the example of a truthful person who does not suffer burning, it shows worldly existence ends through knowledge of non-difference; through the example of a thief who lies and suffers burning, it shows that false adherence to difference leads to worldly existence.

units.label: Prose II.1.29
units.deva: "त इह व्याघ्रो वा" इत्यादिना चाभेददर्शनात् "[स] सर्वाड् भवति" इत्य् उक्त्वा तद्विपरीतेन भेददर्शनेन संसारगमनं दर्शयन्ति -- "अथ ये ऽन्यथातो विदुर् अन्यराजानस् ते क्षय्यलोका भवन्ति" इति प्रतिशाखम् । तस्मान् मृषैवावादीः -- ब्राह्मणपुत्रो ऽदोन्वयः संसारी परमात्मविलक्षण इति
units.iast: "ta iha vyāghro vā" ityādinā cābhedadarśanāt "[sa] sarvāḍ bhavati" ity uktvā tadviparītena bhedadarśanena saṃsāragamanaṃ darśayanti -- "atha ye 'nyathāto vidur anyarājānas te kṣayyalokā bhavanti" iti pratiśākham । tasmān mṛṣaivāvādīḥ -- brāhmaṇaputro 'donvayaḥ saṃsārī paramātmavilakṣaṇa iti
units.translation: Likewise, the passage beginning ‘here they become a tiger’ says that through seeing non-difference ‘one becomes all’; by contrast, it says in each branch that those who understand otherwise and see another as their ruler have worlds that perish. Therefore you were mistaken to say, ‘I am a son of a Brahmin of such-and-such family, a person in worldly existence, different from the Supreme Self.’”

units.label: Prose II.1.30
units.deva: तस्मात् प्रतिषिद्धत्वाद् भेददर्शनस्य, भेदविषयत्वाच् च कर्मोपादानस्य, कर्मसाधनत्वाच् च यज्ञोपवीतादेः कर्मसाधनोपादानस्य परमात्माभेदप्रतिपत्त्या प्रतिषेधः कृतो वेदितव्यः । कर्मणां तत्साधनानां च यज्ञोपवीतादीनां परमात्माभेदप्रतिपत्तिविरुद्धत्वात् । संसारिणो हि कर्माणि विधीयन्ते तत्साधनानि च यज्ञोपवीतादीनि, न परमात्मनो ऽभेददर्शिनः । भेददर्शनमात्रेण च ततो ऽन्यत्वम्
units.iast: tasmāt pratiṣiddhatvād bhedadarśanasya, bhedaviṣayatvāc ca karmopādānasya, karmasādhanatvāc ca yajñopavītādeḥ karmasādhanopādānasya paramātmābhedapratipattyā pratiṣedhaḥ kṛto veditavyaḥ । karmaṇāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ ca yajñopavītādīnāṃ paramātmābhedapratipattiviruddhatvāt । saṃsāriṇo hi karmāṇi vidhīyante tatsādhanāni ca yajñopavītādīni, na paramātmano 'bhedadarśinaḥ । bhedadarśanamātreṇa ca tato 'nyatvam
units.translation: “Since scripture forbids the vision of difference, since taking up action is based on seeing difference, and since the sacred thread and the rest are means to action, one must understand that knowledge of identity with the Supreme Self rejects them. Actions and their means, such as the sacred thread, belong to one who lives in worldly existence, not to the one who sees identity with the Supreme Self. Seeing difference alone makes one other than it.”

units.label: Prose II.1.31
units.deva: यदि च कर्माणि कर्तव्यानि न निवर्तयिषितानि कर्मसाधनासम्बन्धिनः कर्मनिमित्तजात्याश्रमाद्यसम्बन्धिनश् च परमात्मन आत्मनैवाभेदप्रतिपत्तिं नावक्ष्यत् "स आत्मा तत् त्वम् असि" इत्येवमादिभिर् निश्चितरूपैर् वाक्यैः, भेदप्रतिपत्तिनिन्दां च नाभ्यधास्यत् "एष नित्यो महिमा ब्राह्मणस्य", "अनन्वागतं पुण्येनानन्वागतं पापेन", "अत्र स्तेनो ऽस्तेनः" इत्यादिना
units.iast: yadi ca karmāṇi kartavyāni na nivartayiṣitāni karmasādhanāsambandhinaḥ karmanimittajātyāśramādyasambandhinaś ca paramātmana ātmanaivābhedapratipattiṃ nāvakṣyat "sa ātmā tat tvam asi" ityevamādibhir niścitarūpair vākyaiḥ, bhedapratipattinindāṃ ca nābhyadhāsyat "eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya", "ananvāgataṃ puṇyenānanvāgataṃ pāpena", "atra steno 'stenaḥ" ityādinā
units.translation: “If actions had to be performed and were not to be given up, scripture would not teach that the Supreme Self is identical with you through decisive sentences such as ‘That is the Self; you are that,’ nor condemn seeing difference through ‘This is the eternal glory of a Brahmin,’ ‘merit does not follow him, nor does sin,’ and ‘here the thief is no thief,’ and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.32
units.deva: कर्मासम्बन्धरूपत्वं कर्मनिमित्तवर्णाद्यसम्बन्धरूपतां [च] नाभ्यधास्यत्, कर्माणि [च] कर्मसाधनानि [च] यज्ञोपवीतादीनि यद्य् अपरितित्याजयिषितानि । तस्मात् ससाधनं कर्म परित्यक्तव्यं मुमुक्षुणा परमात्माभेददर्शनविरोधात् । आत्मा च पर एवेति प्रतिपत्तव्यो यथाश्रुत्युक्तलक्षणः
units.iast: karmāsambandharūpatvaṃ karmanimittavarṇādyasambandharūpatāṃ [ca] nābhyadhāsyat, karmāṇi [ca] karmasādhanāni [ca] yajñopavītādīni yady aparitityājayiṣitāni । tasmāt sasādhanaṃ karma parityaktavyaṃ mumukṣuṇā paramātmābhedadarśanavirodhāt । ātmā ca para eveti pratipattavyo yathāśrutyuktalakṣaṇaḥ
units.translation: “If one were not meant to relinquish action and its means, such as the sacred thread, scripture would not declare freedom from action and from caste, which is a condition for action. Therefore the seeker of liberation should give up action together with its means, since it conflicts with seeing identity with the Supreme Self. One should understand the Self to be the Supreme Self, with the nature described by scripture.”

units.label: Prose II.1.33
units.deva: स यदि ब्रूयात् -- भगवन्, दह्यमाने छिद्यमाने वा देहे प्रत्यक्षा वेदना, अशनायादिनिमित्तं च प्रत्यक्षं दुःखं मम । परश् चात्मा "अपहतपाप्मा विजरो विमृत्युर् विशोको विजिघत्सो ऽपिपासः" सर्वसंसारधर्मविवर्जितः श्रूयते सर्वश्रुतिषु स्मृतिषु च । कथं तद्विलक्षणो ऽनेकसंसारधर्मसंयुक्तः परमात्मानम् आत्मत्वेन मां च संसारिणं परमात्मत्वेनाग्निम् इव शीतत्वेन प्रतिपद्येयम् । संसारी च सन् सर्वाभ्युदयनिःश्रेयससाधने ऽधिकृतो ऽभ्युदयनिःश्रेयससाधनानि कर्माणि तत्साधनानि च यज्ञोपवीतादीनि कथं परित्यजेयम् इति
units.iast: sa yadi brūyāt -- bhagavan, dahyamāne chidyamāne vā dehe pratyakṣā vedanā, aśanāyādinimittaṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ duḥkhaṃ mama । paraś cātmā "apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ" sarvasaṃsāradharmavivarjitaḥ śrūyate sarvaśrutiṣu smṛtiṣu ca । kathaṃ tadvilakṣaṇo 'nekasaṃsāradharmasaṃyuktaḥ paramātmānam ātmatvena māṃ ca saṃsāriṇaṃ paramātmatvenāgnim iva śītatvena pratipadyeyam । saṃsārī ca san sarvābhyudayaniḥśreyasasādhane 'dhikṛto 'bhyudayaniḥśreyasasādhanāni karmāṇi tatsādhanāni ca yajñopavītādīni kathaṃ parityajeyam iti
units.translation: The student says: “Revered one, when my body is burned or cut, I directly feel pain; I directly experience suffering from hunger and the rest. Yet scripture and tradition describe the Supreme Self as ‘free from evil, ageless, deathless, sorrowless, without hunger or thirst,’ free from every condition of worldly existence. How can I, who experience many such conditions and am different from that Self, understand the Supreme Self as myself and myself as the Supreme Self—as though fire were cold? While I am a person in worldly existence, entitled to actions that bring prosperity and the highest good, how can I abandon actions and their means, such as the sacred thread?”

units.label: Prose II.1.34
units.deva: तं प्रति ब्रूयात् -- यद् अवोचो दह्यमाने छिद्यमाने वा देहे प्रत्यक्षा वेदनोपलभ्यते ममेति तद् असत् । कस्मत् । दह्यमाने छिद्यमान इव व्र्क्ष उपलब्धुर् उपलभ्यमाने कर्मणि शरीरे दाहच्छेदवेदनाया उपलभ्यमानत्वाद् दाहादिसमानाश्रयैव वेदना । यत्र हि दाहश् छेदो वा क्रियते तत्रैव व्यपदिशति दाहादिवेदनां लोको न दाहाद्युपलब्धरीति । कथम् । क्व ते वेदनेति पृष्टः शिरसि मे वेदनोरस्य् उदर इति यत्र दाहादिस् तत्र व्यपदिशति, नोपलब्धरीति । यद्य् उपलब्धरि वेदना स्याद् वेदनानिमित्तं वा दाहच्छेदादि, वेदनाश्रयत्वेनोपदिशेद् दाहाद्याश्रयावत्
units.iast: taṃ prati brūyāt -- yad avoco dahyamāne chidyamāne vā dehe pratyakṣā vedanopalabhyate mameti tad asat । kasmat । dahyamāne chidyamāna iva vrkṣa upalabdhur upalabhyamāne karmaṇi śarīre dāhacchedavedanāyā upalabhyamānatvād dāhādisamānāśrayaiva vedanā । yatra hi dāhaś chedo vā kriyate tatraiva vyapadiśati dāhādivedanāṃ loko na dāhādyupalabdharīti । katham । kva te vedaneti pṛṣṭaḥ śirasi me vedanorasy udara iti yatra dāhādis tatra vyapadiśati, nopalabdharīti । yady upalabdhari vedanā syād vedanānimittaṃ vā dāhacchedādi, vedanāśrayatvenopadiśed dāhādyāśrayāvat
units.translation: The teacher replies: “What you said—that when the body is burned or cut you directly experience pain as your own—is false. Why? When a body is burned or cut, the one who observes it also observes the pain as belonging to the body, just as with an action performed on another object. The pain of burning and cutting is located where the burning and cutting occur. People speak of pain where the injury occurs, not in the one who observes it. If asked ‘Where is your pain?’ one says ‘in my head, chest or stomach’—where the injury is—not in the observer. If pain belonged to the observer, or burning and cutting caused pain in the observer, one would speak of the observer as the seat of the pain, just as one speaks of the body as the seat of burning and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.35
units.deva: स्वयं च नोपलभ्येत चक्षुर्गतरूपवत् । तस्माद् दाहच्छेदादिसमानाश्रयत्वेनोपलभ्यमानत्वाद् दाहादिवत् कर्मभूतैव वेदना । भावरूपत्वाच् च साश्रया तण्डुलपाकवत् । वेदनासमानाश्रय एव तत्संस्कारः । स्मृतिसमानकाल एवोपलभ्यमानत्वात् । वेदनाविषयस् तन्निमित्तविषयश् च द्वेषो ऽपि संस्कारसमानाश्रय एव । तथा चोक्तम् -- "रूपसंस्कारतुल्याधी रागद्वेषौ भयं च यत् । गृह्यते धीश्रयं तस्माज् ज्ञाता शुद्धो ऽभयः सदा"
units.iast: svayaṃ ca nopalabhyeta cakṣurgatarūpavat । tasmād dāhacchedādisamānāśrayatvenopalabhyamānatvād dāhādivat karmabhūtaiva vedanā । bhāvarūpatvāc ca sāśrayā taṇḍulapākavat । vedanāsamānāśraya eva tatsaṃskāraḥ । smṛtisamānakāla evopalabhyamānatvāt । vedanāviṣayas tannimittaviṣayaś ca dveṣo 'pi saṃskārasamānāśraya eva । tathā coktam -- "rūpasaṃskāratulyādhī rāgadveṣau bhayaṃ ca yat । gṛhyate dhīśrayaṃ tasmāj jñātā śuddho 'bhayaḥ sadā"
units.translation: “The observer does not perceive pain in itself, as the eye does not see its own form. Because pain is observed in the same place as burning, cutting and the rest, pain is an object of experience, like the action of burning. Being a condition, it must have a basis, like rice being cooked. Its impression remains in the same basis as the pain, since it is perceived at the same time as memory. Aversion toward pain and toward its causes likewise rests on that basis of impressions. As has been said: ‘Color, impressions, attachment, aversion and fear are grasped as belonging to the intellect; therefore the knower is always pure and fearless.’”

units.label: Prose II.1.36
units.deva: किमाश्रयः पुना रूपादिसंस्कारादय इति । उच्यते । यत्र कामादायः । क्व पुनस् ते कामादयः । "कामः सङ्कल्पो विचिकित्सा" इत्यादिश्रुतेर् बुद्धाव् एव । तत्रैव रूपादिसंस्कारदयो ऽपि, "कस्मिन् नु रूपाणि प्रतिष्ठितानीति हृदये" इति श्रुतेः । "कामा ये ऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः", "तीर्णो हि ", "असङ्गो ह्य् अयम्", "तद् वा अस्यैतद् अतिच्छन्दाः" इत्यादिश्रुतिशतेभ्यः, "अविकार्यो ऽयम् उच्यते", "अनादित्वान् निर्गुणत्वात्" इत्यादि -- इच्छाद्वेषादि च क्षेत्रस्यैव विषयस्य धर्मो नात्मन इति -- स्मृतिभ्यश् च कर्मस्थैवाशुद्धिर् नात्मस्था इति
units.iast: kimāśrayaḥ punā rūpādisaṃskārādaya iti । ucyate । yatra kāmādāyaḥ । kva punas te kāmādayaḥ । "kāmaḥ saṅkalpo vicikitsā" ityādiśruter buddhāv eva । tatraiva rūpādisaṃskāradayo 'pi, "kasmin nu rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitānīti hṛdaye" iti śruteḥ । "kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ", "tīrṇo hi ", "asaṅgo hy ayam", "tad vā asyaitad aticchandāḥ" ityādiśrutiśatebhyaḥ, "avikāryo 'yam ucyate", "anāditvān nirguṇatvāt" ityādi -- icchādveṣādi ca kṣetrasyaiva viṣayasya dharmo nātmana iti -- smṛtibhyaś ca karmasthaivāśuddhir nātmasthā iti
units.translation: “Where do impressions of color and the rest, and the other states, reside? In the intellect, where desire and the rest occur.” Where do desire and the rest occur? Scripture says, “‘Desire, intention, doubt…’”; they are in the intellect. Impressions of color and the rest are there too, as scripture says, ‘Where are forms established? In the heart.’ Many passages say: ‘the desires lodged in his heart’; ‘he has crossed beyond’; ‘this one is unattached’; and the rest. Tradition says: ‘It is called changeless’; ‘because it is beginningless and without qualities.’ Desire, aversion and the rest are properties of the field, the object, not of the Self. Thus impurity belongs to action and its field, not to the Self.”

units.label: Prose II.1.37
units.deva: अतो रूपादिसंस्काराद्यशुद्धिसंबन्धाभावान् न परस्माद् आत्मनो विलक्षणस् त्वम् इति प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधाभावाद् युक्तं पर एवात्माहम् इति प्रतिपत्तुम् -- "तद् आत्मानम् एवावेद् [अहं ब्रह्मास्मि]", "एकधैवानुद्रष्टव्यम्", "अहम् एवाधस्तात्", "आत्मैवाधस्तात्", "सर्वम् आत्मानं पश्येत्", "यत्र त्व् अस्य सर्वम् आत्मैव", "इदं सर्वं यद् अयम् आत्म", "स एषो [ऽकलः ]", "अनन्तरम् अबाह्यम्", "सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्य् अजः", "ब्रह्मैवेदम्", "एतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत", "प्रज्ञानस्य नामधेयानि", "सत्यं ज्ञानम् अनन्तं ब्रह्म", "तस्माद् वा", "तत् सृष्ट्वा तद् एवानुप्राविशत्", "एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः", "अशरीरं शरीरेषु", "न जायते म्रियते", "स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तम्", "स म आत्मेति विद्यात्", "यस् तु सर्वाणि भूतानि", "तद् एजति तन् नैजति", "वेनस् तत् पश्यन्", "तद् एवाग्निः", "अहम्, मनुर् अभवम् सूर्यश् च" "अन्तः प्रविष्टः शास्ता जनानाम्", "सद् एव सोम्य", "तत् सत्यं स आत्मा तत् त्वम् असि" इत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः
units.iast: ato rūpādisaṃskārādyaśuddhisaṃbandhābhāvān na parasmād ātmano vilakṣaṇas tvam iti pratyakṣādivirodhābhāvād yuktaṃ para evātmāham iti pratipattum -- "tad ātmānam evāved [ahaṃ brahmāsmi]", "ekadhaivānudraṣṭavyam", "aham evādhastāt", "ātmaivādhastāt", "sarvam ātmānaṃ paśyet", "yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaiva", "idaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātma", "sa eṣo ['kalaḥ ]", "anantaram abāhyam", "sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ", "brahmaivedam", "etayā dvārā prāpadyata", "prajñānasya nāmadheyāni", "satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma", "tasmād vā", "tat sṛṣṭvā tad evānuprāviśat", "eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ", "aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu", "na jāyate mriyate", "svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntam", "sa ma ātmeti vidyāt", "yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāni", "tad ejati tan naijati", "venas tat paśyan", "tad evāgniḥ", "aham, manur abhavam sūryaś ca" "antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānām", "sad eva somya", "tat satyaṃ sa ātmā tat tvam asi" ityādiśrutibhyaḥ
units.translation: “Therefore, because you have no connection with the impurity of impressions of form and the rest, you are not different from the Supreme Self. Since no conflict with perception or another means of knowledge follows, it is reasonable to understand ‘I am the Supreme Self.’ Scripture says: ‘He knew, “I am Brahman”’; ‘one should see it as one’; ‘I alone am below’; ‘the Self alone is below’; ‘one should see all as the Self’; ‘where everything is the Self’; ‘all this is what this Self is’; ‘it is without parts’; ‘without inner or outer’; ‘unborn within and without’; ‘all this is Brahman’; ‘he entered by this door’; ‘the names of awareness’; ‘Brahman is reality, knowledge and infinity’; ‘from that’; ‘having created it, he entered into it’; ‘the one divine Self hidden in all beings’; ‘bodiless among bodies’; ‘it is not born or does it die’; ‘the end of dream and waking’; ‘know that as my Self’; ‘whoever sees all beings’; ‘it moves and does not move’; ‘seeing that, one sees’; ‘that alone is fire’; ‘I became Manu and the sun’; ‘the ruler who entered within’; ‘Being alone, dear one’; and ‘That is real, that is the Self, you are that.’”

units.label: Prose II.1.38
units.deva: स्मृतिभ्यश् च -- "पूः प्राणिनः ... गुहाशयस्य", "आत्मैव देवताः", "नवद्वारे पुरे", "समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु", "विद्याविनयसंपन्ने", "अविभक्तंविभक्तेषु ", "वासुदेवः सर्वम्" इत्यादिभ्यः, एक एवात्मा परं ब्रह्म [सर्व]संसारधर्मविनिर्मुक्तस् त्वम् इति सिद्धम्
units.iast: smṛtibhyaś ca -- "pūḥ prāṇinaḥ ... guhāśayasya", "ātmaiva devatāḥ", "navadvāre pure", "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu", "vidyāvinayasaṃpanne", "avibhaktaṃvibhakteṣu ", "vāsudevaḥ sarvam" ityādibhyaḥ, eka evātmā paraṃ brahma [sarva]saṃsāradharmavinirmuktas tvam iti siddham
units.translation: “Tradition also says: ‘All beings are the dwelling of the One who rests in the heart’; ‘all the gods are the Self’; ‘the person in the city of nine gates’; ‘equal in all beings’; ‘in one endowed with knowledge and humility’; ‘undivided among the divided’; ‘Vāsudeva is all’; and the rest. Thus you are established as the one Self, Supreme Brahman, free from every condition of worldly existence.”

units.label: Prose II.1.39
units.deva: स यदि ब्रूयात् -- यदि भगवन् "अनन्तरो ऽबाह्यः", "सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्य् अजः", "कृत्स्नः प्रज्ञानघन एव" सैन्धवघनवद् आत्मा सर्वमूर्तिभेदवर्जित आकाशवद् एकरसः, किम् इदं दृश्यते श्रूयते वा सध्यं साधनं [वा] साधकश् चेति श्रुतिस्मृतिलोकप्रसिद्धं वादिशतविप्रतिपत्तिविषय इति
units.iast: sa yadi brūyāt -- yadi bhagavan "anantaro 'bāhyaḥ", "sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ", "kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva" saindhavaghanavad ātmā sarvamūrtibhedavarjita ākāśavad ekarasaḥ, kim idaṃ dṛśyate śrūyate vā sadhyaṃ sādhanaṃ [vā] sādhakaś ceti śrutismṛtilokaprasiddhaṃ vādiśatavipratipattiviṣaya iti
units.translation: The student says: “Revered one, if the Self is ‘without inner or outer,’ ‘unborn within and without,’ and a complete mass of awareness, like a solid lump of salt, free from every distinction of form and all of one nature like space, what is this that is seen and heard—the real and unreal, means and results, agent and the rest—accepted in scripture, tradition and ordinary experience, yet disputed by hundreds of schools?”

units.label: Prose II.1.40
units.deva: आचार्यो ब्रूयात् -- अविद्याकृतम् एतद् यद् इदं दृश्यते श्रूयते वा, परमार्थतस् त्व् एक एवात्मा अविद्याद्र्ष्टेर् अनेकवद् अवाभासते, तिमिरदृष्ट्यानेकचन्द्रवत् । "यत्र वान्यद् इव स्यात्", "यत्र हि द्वैतम् इव भवति तद् इतर इतरं पश्यति", "मृत्योः स मृत्युम् आप्नोति", "अथ यत्रान्यत् पश्यत्य् अन्यच् छृणोत्य् अन्यद् विजानाति तद् अल्पम्, ... अथ यद् अल्पं तन् मर्त्यम्", इति, "वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयम्", ["अनृतम्",] "अन्यो ऽसाव् अन्यो ऽहम्" इति भेददर्शननिन्दोपपत्तेर् अविद्याकृतं द्वैतम् "एकम् एवाद्वितीयम्", "यत्र त्व् अस्य", "को मोहः कः शोकः" इत्याद्येकत्वविधिश्रुतिभ्यश् चेति
units.iast: ācāryo brūyāt -- avidyākṛtam etad yad idaṃ dṛśyate śrūyate vā, paramārthatas tv eka evātmā avidyādrṣṭer anekavad avābhāsate, timiradṛṣṭyānekacandravat । "yatra vānyad iva syāt", "yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati", "mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti", "atha yatrānyat paśyaty anyac chṛṇoty anyad vijānāti tad alpam, ... atha yad alpaṃ tan martyam", iti, "vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam", ["anṛtam",] "anyo 'sāv anyo 'ham" iti bhedadarśananindopapatter avidyākṛtaṃ dvaitam "ekam evādvitīyam", "yatra tv asya", "ko mohaḥ kaḥ śokaḥ" ityādyekatvavidhiśrutibhyaś ceti
units.translation: The teacher says: “What is seen or heard is created by ignorance; in reality the Self alone exists, but to the vision of ignorance it appears as many, like one moon appearing as many to someone with an eye disease. Scripture condemns the perception of difference: ‘where there seems to be another’; ‘where there is duality, as it were, one sees another’; ‘he goes from death to death’; ‘where one sees, hears or knows something else, that is the small and mortal’; and ‘a modification is only a name arising from speech.’ Since it condemns the view ‘he is another; I am another,’ it teaches nonduality: ‘one alone without a second’; ‘where everything is the Self’; ‘what delusion or sorrow could there be?’; and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.41
units.deva: यद्य् एवं भगवन्, किमर्थं श्रुत्या साध्यसाधनादिभेद उच्यते उत्पत्तिः प्रलयश् चेति
units.iast: yady evaṃ bhagavan, kimarthaṃ śrutyā sādhyasādhanādibheda ucyate utpattiḥ pralayaś ceti
units.translation: The student asks: “Revered one, if this is so, why does scripture speak of differences between what is to be achieved and the means, and of creation and dissolution?”

units.label: Prose II.1.42
units.deva: अत्रोच्यते -- अविद्यावत उपात्तशरीरादिभेदस्येष्टानिष्टयोगिनम् आत्मानं मन्यमानस्य साधनैर् एवेष्टानिष्टप्राप्तिपरिहारोपायविवेकम् अजानत इष्टप्राप्तिं चानिष्टपरिहारं चेच्छतः शनैस् तद्विषयम् अज्ञानं निवर्तयति शास्त्रं न साध्यसाधनादिभेदं विधत्ते । अनिष्टरूपः संसारो हि स इति तद् भेददृष्टिम् एवाविद्यां संसारमूलम् उन्मूलयति उत्पत्तिप्रलयाद्येकत्वोपपत्तिप्रदर्शनेन
units.iast: atrocyate -- avidyāvata upāttaśarīrādibhedasyeṣṭāniṣṭayoginam ātmānaṃ manyamānasya sādhanair eveṣṭāniṣṭaprāptiparihāropāyavivekam ajānata iṣṭaprāptiṃ cāniṣṭaparihāraṃ cecchataḥ śanais tadviṣayam ajñānaṃ nivartayati śāstraṃ na sādhyasādhanādibhedaṃ vidhatte । aniṣṭarūpaḥ saṃsāro hi sa iti tad bhedadṛṣṭim evāvidyāṃ saṃsāramūlam unmūlayati utpattipralayādyekatvopapattipradarśanena
units.translation: The teacher replies: “For one who is ignorant, identifies with an acquired body and thinks the Self subject to desirable and undesirable things, scripture does not prescribe a real distinction between means and ends. It gradually removes ignorance from one who does not understand how to attain the desirable and avoid the undesirable, and who seeks those ends. Worldly existence itself is undesirable; scripture uproots ignorance, the root of bondage—the perception of difference—by showing through creation, dissolution and the rest how nonduality is reasonable.”

units.label: Prose II.1.43
units.deva: अविद्यायाम् उन्मूलितायां श्रुतिस्मृतिन्यायेभ्यः "अनन्तरम् अबाह्यम्", "सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्य् अजः" सैन्धवघनवत् "प्रज्ञानघन एव", एकरस आत्मा आकाशवत् परिपूर्ण इत्य् अत्रैवैका प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता परमार्थदर्शिनो भवति, न साध्यसाधनोत्पत्तिप्रलयादिभेदेनाशुद्धिगन्धो ऽप्य् उपपद्यते
units.iast: avidyāyām unmūlitāyāṃ śrutismṛtinyāyebhyaḥ "anantaram abāhyam", "sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ" saindhavaghanavat "prajñānaghana eva", ekarasa ātmā ākāśavat paripūrṇa ity atraivaikā prajñā pratiṣṭhitā paramārthadarśino bhavati, na sādhyasādhanotpattipralayādibhedenāśuddhigandho 'py upapadyate
units.translation: “When ignorance has been uprooted, from scripture, tradition and reasoning one has a single understanding: the Self is without inner or outer, unborn within and without, a mass of awareness alone like solid salt, of one nature, complete like space. For one who sees reality, no trace of impurity can follow from distinctions between means and ends, creation and dissolution, or the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.1.44
units.deva: तच् चैतत् परमार्थदर्शनं प्रतिपत्तुम् इच्छता वर्णाश्रमाद्यभिमानकृतपाङ्क्तरूपपुत्रवित्तलोकैषणादिभ्यो व्युत्थानं कर्तव्यम् । सम्यक्प्रत्ययविरोधात् तदभिमानस्य भेददर्शनप्रतिषेधार्थोपपत्तिश् चोपपद्यते । न ह्य् एकस्मिन्न् आत्मन्य् असंसारित्वबुद्धौ शास्त्रन्यायोत्पादितायां तद्विपरीता बुद्धिर् भवति । न ह्य् अग्नौ शीतत्वबुद्धिः, शरीरे वाजरामरणबुद्धिः । तस्माद् अविद्याकार्यत्वात् सर्वकर्मणां तत्साधनानां च यज्ञोपवीतादीनां परमार्थदर्शननिष्ठेन त्यागः कर्तव्यः
units.iast: tac caitat paramārthadarśanaṃ pratipattum icchatā varṇāśramādyabhimānakṛtapāṅktarūpaputravittalokaiṣaṇādibhyo vyutthānaṃ kartavyam । samyakpratyayavirodhāt tadabhimānasya bhedadarśanapratiṣedhārthopapattiś copapadyate । na hy ekasminn ātmany asaṃsāritvabuddhau śāstranyāyotpāditāyāṃ tadviparītā buddhir bhavati । na hy agnau śītatvabuddhiḥ, śarīre vājarāmaraṇabuddhiḥ । tasmād avidyākāryatvāt sarvakarmaṇāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ ca yajñopavītādīnāṃ paramārthadarśananiṣṭhena tyāgaḥ kartavyaḥ
units.translation: “One who wishes to understand this vision of reality must therefore withdraw from the desires for a wife, children, wealth and worlds, born of pride in caste, stage of life and the rest. Such identification conflicts with right knowledge. Scripture and reasoning justify renunciation to deny the vision of difference. Once knowledge of the one, non-worldly Self has arisen from scripture and reasoning, its opposite cannot remain, just as one cannot think fire is cold or the body free from old age and death. Therefore, since actions and their means—including the sacred thread—are effects of ignorance, one established in seeing reality must renounce them.”

units.label: Prose II.2.45
units.deva: सुखम् आसीनं ब्राह्मणं ब्रह्मनिष्ठं कश्चिद् ब्रह्मचारी जन्ममरणलक्षणात् संसारान् निर्विण्णो मुमुक्षुर् विधिवद् उपसन्नः पप्रच्छ -- भगवन्, कथम् अहं संसारान् मोक्षिष्ये । शरीरेन्द्रियविषयवेदनावान् जागरिते दुःखम् अनुभवामि तथा स्वप्ने ऽनुभवामि पुनः पुनः सुषुप्तिप्रतिपत्त्या विश्रम्य । किम् अयम् एव मम स्वभावः, किं वान्यस्वभावस्य सतो नैमित्तिक इति । यदि स्वभावो न मे मोक्षाशा स्वभावस्यावर्जनीयत्वात् । अथ नैमित्तिको निमित्तपरिहारे स्यान् मोक्षोपपत्तिः
units.iast: sukham āsīnaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brahmaniṣṭhaṃ kaścid brahmacārī janmamaraṇalakṣaṇāt saṃsārān nirviṇṇo mumukṣur vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha -- bhagavan, katham ahaṃ saṃsārān mokṣiṣye । śarīrendriyaviṣayavedanāvān jāgarite duḥkham anubhavāmi tathā svapne 'nubhavāmi punaḥ punaḥ suṣuptipratipattyā viśramya । kim ayam eva mama svabhāvaḥ, kiṃ vānyasvabhāvasya sato naimittika iti । yadi svabhāvo na me mokṣāśā svabhāvasyāvarjanīyatvāt । atha naimittiko nimittaparihāre syān mokṣopapattiḥ
units.translation: A student who wished for liberation, wearied by worldly existence marked by birth and death, approached properly a Brahmin teacher who was peacefully seated and established in Brahman. The student asked: “Revered one, how can I be freed from worldly existence? When awake I experience suffering from the body, senses and objects, and I experience it again and again in dreams, finding rest only in deep sleep. Is this my nature, or does it arise from a cause though I am of another nature? If it is my nature, I have no hope of liberation, since one cannot avoid one’s own nature. If it is caused, liberation is possible by removing its cause.”

units.label: Prose II.2.46
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- शृणु वत्स, न तवायं स्वभावः । नैमित्तिकः
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- śṛṇu vatsa, na tavāyaṃ svabhāvaḥ । naimittikaḥ
units.translation: The teacher said: “Listen, child. This is not your nature; it arises from a cause.”

units.label: Prose II.2.47
units.deva: इत्य् उक्तः शिष्य उवाच -- किं निमित्तम्, किं वा तस्य निवर्तकम्, को वा मम स्वभावः, यस्मिन् निमित्ते निवर्तिते नैमित्तिकाभावो रोगनिमित्तनिवृत्ताव् इव रोगी स्वभावं प्रतिपद्येयेति
units.iast: ity uktaḥ śiṣya uvāca -- kiṃ nimittam, kiṃ vā tasya nivartakam, ko vā mama svabhāvaḥ, yasmin nimitte nivartite naimittikābhāvo roganimittanivṛttāv iva rogī svabhāvaṃ pratipadyeyeti
units.translation: The student asked: “What is the cause, and what removes it? What is my own nature, such that when the cause is removed its effect ends and I return to my nature, as a sick person does when the cause of illness is removed?”

units.label: Prose II.2.48
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच -- अविद्या निमित्तम्, विद्या तस्या निवर्तिका, अविद्यायां निवृत्तायां तन्निमित्ताभावान् मोक्ष्यसे जन्ममरणलक्षणात् संसारात्, स्वप्नजाग्रद्दुःखं च नानुभविष्यसीति
units.iast: gurur uvāca -- avidyā nimittam, vidyā tasyā nivartikā, avidyāyāṃ nivṛttāyāṃ tannimittābhāvān mokṣyase janmamaraṇalakṣaṇāt saṃsārāt, svapnajāgradduḥkhaṃ ca nānubhaviṣyasīti
units.translation: The teacher said: “Ignorance is the cause; knowledge removes it. When ignorance ends, its cause is gone, and you will be freed from worldly existence marked by birth and death; you will no longer experience the suffering of waking and dream.”

units.label: Prose II.2.49
units.deva: शिष्य उवाच -- का साविद्या, किंविषया वा, विद्या च काविद्यानिवर्तिका यया स्वभावं प्रतिपद्येयेति
units.iast: śiṣya uvāca -- kā sāvidyā, kiṃviṣayā vā, vidyā ca kāvidyānivartikā yayā svabhāvaṃ pratipadyeyeti
units.translation: The student asked: “What is this ignorance, and what is its object? What is the knowledge that removes it, through which I may return to my own nature?”

units.label: Prose II.2.50
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच-- त्वं परमात्मानं सन्तम् असंसारिणं संसार्य् अहम् अस्मीति विपरीतं प्रतिपद्यसे, अकर्तारं सन्तं कर्तेति, अभोक्तारं सन्तं भोक्तेति, विद्यमानं चाविद्यमानम् इति, इयम् अविद्या
units.iast: gurur uvāca-- tvaṃ paramātmānaṃ santam asaṃsāriṇaṃ saṃsāry aham asmīti viparītaṃ pratipadyase, akartāraṃ santaṃ karteti, abhoktāraṃ santaṃ bhokteti, vidyamānaṃ cāvidyamānam iti, iyam avidyā
units.translation: The teacher says: “You are the Supreme Self, yet you understand yourself in the opposite way: you think ‘I am bound in worldly existence,’ though you are not; ‘I am the doer,’ though you are not; ‘I am the enjoyer,’ though you are not; and you treat as nonexistent what is real. This is ignorance.”

units.label: Prose II.2.51
units.deva: शिष्य उवाच -- यद्य् अप्य् अहं विद्यमानस् तथापि न परमात्मा । कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वलक्षणः संसारो मम स्वभावः, प्रत्यक्षादिभिः प्रमाणैर् अनुभूयमानत्वात् । नाविद्यानिमित्तः, अविद्यायाः स्वात्मविषयत्वानुपपत्तेः । अविद्या नामान्यस्मिन्न् अन्यधर्माध्यारोपणा । यथा प्रसिद्धं रजतं प्रसिद्धायां शुक्तिकायाम्, यथा प्रसिद्धं पुरुषं स्थाणाव् अध्यारोपयति, प्रसिद्धं वा स्थाणुं पुरुषे । नाप्रसिद्धं प्रसिद्धे, प्रसिद्धं वाप्रसिद्धे । न चात्मन्य् अनात्मानम् अध्यारोपयति, आत्मनो ऽप्रसिद्धत्वात् । तथात्मानम् अनात्मनि, आत्मनो ऽप्रसिद्धत्वाद् एव
units.iast: śiṣya uvāca -- yady apy ahaṃ vidyamānas tathāpi na paramātmā । kartṛtvabhoktṛtvalakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāro mama svabhāvaḥ, pratyakṣādibhiḥ pramāṇair anubhūyamānatvāt । nāvidyānimittaḥ, avidyāyāḥ svātmaviṣayatvānupapatteḥ । avidyā nāmānyasminn anyadharmādhyāropaṇā । yathā prasiddhaṃ rajataṃ prasiddhāyāṃ śuktikāyām, yathā prasiddhaṃ puruṣaṃ sthāṇāv adhyāropayati, prasiddhaṃ vā sthāṇuṃ puruṣe । nāprasiddhaṃ prasiddhe, prasiddhaṃ vāprasiddhe । na cātmany anātmānam adhyāropayati, ātmano 'prasiddhatvāt । tathātmānam anātmani, ātmano 'prasiddhatvād eva
units.translation: The student says: “Even if I exist, I am not the Supreme Self. Worldly existence, marked by agency and enjoyment, is my nature, because I experience it through perception and the other means of knowledge. It is not caused by ignorance, because ignorance cannot have the Self as its object. Ignorance means superimposing the properties of one thing on another—for example, seeing familiar silver in a familiar shell, or a familiar man in a post, or a familiar post in a man. One cannot superimpose something unfamiliar on what is familiar, or something familiar on what is unfamiliar. I cannot superimpose the not-Self on the Self, because the Self is unfamiliar; nor can I superimpose the Self on the not-Self, for the same reason.”

units.label: Prose II.2.52
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- न, व्यभिचारात् । न हि वत्स, प्रसिद्धं प्रसिद्ध एवाध्यारोपयतीति नियन्तुं शक्यम् । आत्मन्य् अध्यारोपणदर्शनात् । गौरो ऽहं कृष्णो ऽहम् इति देहधर्मस्याहंप्रत्ययविषय आत्मन्य् अहंप्रत्ययविषयस्य च देहे ऽयम् अहम् अस्मीति
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- na, vyabhicārāt । na hi vatsa, prasiddhaṃ prasiddha evādhyāropayatīti niyantuṃ śakyam । ātmany adhyāropaṇadarśanāt । gauro 'haṃ kṛṣṇo 'ham iti dehadharmasyāhaṃpratyayaviṣaya ātmany ahaṃpratyayaviṣayasya ca dehe 'yam aham asmīti
units.translation: The teacher replies: “No; that rule fails. Dear one, it cannot be restricted to saying that one familiar thing is superimposed only on another familiar thing. We see superimposition on the Self: one says ‘I am fair’ or ‘I am dark,’ though fairness and darkness belong to the body, which is the object of the thought ‘I’; and one says ‘I am this,’ though the body is the object of the Self-directed ‘I’-thought.”

units.label: Prose II.2.53
units.deva: शिष्य आह -- प्रसिद्ध एव तर्ह्य् आत्माहंप्रत्ययविषयतया देहश् चायम् इति । तत्रैवं सति प्रसिद्धयोर् एव देहात्मनोर् इतरेतराध्यारोपणा[त्] स्थाणुपुरुषयोः शुक्तिकारजतयोर् इव । तत्र कं विसेषम् आश्रित्य भगवतोक्तं प्रसिद्धयोर् इतरेतराध्यारोपणेति नियन्तुं न शक्यत इति
units.iast: śiṣya āha -- prasiddha eva tarhy ātmāhaṃpratyayaviṣayatayā dehaś cāyam iti । tatraivaṃ sati prasiddhayor eva dehātmanor itaretarādhyāropaṇā[t] sthāṇupuruṣayoḥ śuktikārajatayor iva । tatra kaṃ viseṣam āśritya bhagavatoktaṃ prasiddhayor itaretarādhyāropaṇeti niyantuṃ na śakyata iti
units.translation: The student says: “Then the Self is familiar as the object of the thought ‘I,’ and the body is familiar as ‘this.’ Since both are familiar, the body and Self are superimposed on one another, as a post and a man, or a shell and silver, can be.” He asks what difference permits the teacher to deny superimposition between two familiar things.

units.label: Prose II.2.54
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच -- शृणु । सत्यं प्रसिद्धौ देहात्मानौ न तु स्थाणुपुरुषाव् इव विविक्तप्रत्ययविषयतया सर्वलोकप्रसिद्धौ । कथं तर्हि । नित्यम् एव निरन्तराविविक्तप्रत्ययविषयतया । न ह्य् अयं देहो ऽयम् आत्मेति विविक्ताभ्यां प्रत्ययाभ्यां देहात्मानौ गृह्णाति यतः कश्चित् । अत एव हि मोमुह्यते लोक आत्मानात्मविषये, एवम् आत्मा नैवम् आत्मेति । इमं विशेषम् आश्रित्यावोचं नैवं शक्यम् इति
units.iast: gurur uvāca -- śṛṇu । satyaṃ prasiddhau dehātmānau na tu sthāṇupuruṣāv iva viviktapratyayaviṣayatayā sarvalokaprasiddhau । kathaṃ tarhi । nityam eva nirantarāviviktapratyayaviṣayatayā । na hy ayaṃ deho 'yam ātmeti viviktābhyāṃ pratyayābhyāṃ dehātmānau gṛhṇāti yataḥ kaścit । ata eva hi momuhyate loka ātmānātmaviṣaye, evam ātmā naivam ātmeti । imaṃ viśeṣam āśrityāvocaṃ naivaṃ śakyam iti
units.translation: The teacher says: “Listen. The body and Self are indeed familiar, but not to all people as distinct objects of separate cognitions, like a post and a man. Rather, they are always the objects of a single, continuous, undistinguished cognition. No one grasps them with separate thoughts, ‘this is the body’ and ‘this is the Self.’ That is why the world is confused about Self and not-Self, thinking ‘the Self is like this’ or ‘not like this.’ That is the difference I had in mind.”

units.label: Prose II.2.55
units.deva: नन्व् अविद्याध्यारोपितं [यत्र] यत् तद् असत् [तत्र] दृष्टम्, यथा रजतं शुक्तिकायाम्, स्थाणौ पुरुषः, रज्ज्वां सर्पः, आकाशे तलमलिनत्वम् इत्यादि । तथा देहात्मनोर् अपि नित्यम् एवो निरन्तराविविक्तप्रत्ययतयेतरेतराध्यारोपणा कृता स्यात्, तद् इतरेतरयोर् नित्यम् एवासत्त्वं स्यात् । यथा शुक्तिकादिष्व् अविद्याध्यारोपितानां रजतादीनां नित्यम् एवात्यन्तासत्त्वम्, तद्विपरीतानां च विपरीतेषु, तद्वद् देहात्मनोर् अविद्ययैवेतरेतराध्यारोपणा कृता स्यात् । तत्रैवं सति देहात्मनोर् असत्त्वं प्रसज्येत । तच् चानिष्टम्, वैनाशिकपक्षत्वात् । अथ तद्विपर्ययेण देह आत्मन्य् अविद्ययाध्यारोपितः, देहस्यात्मनि सति असत्त्वं प्रसज्येत । तच् चानिष्टम्, प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधात् । तस्माद् देहात्मानौ नाविद्ययेतरेतरस्मिन्न् अध्यारोपितौ । कथं तर्हि । वंशस्तम्भवन् नित्यसंयुक्तौ
units.iast: nanv avidyādhyāropitaṃ [yatra] yat tad asat [tatra] dṛṣṭam, yathā rajataṃ śuktikāyām, sthāṇau puruṣaḥ, rajjvāṃ sarpaḥ, ākāśe talamalinatvam ityādi । tathā dehātmanor api nityam evo nirantarāviviktapratyayatayetaretarādhyāropaṇā kṛtā syāt, tad itaretarayor nityam evāsattvaṃ syāt । yathā śuktikādiṣv avidyādhyāropitānāṃ rajatādīnāṃ nityam evātyantāsattvam, tadviparītānāṃ ca viparīteṣu, tadvad dehātmanor avidyayaivetaretarādhyāropaṇā kṛtā syāt । tatraivaṃ sati dehātmanor asattvaṃ prasajyeta । tac cāniṣṭam, vaināśikapakṣatvāt । atha tadviparyayeṇa deha ātmany avidyayādhyāropitaḥ, dehasyātmani sati asattvaṃ prasajyeta । tac cāniṣṭam, pratyakṣādivirodhāt । tasmād dehātmānau nāvidyayetaretarasminn adhyāropitau । kathaṃ tarhi । vaṃśastambhavan nityasaṃyuktau
units.translation: The student objects: “What is superimposed through ignorance is seen to be unreal: silver on a shell, a person on a post, a snake on a rope, a stain on the sky. In the same way, if body and Self are continuously and mutually superimposed, both must always be unreal. If the body were superimposed on the Self, the body would be unreal; if the Self were superimposed on the body, the Self would be unreal. Then the body and Self would both be unreal, which is undesirable because it is the doctrine of annihilationists. If instead the body alone is superimposed on the Self, the body would be unreal, contrary to perception and the other means of knowledge. Therefore body and Self cannot be superimposed on one another. How, then, are they related?” The teacher replies: “They are continually joined, like two bamboo posts.”

units.label: Prose II.2.56
units.deva: न । अनित्यत्वपरार्थत्वप्रसङ्गात् । संहतत्वात् [परार्थत्वम् अनित्यत्वं च] वंशस्तम्भादिवद् एव । किं च यस् तु परैर् देहेन संहतः कल्पित आत्मा स संहतत्वात् परार्थः । तेनासंहतः परो ऽन्यो नित्यः सिद्धस् तावत्
units.iast: na । anityatvaparārthatvaprasaṅgāt । saṃhatatvāt [parārthatvam anityatvaṃ ca] vaṃśastambhādivad eva । kiṃ ca yas tu parair dehena saṃhataḥ kalpita ātmā sa saṃhatatvāt parārthaḥ । tenāsaṃhataḥ paro 'nyo nityaḥ siddhas tāvat
units.translation: The student answers: “No, because then the Self would be impermanent and exist for the sake of another, like a composite such as bamboo. What is joined to the body as part of a composite would exist for something else. A distinct, unjoined and eternal Self must therefore be established.”

units.label: Prose II.2.57
units.deva: तस्यासंहतस्य देहे देहमात्रतयाध्यारोपितत्वेनासत्त्वानित्यत्वादिदोषप्रसङ्गो भवति । तत्र निरात्मको देह इति वैनाशिकपक्षप्राप्तिदोषः स्यात्
units.iast: tasyāsaṃhatasya dehe dehamātratayādhyāropitatvenāsattvānityatvādidoṣaprasaṅgo bhavati । tatra nirātmako deha iti vaināśikapakṣaprāptidoṣaḥ syāt
units.translation: “But if this distinct, unjoined Self is superimposed on the body as though it were only the body, it would become unreal and impermanent. Then the fault of the annihilationist view would follow: the body would be without a Self.”

units.label: Prose II.2.58
units.deva: न । स्वत एवात्मन आकाशस्येवासंहतत्वाभ्युपगमात् । सर्वेणासंहतः सन्न् आत्मेति न निरात्मको देहादिः सर्वः स्यात् । यथा चाकाशं सर्वेणासंहतम् इति सर्वं न निराकाशं भवति, एवम् । तस्मान् न वैनाशिकपक्षप्राप्तिदोषः स्यात्
units.iast: na । svata evātmana ākāśasyevāsaṃhatatvābhyupagamāt । sarveṇāsaṃhataḥ sann ātmeti na nirātmako dehādiḥ sarvaḥ syāt । yathā cākāśaṃ sarveṇāsaṃhatam iti sarvaṃ na nirākāśaṃ bhavati, evam । tasmān na vaināśikapakṣaprāptidoṣaḥ syāt
units.translation: The teacher says: “No, because the Self is accepted as unjoined by its very nature, like space. Though unjoined with everything, the Self exists; therefore the whole body and the rest need not be without a Self, just as space, though unjoined with everything, means that the world is not without space.”

units.label: Prose II.2.59
units.deva: यत् पुनर् उक्तम्, देहस्यात्मन्य् असत्त्वे प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधः स्याद् इति । तन् न । प्रत्यक्षादिभिर् आत्मनि देहस्य सत्त्वानुपलब्धेः । न ह्य् आत्मनि, कुण्डे बदरम्, क्षीरे सर्पिः, तिले तैलम्, भित्तौ चित्रम् इव च, प्रत्यक्षादिभिर् देह उपलभ्यते । तस्मान् न प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधः
units.iast: yat punar uktam, dehasyātmany asattve pratyakṣādivirodhaḥ syād iti । tan na । pratyakṣādibhir ātmani dehasya sattvānupalabdheḥ । na hy ātmani, kuṇḍe badaram, kṣīre sarpiḥ, tile tailam, bhittau citram iva ca, pratyakṣādibhir deha upalabhyate । tasmān na pratyakṣādivirodhaḥ
units.translation: “As for the claim that the body’s existence in the Self would conflict with perception: it does not. Perception and the other means of knowledge do not show the body existing inside the Self. They do not reveal a body in the Self as they reveal a berry in a bowl, clarified butter in milk, oil in sesame, or a painting on a wall. So there is no such conflict.”

units.label: Prose II.2.60
units.deva: कथं तर्हि प्रत्यक्षाद्यप्रसिद्धात्मनि देहाध्यारोपण, देहे चात्मारोपणा
units.iast: kathaṃ tarhi pratyakṣādyaprasiddhātmani dehādhyāropaṇa, dehe cātmāropaṇā
units.translation: The student asks: “How, then, is the body superimposed on the Self, or the Self on the body, if the Self is not established by perception or the other means?”

units.label: Prose II.2.61
units.deva: नायं दोषः । स्वभाव[प्र]सिद्धत्वाद् आत्मनः । न हि कादाचित्कसिद्धाव् एवाध्यारोपणा न नित्यसिद्धाव् इति नियन्तुं शक्यम्, आकाशे तलमलाद्यध्यारोपणदर्शनात्
units.iast: nāyaṃ doṣaḥ । svabhāva[pra]siddhatvād ātmanaḥ । na hi kādācitkasiddhāv evādhyāropaṇā na nityasiddhāv iti niyantuṃ śakyam, ākāśe talamalādyadhyāropaṇadarśanāt
units.translation: The teacher says: “There is no fault in this, because the Self is established by its own nature. One cannot insist that superimposition occurs only on what is established occasionally, and never on what is always established; we see stains and the rest superimposed on the sky.”

units.label: Prose II.2.62
units.deva: किं भगवन्, देहात्मनोर् इतरेतराध्यारोपणा देहादिसंघाटकृताथवात्मकृतेति
units.iast: kiṃ bhagavan, dehātmanor itaretarādhyāropaṇā dehādisaṃghāṭakṛtāthavātmakṛteti
units.translation: The student asks: “Revered one, is the mutual superimposition of body and Self caused by the aggregate of body and senses, or by the Self?”

units.label: Prose II.2.63
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच -- यदि देहादिसंघातकृता, यदि वात्मकृता, किं तव स्यात्
units.iast: gurur uvāca -- yadi dehādisaṃghātakṛtā, yadi vātmakṛtā, kiṃ tava syāt
units.translation: The teacher says: “Whether the aggregate causes it or the Self causes it, what difference would that make to you?”

units.label: Prose II.2.64
units.deva: इत्य् उक्तः शिष्य आह -- यद्य् अहं देहादिसंघातमात्रः, ततो ममाचेतनत्वात् परार्थत्वम् इति न मत्कृता देहात्मनोर् इतरेतराध्यारोपणा । अथाहम् आत्मा परो ऽन्यः संघातात्, चितिमत्त्वात् स्वार्थ इति मयैव चितिमतात्मन्य् अध्यारोपणा क्रियते सर्वानर्थबीजभूता
units.iast: ity uktaḥ śiṣya āha -- yady ahaṃ dehādisaṃghātamātraḥ, tato mamācetanatvāt parārthatvam iti na matkṛtā dehātmanor itaretarādhyāropaṇā । athāham ātmā paro 'nyaḥ saṃghātāt, citimattvāt svārtha iti mayaiva citimatātmany adhyāropaṇā kriyate sarvānarthabījabhūtā
units.translation: The student replies: “If I am only the aggregate of body and senses, I am insentient and exist for another, so I cannot cause the mutual superimposition. But if I am a distinct Self, separate from the aggregate, conscious and existing for my own sake, then I myself superimpose one on the other as a conscious being. This superimposition is the seed of all misery.”

units.label: Prose II.2.65
units.deva: इत्य् उक्तो गुरुर् उवाच -- अनर्थबीजभूतां चेन् मिथ्याध्यारोपणां जानीषे, मा कार्षीस् तर्हि
units.iast: ity ukto gurur uvāca -- anarthabījabhūtāṃ cen mithyādhyāropaṇāṃ jānīṣe, mā kārṣīs tarhi
units.translation: The teacher says: “If you know this false superimposition is the seed of misery, then do not make it.”

units.label: Prose II.2.66
units.deva: नैव भगवन्, शक्नोमि न कर्तुम् । अन्येन केनचित् प्रयुक्तो ऽहं न स्वतन्त्र इति
units.iast: naiva bhagavan, śaknomi na kartum । anyena kenacit prayukto 'haṃ na svatantra iti
units.translation: The student replies: “Revered one, I cannot help doing it. I am driven by something else and am not independent.”

units.label: Prose II.2.67
units.deva: न तर्ह्य् अचितिमत्त्वात् स्वार्थस् त्वम् । येन प्रयुक्तो ऽस्वतन्त्रः प्रवर्तसे, स चितिमान् स्वार्थः, संघाट एव त्वम्
units.iast: na tarhy acitimattvāt svārthas tvam । yena prayukto 'svatantraḥ pravartase, sa citimān svārthaḥ, saṃghāṭa eva tvam
units.translation: The teacher says: “Then you are not a conscious being existing for yourself. The one who drives you, and by whom you act without independence, is conscious and exists for itself; you are only the aggregate.”

units.label: Prose II.2.68
units.deva: यद्य् अचेतनो ऽहम्, कथं सुखदुःखवेदनां भवदुक्तं च जानामि
units.iast: yady acetano 'ham, kathaṃ sukhaduḥkhavedanāṃ bhavaduktaṃ ca jānāmi
units.translation: The student objects: “If I am insentient, how do I experience happiness and sorrow, and understand what you say?”

units.label: Prose II.2.69
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच -- किं सुखदुःखवेदनाया मदुक्ताच् चान्यस् त्वं किं वानन्य एवेति
units.iast: gurur uvāca -- kiṃ sukhaduḥkhavedanāyā maduktāc cānyas tvaṃ kiṃ vānanya eveti
units.translation: The teacher asks: “Are you other than the experience of happiness and sorrow and the words I have spoken, or are you non-different from them?”

units.label: Prose II.2.70
units.deva: शिष्य उवाच -- नाहं तावद् अनन्यः । कस्मात् । यस्मात् तदुभयं कर्मभूतं गटादिम् इव जानामि । यदि अनन्यो ऽहम्, तेन तदुभयं न जानीयाम्, किं तु जानामि, तस्माद् अन्यः । सुखदुःखवेदनाविक्रिया च स्वार्थैव प्राप्नोति, त्वदुक्तं च स्यात्, अनन्यत्वे, न च तयोः स्वार्थता युक्ता । न हि चन्दनकण्टककृते सुखदुःखे चन्दनकण्टकार्थे, घटोपयोगो वा घटार्थः । तस्मात् तद्विज्ञातुर् मम चन्दनादिकृतो ऽर्थः । अहं हि ततो ऽन्यः समस्तम् अर्थं जानामि बुद्ध्यारूढम्
units.iast: śiṣya uvāca -- nāhaṃ tāvad ananyaḥ । kasmāt । yasmāt tadubhayaṃ karmabhūtaṃ gaṭādim iva jānāmi । yadi ananyo 'ham, tena tadubhayaṃ na jānīyām, kiṃ tu jānāmi, tasmād anyaḥ । sukhaduḥkhavedanāvikriyā ca svārthaiva prāpnoti, tvaduktaṃ ca syāt, ananyatve, na ca tayoḥ svārthatā yuktā । na hi candanakaṇṭakakṛte sukhaduḥkhe candanakaṇṭakārthe, ghaṭopayogo vā ghaṭārthaḥ । tasmāt tadvijñātur mama candanādikṛto 'rthaḥ । ahaṃ hi tato 'nyaḥ samastam arthaṃ jānāmi buddhyārūḍham
units.translation: The student says: “I am certainly not non-different from them, because I know both as things experienced, like a pot. If I were identical with them, I would not know them; since I do, I am other than they are. The changing experience of pleasure and pain is therefore for my sake, as you said. It would not make sense for either to exist for its own sake: sandalwood and thorns do not experience the pleasure or pain they cause, and a pot is not for the pot’s own use. Their purpose is for me, their knower. I am other than all of them and know everything that appears in the intellect.”

units.label: Prose II.2.71
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- एवं तर्हि स्वार्थस् त्वं चितिमत्त्वान् न परेण प्रयुज्यसे । न हि चितिमान् परतन्त्रः परेण प्रयुज्यते, चितिमतश् चितिमदर्थत्वानुपपत्तेः, समत्वात्, प्रकाशयोर् इव । नाप्य् अचितिमदर्थत्वं चितिमतो भवति, अचितिमतो ऽचितिमत्त्वाद् एव स्वार्थसंबन्धानुपपत्तेः । नाप्य् अचितिमतोर् अन्योन्यार्थत्वं दृष्टम् । न हि काष्ठकुड्ये ऽन्योन्यार्थं कुर्वाते
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- evaṃ tarhi svārthas tvaṃ citimattvān na pareṇa prayujyase । na hi citimān paratantraḥ pareṇa prayujyate, citimataś citimadarthatvānupapatteḥ, samatvāt, prakāśayor iva । nāpy acitimadarthatvaṃ citimato bhavati, acitimato 'citimattvād eva svārthasaṃbandhānupapatteḥ । nāpy acitimator anyonyārthatvaṃ dṛṣṭam । na hi kāṣṭhakuḍye 'nyonyārthaṃ kurvāte
units.translation: The teacher says: “Then you are conscious and exist for yourself; you are not employed by another. A conscious being is not subject to another, since one conscious being cannot exist for the sake of another conscious being: they are equal, like two lights. Nor can a conscious being exist for the sake of something insentient, since the insentient cannot have a relation of purpose for itself. Nor do two insentient things exist for each other’s sake; wood and a wall do not act for one another.”

units.label: Prose II.2.72
units.deva: ननु चितिमत्त्वे समे ऽपि भृत्यस्वामिनोर् अन्योन्यार्थत्वं दृष्टम्
units.iast: nanu citimattve same 'pi bhṛtyasvāminor anyonyārthatvaṃ dṛṣṭam
units.translation: The student objects: “Yet a servant and master, both conscious, are seen to act for one another.”

units.label: Prose II.2.73
units.deva: नैवम्, अग्नेर् उष्णप्रकाशवत् तव चितिमत्त्वस्य विवक्षितत्वात् । दर्शितश् च दृष्टान्तः प्रकाशयोर् इवेति । तत्रैवं सति स्वबुद्ध्यारूढम् एव सर्वम् उपलभसे ऽग्न्युष्णप्रकाशतुल्येन कूटस्थनित्यचैतन्यस्वरूपेण । यदि चैवम् आत्मनः सर्वदा निर्विशेषत्वम् अभ्युपगच्छसि । किम् इत्य् ऊचिवान्, सुषुप्ते विश्रम्य विश्रम्य जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोर् दुःखम् अनुभवामि । किम् अयम् एव मम स्वभावः, किं वा नैमित्तिक इति च । किम् असौ व्यामोहो ऽपगतः, किं वा न
units.iast: naivam, agner uṣṇaprakāśavat tava citimattvasya vivakṣitatvāt । darśitaś ca dṛṣṭāntaḥ prakāśayor iveti । tatraivaṃ sati svabuddhyārūḍham eva sarvam upalabhase 'gnyuṣṇaprakāśatulyena kūṭasthanityacaitanyasvarūpeṇa । yadi caivam ātmanaḥ sarvadā nirviśeṣatvam abhyupagacchasi । kim ity ūcivān, suṣupte viśramya viśramya jāgratsvapnayor duḥkham anubhavāmi । kim ayam eva mama svabhāvaḥ, kiṃ vā naimittika iti ca । kim asau vyāmoho 'pagataḥ, kiṃ vā na
units.translation: The teacher says: “That is not so in the sense intended. What matters is consciousness itself, like the heat and light of fire, as the example of lights shows. In that way, you experience everything that appears in your intellect through your own understanding, which is changeless, eternal consciousness, like fire’s heat and light. If you accept that the Self is always without distinctions, why did you say that after resting in deep sleep you experience sorrow in waking and dream? Is your delusion gone, or not?”

units.label: Prose II.2.74
units.deva: इत्य् उक्तः शिष्य उवाच -- भगवन्, अपगतस् त्वत्प्रसादाद् व्यामोहः, किं तु मम कूटस्थतायां संशयः । कथम् । शब्दादीनां स्वतःसिद्धिर् नास्ति, अचेतनत्वात् । शब्दाद्याकारप्रत्ययोत्पत्तेस् तु तेषाम् । प्रत्ययानाम् इतरेतरव्यावृत्तविशेषणानां नीलपीताद्याकारवतां स्वतःसिद्ध्यसंभवात् । तस्माद् बाह्याकारनिमित्तत्वं गम्यत इति बाह्याकारवच्छब्दाद्याकारत्वसिद्धिः । तथा प्रत्ययानाम् अप्य् अहंप्रत्ययालम्बनवस्तुभेदानां संहतत्वाद् अचैतन्योपपत्तेः स्वार्थत्वासंभवात् स्वरूपव्यतिरिक्तग्राहकग्राह्यत्वेन सिद्धिः शब्दादिवद् एव । असंहतत्वे सति चैतन्यात्मकत्वात् स्वार्थो ऽप्य् अहं प्रत्ययानां नीलपीताद्याकाराणाम् उपलब्धेति विक्रियावान् एव, कूटस्थ इति संशयः
units.iast: ity uktaḥ śiṣya uvāca -- bhagavan, apagatas tvatprasādād vyāmohaḥ, kiṃ tu mama kūṭasthatāyāṃ saṃśayaḥ । katham । śabdādīnāṃ svataḥsiddhir nāsti, acetanatvāt । śabdādyākārapratyayotpattes tu teṣām । pratyayānām itaretaravyāvṛttaviśeṣaṇānāṃ nīlapītādyākāravatāṃ svataḥsiddhyasaṃbhavāt । tasmād bāhyākāranimittatvaṃ gamyata iti bāhyākāravacchabdādyākāratvasiddhiḥ । tathā pratyayānām apy ahaṃpratyayālambanavastubhedānāṃ saṃhatatvād acaitanyopapatteḥ svārthatvāsaṃbhavāt svarūpavyatiriktagrāhakagrāhyatvena siddhiḥ śabdādivad eva । asaṃhatatve sati caitanyātmakatvāt svārtho 'py ahaṃ pratyayānāṃ nīlapītādyākārāṇām upalabdheti vikriyāvān eva, kūṭastha iti saṃśayaḥ
units.translation: The student replies: “Revered one, through your grace my delusion is gone, but I doubt whether I am changeless. Sounds and other objects are not established by themselves, since they are insentient; they are established when cognitions shaped like sound and the rest arise. But those cognitions, distinct from one another and qualified by blue, yellow and other forms, cannot establish themselves. Therefore they seem to be caused by external forms, and so are shown to have the forms of sounds and the rest. Likewise cognitions are joined to distinct objects indicated by the ‘I’-thought; because they are composite and insentient, they cannot exist for themselves. They appear to be grasped by something other than themselves, like sounds and the rest. Yet the ‘I’-thought seems unjoined, conscious and for itself; it may be the perceiver. But because it has different forms, perhaps it changes. So I doubt that I am changeless.”

units.label: Prose II.2.75
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- न युक्तस् तव संशयः । यतस् तेषां प्रत्ययानां नियमेनाशेषत उपलब्धेर् एवापरिणामित्वात् कूटस्थत्वसिद्धौ निश्चयहेतुम् एवाशेषचित्तप्रचारोपलब्धिं संशयहेतुम् आत्थ । यदि हि तव परिणामित्वं स्यात्, अशेषस्वविषयचित्तप्रचारोपलब्धिर् न स्यात्, चित्तस्येव स्वविषये यथा चेन्द्रियाणां स्वविषयेषु । न च तथात्मनस् तव स्वविषयैकदेशोपलब्धिः । अतः कूटस्थतैव तवेति
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- na yuktas tava saṃśayaḥ । yatas teṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ niyamenāśeṣata upalabdher evāpariṇāmitvāt kūṭasthatvasiddhau niścayahetum evāśeṣacittapracāropalabdhiṃ saṃśayahetum āttha । yadi hi tava pariṇāmitvaṃ syāt, aśeṣasvaviṣayacittapracāropalabdhir na syāt, cittasyeva svaviṣaye yathā cendriyāṇāṃ svaviṣayeṣu । na ca tathātmanas tava svaviṣayaikadeśopalabdhiḥ । ataḥ kūṭasthataiva taveti
units.translation: The teacher says: “Your doubt is unfounded. Cognitions are necessarily known in their entirety and without exception; since they are known, the Self’s changelessness is established. You have called this complete awareness of every movement of the mind a reason for doubt, though it is itself a reason for certainty. If you changed, you could not know every movement within your field. The mind knows only its own objects, as the senses know only their own; you are not limited to knowing one part of your field. Therefore you are certainly changeless.”

units.label: Prose II.2.76
units.deva: तत्राह -- उपलब्धिर् नाम धात्वर्थो विक्रियैव, उपलब्धुः कूटस्थ्[आत्म्]अता चेति विरुद्धम्
units.iast: tatrāha -- upalabdhir nāma dhātvartho vikriyaiva, upalabdhuḥ kūṭasth[ātm]atā ceti viruddham
units.translation: The student objects: “But ‘knowing’ is an action-word and means a change. How can the knower be changeless?”

units.label: Prose II.2.77
units.deva: न । धात्वर्थविक्रियायाम् उपलब्ध्युपचारात् । यो हि बौद्धः प्रत्ययः स धात्वर्थो विक्रियात्मक आत्मन उपलब्ध्याभासफलावसान इत्य् उपलब्धिशब्देनोपचर्यते । यथा छिदिक्रिया द्वैधीभावफलावसानेति धात्वर्थत्वेनोपचर्यते, तद्वत्
units.iast: na । dhātvarthavikriyāyām upalabdhyupacārāt । yo hi bauddhaḥ pratyayaḥ sa dhātvartho vikriyātmaka ātmana upalabdhyābhāsaphalāvasāna ity upalabdhiśabdenopacaryate । yathā chidikriyā dvaidhībhāvaphalāvasāneti dhātvarthatvenopacaryate, tadvat
units.translation: The teacher replies: “No. The word ‘knowing’ is figuratively used for the change expressed by the verbal root. A cognition in the intellect is a change and resembles the result of awareness; therefore it is spoken of as knowing. Just as the verbal root ‘cut’ refers to an action that ends in division, so too.”

units.label: Prose II.2.78
units.deva: इत्य् उक्तः शिष्य आह -- ननु भगवन्, मम कूटस्थत्वप्रतिपादनं प्रत्य् असमर्थो दृष्टान्तः । कथम् । छिदिश् छेद्यविक्रियावसानोपचर्यते यथा धात्वर्थत्वेन, तथोपलब्धिशब्दोपचरितो ऽपि धात्वर्थो बौद्धप्रत्यय आत्मन उपलब्धिविक्रियावसानश् चेन् नात्मनः कूटस्थतां प्रतिपादयितुं समर्थः
units.iast: ity uktaḥ śiṣya āha -- nanu bhagavan, mama kūṭasthatvapratipādanaṃ praty asamartho dṛṣṭāntaḥ । katham । chidiś chedyavikriyāvasānopacaryate yathā dhātvarthatvena, tathopalabdhiśabdopacarito 'pi dhātvartho bauddhapratyaya ātmana upalabdhivikriyāvasānaś cen nātmanaḥ kūṭasthatāṃ pratipādayituṃ samarthaḥ
units.translation: The student says: “Revered one, that example does not establish my changelessness. ‘Cutting’ refers to an action ending in a change in what is cut. Likewise, if ‘knowing’ refers to an intellectual change ending in a cognition, it cannot establish that the Self is changeless.”

units.label: Prose II.2.79
units.deva: गुरुर् उवाच -- सत्यम् एवं स्यात्, यद्य् उपलब्ध्युपलब्ध्रोर् विशेषः । नित्योपलब्धिमात्र एव ह्य् उपलब्धा । न तु तार्किकसमय इवान्योपलब्धिर् अन्य च उपलब्धा च
units.iast: gurur uvāca -- satyam evaṃ syāt, yady upalabdhyupalabdhror viśeṣaḥ । nityopalabdhimātra eva hy upalabdhā । na tu tārkikasamaya ivānyopalabdhir anya ca upalabdhā ca
units.translation: The teacher says: “That would be so if awareness and the knower were different. The knower is only eternal awareness; there is not, as the logicians hold, one awareness and a separate knower.”

units.label: Prose II.2.80
units.deva: ननूपलब्धिफलावसानो धात्वर्थः कथम् इति
units.iast: nanūpalabdhiphalāvasāno dhātvarthaḥ katham iti
units.translation: The student asks: “Then how can a verb whose meaning ends in an effect refer to awareness?”

units.label: Prose II.2.81
units.deva: उच्यते -- शृणु, उपलब्ध्याभासफलावसान इत्य् उक्तम्, किं न श्रुतं त्वया । न त्व् आत्मनो विक्रियोत्पादनावसान इति मयोक्तम्
units.iast: ucyate -- śṛṇu, upalabdhyābhāsaphalāvasāna ity uktam, kiṃ na śrutaṃ tvayā । na tv ātmano vikriyotpādanāvasāna iti mayoktam
units.translation: The teacher says: “Listen. I said that it ends in the apparent result of awareness; I did not say that it ends in producing a change in the Self.”

units.label: Prose II.2.82
units.deva: शिष्य आह -- कथं तर्हि कूटस्थे मय्य् अशेषस्वविषयचित्तप्रचारोपलब्धृत्वम् इत्य् आत्थ
units.iast: śiṣya āha -- kathaṃ tarhi kūṭasthe mayy aśeṣasvaviṣayacittapracāropalabdhṛtvam ity āttha
units.translation: The student asks: “How, then, could I, who am changeless, know every movement in the field of my mind?”

units.label: Prose II.2.83
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- सत्यम् एवावोचम्, तेनैव कूटस्थताम् अब्रुवं तव
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- satyam evāvocam, tenaiva kūṭasthatām abruvaṃ tava
units.translation: The teacher says: “I spoke truly; that very fact establishes your changelessness.”

units.label: Prose II.2.84
units.deva: यद्य् एवं भगवन्, कूटस्थनित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपे मयि शब्दाद्याकारबौद्धप्रत्ययेषु मत्स्वरूपोपलब्ध्याभासफलावसानवत्सूत्पद्यामनेषु, कस् त्व् अपराधो मम
units.iast: yady evaṃ bhagavan, kūṭasthanityopalabdhisvarūpe mayi śabdādyākārabauddhapratyayeṣu matsvarūpopalabdhyābhāsaphalāvasānavatsūtpadyāmaneṣu, kas tv aparādho mama
units.translation: The student asks: “Revered one, if I am changeless, eternal awareness, and cognitions shaped like sound and the rest arise in me and end in an apparent reflection of my nature, what fault is mine?”

units.label: Prose II.2.85
units.deva: सत्यम्, नास्त्य् अपराधः, किं त्व् अविद्यामात्रस् तु अपराध इति प्राग् एवावोचम्
units.iast: satyam, nāsty aparādhaḥ, kiṃ tv avidyāmātras tu aparādha iti prāg evāvocam
units.translation: The teacher replies: “You are right: there is no fault in you. As I said before, the fault is ignorance alone.”

units.label: Prose II.2.86
units.deva: यदि भगवन्, सुषुप्त इव मम विक्रिया नास्ति, कथं स्वप्नजागरिते
units.iast: yadi bhagavan, suṣupta iva mama vikriyā nāsti, kathaṃ svapnajāgarite
units.translation: The student asks: “If I undergo no change, as in deep sleep, how can there be waking and dream?”

units.label: Prose II.2.87
units.deva: तं गुरुर् उवाच -- किं त्व् अनुभूयेते त्वया स[न्]ततम्
units.iast: taṃ gurur uvāca -- kiṃ tv anubhūyete tvayā sa[n]tatam
units.translation: The teacher asks: “Are those states continuously experienced by you?”

units.label: Prose II.2.88
units.deva: बाढम् अनुभवामि, किं तु विच्छिद्य विच्छिद्य न तु सन्ततम्
units.iast: bāḍham anubhavāmi, kiṃ tu vicchidya vicchidya na tu santatam
units.translation: The student replies: “Certainly I experience them, but intermittently, not continuously.”

units.label: Prose II.2.89
units.deva: [तं] गुरुर् उवाच -- आगन्तुके त्व् एते न तवात्मभूते । यदि तवात्मभूते चैतन्यस्वरूपवत् स्वतःसिद्धे सन्तते एव स्याताम् । किं च स्वप्नजागरिते न तवात्मभूते, व्यभिचारित्वात्, वस्त्रादिवत् । न हि यस्य यत् स्वरूपं तत् तद्व्यभिचारि दृष्टम् । स्वप्नजागरिते तु चैतन्यमात्रत्वाद् व्यभिचरतः । सुषुप्ते चेत् स्वरूपं व्यभिचरेत्, तन् नष्टं नास्तीति वा बाध्यम् एव स्यात्, आगन्तुकानाम् अतद्धर्माणाम् उभयात्मकत्वदर्शनात्, यथा धनवस्त्रादीनां नाशो दृष्टः, स्वप्नभ्रान्तिलब्धानां त्व् अभावो दृष्टः
units.iast: [taṃ] gurur uvāca -- āgantuke tv ete na tavātmabhūte । yadi tavātmabhūte caitanyasvarūpavat svataḥsiddhe santate eva syātām । kiṃ ca svapnajāgarite na tavātmabhūte, vyabhicāritvāt, vastrādivat । na hi yasya yat svarūpaṃ tat tadvyabhicāri dṛṣṭam । svapnajāgarite tu caitanyamātratvād vyabhicarataḥ । suṣupte cet svarūpaṃ vyabhicaret, tan naṣṭaṃ nāstīti vā bādhyam eva syāt, āgantukānām ataddharmāṇām ubhayātmakatvadarśanāt, yathā dhanavastrādīnāṃ nāśo dṛṣṭaḥ, svapnabhrāntilabdhānāṃ tv abhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ
units.translation: The teacher says: “Then they are adventitious, not your own nature. If they belonged to you as your nature does, they would be continuous and self-established. Waking and dream are not your nature because they are intermittent. What is someone’s own nature is never absent; waking and dream, however, come and go, like clothes and other possessions. If the Self’s nature came and went, it would perish or be sublated like other adventitious things, as with wealth that can be lost or a dream that proves unreal.”

units.label: Prose II.2.90
units.deva: नन्व् एवं भगवन्, चैतन्यस्वरूपम् अप्य् आगन्तुकं प्राप्तम्, स्वप्नजागरितयोर् इव सुषुप्ते ऽनुपलब्धेः । अचैतन्यस्वरूपो वा स्याम् अहम्
units.iast: nanv evaṃ bhagavan, caitanyasvarūpam apy āgantukaṃ prāptam, svapnajāgaritayor iva suṣupte 'nupalabdheḥ । acaitanyasvarūpo vā syām aham
units.translation: The student says: “Revered one, then consciousness itself must be something adventitious, since it is not perceived in dream and waking while I am in deep sleep. Or perhaps I am by nature unconscious.”

units.label: Prose II.2.91
units.deva: न, पश्य, तदनुपपत्तेः । चैतन्यस्वरूपं चेद् आगन्तुकं पश्यसि, पश्य । नैतद् वर्शशतेनाप्य् उपपत्त्या कल्पयितुं शक्नुमो वयम्, अन्यो वाचैतन्यो ऽपि । [तस्य] संहतत्वात् पारार्थ्यम् अनेकत्वं नाशित्वं च न केनचिद् उपपत्त्या वारयितुं शक्यम् । अस्वार्थस्य स्वतःसिद्ध्यभावाद् इत्य् अवोचाम । चैतन्यस्वरूपस्य त्व् आत्मनः स्वतःसिद्धेर् अन्यानपेक्षत्वं न केनचिद् वारयितुं शक्यम्, अव्यभिचारात्
units.iast: na, paśya, tadanupapatteḥ । caitanyasvarūpaṃ ced āgantukaṃ paśyasi, paśya । naitad varśaśatenāpy upapattyā kalpayituṃ śaknumo vayam, anyo vācaitanyo 'pi । [tasya] saṃhatatvāt pārārthyam anekatvaṃ nāśitvaṃ ca na kenacid upapattyā vārayituṃ śakyam । asvārthasya svataḥsiddhyabhāvād ity avocāma । caitanyasvarūpasya tv ātmanaḥ svataḥsiddher anyānapekṣatvaṃ na kenacid vārayituṃ śakyam, avyabhicārāt
units.translation: The teacher replies: “No; see that this is impossible. If you think consciousness is adventitious, examine that idea. We cannot establish it by any reasoning, even after hundreds of years; nor can anyone establish some other unconscious Self. If it were composite, it would exist for another, be many and perish—no reasoning can prevent that. We have already explained that what does not exist for itself is not self-established. But no reasoning can deny that the Self, whose nature is consciousness, is self-established and depends on nothing else, since it is never absent.”

units.label: Prose II.2.92
units.deva: ननु व्यभिचारो दर्शितो मया सुषुप्ते न पश्यामीति
units.iast: nanu vyabhicāro darśito mayā suṣupte na paśyāmīti
units.translation: The student objects: “I showed that it is absent: in deep sleep I do not see.”

units.label: Prose II.2.93
