units.deva: न । व्याहतत्वात् । कथं व्याघातः । पश्यतस् तव न पश्यामीति व्याहतं वचनम् । न हि कदाचिद् भगवन्, सुषुप्ते मया चैतन्यम् अन्यद् वा किंचिद् दृष्टम् । पश्यंस् तर्हि सुषुप्ते त्वम् । यस्माद् दृष्टम् एव प्रतिषेधसि, न दृष्टिम् । या तव दृष्टिस् तच् चैतन्यम् इति मयोक्तम् । यया त्वं विद्यमानया न किंचिद् दृष्टम् इति प्रतिषेधसि, सा दृष्टिस् तच् चैतन्यम् । तर्हि सर्वत्राव्यभिचारात् कूटस्थनित्यत्वं सिद्धं स्वत एव, न प्रमाणापेक्षम् । स्वतःसिद्धस्य हि प्रमातुर् अन्यस्य प्रमेयस्य परिच्छित्तिं प्रति प्रमाणापेक्षा । या त्व् अन्या नित्या परिच्छित्तिर् अपेक्ष्यते ऽन्यस्यापरिच्छित्तिरूपस्य परिच्छेदाय, सा हि नित्यैव कूटस्था स्वयंज्योतिःस्वभावा । आत्मनि प्रमाणत्वे प्रमातृत्वे वा न तां प्रति प्रमाणापेक्षा, तत्स्वभावत्वात् । यथा प्रकाशनम् उष्णत्वं वा लोहोदकादिषु परतो ऽपेक्ष्यते ऽग्न्यादित्यादिभ्यः, अतत्स्वभावत्वात्, नाग्न्यादित्यादीनां तदपेक्षा, सर्वदा तत्स्वभावत्वात्
units.iast: na । vyāhatatvāt । kathaṃ vyāghātaḥ । paśyatas tava na paśyāmīti vyāhataṃ vacanam । na hi kadācid bhagavan, suṣupte mayā caitanyam anyad vā kiṃcid dṛṣṭam । paśyaṃs tarhi suṣupte tvam । yasmād dṛṣṭam eva pratiṣedhasi, na dṛṣṭim । yā tava dṛṣṭis tac caitanyam iti mayoktam । yayā tvaṃ vidyamānayā na kiṃcid dṛṣṭam iti pratiṣedhasi, sā dṛṣṭis tac caitanyam । tarhi sarvatrāvyabhicārāt kūṭasthanityatvaṃ siddhaṃ svata eva, na pramāṇāpekṣam । svataḥsiddhasya hi pramātur anyasya prameyasya paricchittiṃ prati pramāṇāpekṣā । yā tv anyā nityā paricchittir apekṣyate 'nyasyāparicchittirūpasya paricchedāya, sā hi nityaiva kūṭasthā svayaṃjyotiḥsvabhāvā । ātmani pramāṇatve pramātṛtve vā na tāṃ prati pramāṇāpekṣā, tatsvabhāvatvāt । yathā prakāśanam uṣṇatvaṃ vā lohodakādiṣu parato 'pekṣyate 'gnyādityādibhyaḥ, atatsvabhāvatvāt, nāgnyādityādīnāṃ tadapekṣā, sarvadā tatsvabhāvatvāt
units.translation: The teacher replies: “No; that statement contradicts itself. How? You say ‘I do not see’ while seeing. Surely, revered one, in deep sleep I did not see consciousness or anything else. Then you were seeing in deep sleep, since you deny seeing anything that was seen; you deny objects, not seeing itself. I said that the seeing which is yours is consciousness. The seeing by which you say ‘I saw nothing’ is that consciousness. Since it is never absent, its changeless permanence is established by itself, without depending on a means of knowledge. A knower who is self-established depends on a means of knowledge only to determine an object other than itself. That other, eternal awareness, needed to determine what is not already known, is itself changeless and self-luminous. No means of knowledge is needed for the Self as knower or as the very nature of awareness. A fire, sun, iron or water may need another source to produce heat or light, since those qualities are not its nature; fire and the sun themselves never depend on something else to be what they are.”

units.label: Prose II.2.94
units.deva: अनित्यत्व एव प्रमा स्यान् न नित्यत्व इति चेत्
units.iast: anityatva eva pramā syān na nityatva iti cet
units.translation: An objection: “Valid cognition can be impermanent, but not eternal.”

units.label: Prose II.2.95
units.deva: न । अवगतेर् नित्यत्वानित्यत्वयोर् विशेषानुपपत्तेः । न ह्य् अवगतेः प्रमात्वे ऽनित्यावगतिः प्रमा न नित्येति विशेषो ऽवगम्यते
units.iast: na । avagater nityatvānityatvayor viśeṣānupapatteḥ । na hy avagateḥ pramātve 'nityāvagatiḥ pramā na nityeti viśeṣo 'vagamyate
units.translation: The answer is no, because no difference between eternal and impermanent awareness can be established. If awareness is a means of valid knowledge, there is no reason to hold that impermanent awareness is valid while eternal awareness is not.

units.label: Prose II.2.96
units.deva: नित्यायां प्रमातुर् अपेक्षाभावः । अनित्यायां तु यत्नान्तरितत्वाद् अवगतिर् अपेक्ष्यत इति विशेषं स्याद् इति चेत्
units.iast: nityāyāṃ pramātur apekṣābhāvaḥ । anityāyāṃ tu yatnāntaritatvād avagatir apekṣyata iti viśeṣaṃ syād iti cet
units.translation: An objection: “The knower does not need anything for eternal cognition, but impermanent cognition depends on a separate effort; that is the difference.”

units.label: Prose II.2.97
units.deva: सिद्धा तर्ह्य् आत्मनः प्रमातुः स्वतःसिद्धिः, प्रनाणनिरपेक्षतयैवेति
units.iast: siddhā tarhy ātmanaḥ pramātuḥ svataḥsiddhiḥ, pranāṇanirapekṣatayaiveti
units.translation: Then the Self as knower is established as self-existing, entirely independent of a means of knowledge.

units.label: Prose II.2.98
units.deva: अभावे ऽप्य् अपेक्षाभावः, नित्यत्वाद् इति चेत् । न । अवगतेर् एवात्मनि सद्भावाद् इति परिहृतम् एतत्
units.iast: abhāve 'py apekṣābhāvaḥ, nityatvād iti cet । na । avagater evātmani sadbhāvād iti parihṛtam etat
units.translation: An objection: “Even if there is no object, there is no need for cognition because the Self is eternal.” The reply: no; it has already been explained that awareness itself is present in the Self.

units.label: Prose II.2.99
units.deva: प्रमातुश् चेत् प्रमाणापेक्षासिद्धिः, कस्य प्रमित्सा स्यात् । यस्य प्रमित्सा स एव प्रमाताभ्युपगम्यते । तदीया च प्रमित्सा प्रमेयविषयैव, न प्रमातृविषया । प्रमातृविषयत्वे ऽनवस्थाप्रसङ्गात् प्रमातुस् तदिच्छायाश् च, तस्याप्य् अन्यः प्रमाता, तस्याप्य् अन्य इति । एवम् एवेच्छायाः प्रमातृविषयत्वे । प्रमातुर् आत्मनो ऽव्यवहितत्वाच् च प्रमेयत्वनुपपत्तिः । लोके हि प्रमेयं नाम प्रमातुर् इच्छास्मृतिप्रयत्नप्रमाणजन्मव्यवहितं सिद्ध्यति, नान्यथावगतिः प्रमेयविषया दृष्टा । न च प्रमातुः प्रमाता स्वस्य स्वयम् एव केनचिद् व्यवहितः कल्पयितुं शक्य इच्छादीनाम् अन्यतमेनापि । स्मृतिश् च स्मर्तव्यविषया, न स्मर्तृविषया । तथेच्छाया इष्टविषयत्वम् एव, नेच्छावद्विषयत्वम् । स्मर्त्रिच्छावद्विषयत्वे ऽपि ह्य् उभयोर् अनवस्था पूर्ववद् अपरिहार्या स्यात्
units.iast: pramātuś cet pramāṇāpekṣāsiddhiḥ, kasya pramitsā syāt । yasya pramitsā sa eva pramātābhyupagamyate । tadīyā ca pramitsā prameyaviṣayaiva, na pramātṛviṣayā । pramātṛviṣayatve 'navasthāprasaṅgāt pramātus tadicchāyāś ca, tasyāpy anyaḥ pramātā, tasyāpy anya iti । evam evecchāyāḥ pramātṛviṣayatve । pramātur ātmano 'vyavahitatvāc ca prameyatvanupapattiḥ । loke hi prameyaṃ nāma pramātur icchāsmṛtiprayatnapramāṇajanmavyavahitaṃ siddhyati, nānyathāvagatiḥ prameyaviṣayā dṛṣṭā । na ca pramātuḥ pramātā svasya svayam eva kenacid vyavahitaḥ kalpayituṃ śakya icchādīnām anyatamenāpi । smṛtiś ca smartavyaviṣayā, na smartṛviṣayā । tathecchāyā iṣṭaviṣayatvam eva, necchāvadviṣayatvam । smartricchāvadviṣayatve 'pi hy ubhayor anavasthā pūrvavad aparihāryā syāt
units.translation: “If the knower were established by depending on a means of knowledge, who would want to know? The one who wants to know is already accepted as the knower. That desire to know concerns an object, never the knower; otherwise an infinite regress would follow: the knower would need another knower to know it, and another for that one. The same regress would follow if the desire to know were about the knower. The Self cannot be an object, because it is immediately present. In ordinary life an object of knowledge is established only when separated from the knower by desire, memory, effort and a means of knowledge; awareness is never seen as an object in any other way. Nor can one imagine some other knower that separates the Self from itself by desire, memory or effort. Memory concerns what is remembered, not the rememberer; desire concerns what is wanted, not the one who desires. If the rememberer or desirer were made an object, the same infinite regress would follow.”

units.label: Prose II.2.100
units.deva: ननु प्रमातृविषयावगत्यनुत्पत्ताव् अनवगत एव प्रमाता स्याद् इति चेत्
units.iast: nanu pramātṛviṣayāvagatyanutpattāv anavagata eva pramātā syād iti cet
units.translation: An objection: “If cognition of the knower as an object did not arise, the knower would be unknown.”

units.label: Prose II.2.101
units.deva: न, अवगन्तुर् अवगतेर् अवगन्तव्यविषयत्वात् । अवगन्तृविषयत्वे चानवस्था पूर्ववत् स्यात् । अवगतिश् चात्मनि कूटस्थनित्यात्मज्योतिर् अन्यतो ऽनपेक्षैव सिद्धा, अग्न्यादित्याद्युष्णप्रकाशवद् इति पूर्वम् एव प्रसाधितम् । अवगतेश् चैतन्यात्मज्योतिषः स्वात्मन्य् अनित्यत्व आत्मनः स्वार्थतानुपपत्तिः, कार्यकरण[संघात]वत् संहतत्वात् पारार्थ्यं दोषवत्त्वं चावोचाम । कथम् । चैतन्यात्मज्योतिषः स्वात्मन्य् अनित्यत्वे स्मृत्यादिव्यवधानात् संहतत्वम् । ततश् च तस्य चैतन्यज्योतिषः प्राग् उत्पत्तेः प्रध्वंसाच् चोर्ध्वम् आत्मन्य् एवाभावात्, चक्षुरादीनाम् इव संहतत्वात्, पारार्थ्यं स्यात् । यदा च तद् उत्पन्नम् आत्मनि विद्यते, न तदात्मनः स्वार्थत्वम् । तद्भावाभावापेक्षा ह्य् आत्मानात्मनोः स्वार्थत्वपरार्थत्वसिद्धिः । तस्माद् आत्मनो ऽन्यनिरपेक्षम् एव नित्यचैतन्यज्योतिष्ट्वं सिद्धम्
units.iast: na, avagantur avagater avagantavyaviṣayatvāt । avagantṛviṣayatve cānavasthā pūrvavat syāt । avagatiś cātmani kūṭasthanityātmajyotir anyato 'napekṣaiva siddhā, agnyādityādyuṣṇaprakāśavad iti pūrvam eva prasādhitam । avagateś caitanyātmajyotiṣaḥ svātmany anityatva ātmanaḥ svārthatānupapattiḥ, kāryakaraṇa[saṃghāta]vat saṃhatatvāt pārārthyaṃ doṣavattvaṃ cāvocāma । katham । caitanyātmajyotiṣaḥ svātmany anityatve smṛtyādivyavadhānāt saṃhatatvam । tataś ca tasya caitanyajyotiṣaḥ prāg utpatteḥ pradhvaṃsāc cordhvam ātmany evābhāvāt, cakṣurādīnām iva saṃhatatvāt, pārārthyaṃ syāt । yadā ca tad utpannam ātmani vidyate, na tadātmanaḥ svārthatvam । tadbhāvābhāvāpekṣā hy ātmānātmanoḥ svārthatvaparārthatvasiddhiḥ । tasmād ātmano 'nyanirapekṣam eva nityacaitanyajyotiṣṭvaṃ siddham
units.translation: The teacher replies: “No. Cognition is immediate because its object is the knower itself; if the knower were an object for another knower, the same regress would follow. Awareness in the Self is established as changeless, eternal, self-luminous and independent, as already proved. If the light of consciousness in the Self were impermanent, the Self could not exist for its own sake; it would be composite and exist for another, like an assemblage of instruments and effects. How? If awareness were impermanent in the Self, it would depend on a preceding memory or effort, become composite, and exist for another, because it would be absent before arising and after it ceased, like sight and the other senses. While it existed, it would still not be for the Self’s own sake. Whether something serves its own sake or another’s is determined by whether it is present or absent for that one. Thus the Self’s nature as the eternal light of consciousness, independent of anything else, is established.”

units.label: Prose II.2.102
units.deva: नन्व् एवं सति, असति प्रमातृत्वे कथं प्रमातुः प्रमातृत्वम्
units.iast: nanv evaṃ sati, asati pramātṛtve kathaṃ pramātuḥ pramātṛtvam
units.translation: The student asks: “If that is so, when there is no agency in the knower, how can the knower be called a knower?”

units.label: Prose II.2.103
units.deva: उच्यते -- प्रमाया नित्यत्वे ऽनित्यत्वे च रूपविशेषाभावात् । अवगतिर् हि प्रमा । तस्याः स्मृतीच्छादिपूर्विकाया अनित्यायः कूटस्थनित्याया वा, न [स्व]रूपविशेषो विद्यते । यथा धात्वर्थस्य तिष्ठत्यादेः फलस्य गत्यादिपूर्वकस्यानित्यस्यापूर्वस्य नित्यस्य वा, रूपविशेषो नास्तीति तुल्यो व्यपदेशो दृष्टः -- तिष्ठन्ति मनुष्याः, तिष्ठन्ति पर्वता इत्यादि । तथा नित्यावगतिस्वरूपे ऽपि प्रमातरि प्रमातृत्वव्यपदेशो न विरुध्यते, फलसामान्याद् इति
units.iast: ucyate -- pramāyā nityatve 'nityatve ca rūpaviśeṣābhāvāt । avagatir hi pramā । tasyāḥ smṛtīcchādipūrvikāyā anityāyaḥ kūṭasthanityāyā vā, na [sva]rūpaviśeṣo vidyate । yathā dhātvarthasya tiṣṭhatyādeḥ phalasya gatyādipūrvakasyānityasyāpūrvasya nityasya vā, rūpaviśeṣo nāstīti tulyo vyapadeśo dṛṣṭaḥ -- tiṣṭhanti manuṣyāḥ, tiṣṭhanti parvatā ityādi । tathā nityāvagatisvarūpe 'pi pramātari pramātṛtvavyapadeśo na virudhyate, phalasāmānyād iti
units.translation: The answer: “There is no difference in nature between awareness that is a means of knowledge and awareness that is eternal. Awareness is valid knowledge. Whether it is impermanent because preceded by memory or desire, or changeless and eternal, its nature is not different. The same expression can be used for an action’s result whether it is temporary or not—people say ‘the people stand’ and ‘the mountains stand.’ Thus one may speak of a changeless knower as a knower, by a common usage of the result.”

units.label: Prose II.2.104
units.deva: अत्राह शिष्यः -- नित्यावगतिस्वरूपस्यात्मनो ऽविक्रियत्वात् कार्यकरणैर् असंहत्य, तक्षादीनाम् इव वास्यादिभिः, कर्तृत्वं नोपपद्यते, असंहतस्वभावस्य च कार्यकरणोपादाने ऽनवस्था प्रसज्येत । तक्षादीनां तु कार्यकरणैर् नित्यम् एव संहतत्वम् इति वास्याद्युपादाने नानवस्था स्याद् इति
units.iast: atrāha śiṣyaḥ -- nityāvagatisvarūpasyātmano 'vikriyatvāt kāryakaraṇair asaṃhatya, takṣādīnām iva vāsyādibhiḥ, kartṛtvaṃ nopapadyate, asaṃhatasvabhāvasya ca kāryakaraṇopādāne 'navasthā prasajyeta । takṣādīnāṃ tu kāryakaraṇair nityam eva saṃhatatvam iti vāsyādyupādāne nānavasthā syād iti
units.translation: The student objects: “Because the Self’s nature is changeless awareness, it cannot join with instruments and become an agent; it is not joined to action-tools as a carpenter is to an axe. If something not joined by nature took up instruments, an infinite regress would follow.”

units.label: Prose II.2.105
units.deva: इह त्व् असंहतस्वभावस्य करणानुपादाने कर्तृत्वं नोपपद्यत इति करणम् उपादेयम्, तदुपादानम् अपि विक्रियैवेति तत्कर्तृत्वे करणान्तरम् उपादेयम्, तदुपादाने ऽप्य् अन्यद् इति प्रमातुः स्वातन्त्र्ये ऽनवस्थापरिहार्या स्यात् । न च क्रियैवात्मानं कारयति, अनिर्वर्तितायाः स्वरूपाभावात् । अथान्यद् आत्मानम् उपेत्य क्रियां कारयतीति चेत् । न । अन्यस्य स्वतःसिद्धत्वाविषयत्वाद्यनुपपत्तेः । न ह्य् आत्मनो ऽन्यद् अचेतनं वस्तु स्वप्रमाणकं दृष्टम् । शब्दादिसर्वम् एवावगतिफलावसानप्रत्ययप्रमितं सिद्धं स्यात् । अवगतिश् चेद् आत्मनो ऽन्यस्य स्यात्, सो ऽप्य् आत्मैवासंहतः स्वार्थः स्यान् न परार्थः । न च देहेन्द्रियविषयाणां स्वार्थताम् अवगन्तुं शक्नुमो ऽवगत्यवसानप्रत्ययापेक्षसिद्धिदर्शनात्
units.iast: iha tv asaṃhatasvabhāvasya karaṇānupādāne kartṛtvaṃ nopapadyata iti karaṇam upādeyam, tadupādānam api vikriyaiveti tatkartṛtve karaṇāntaram upādeyam, tadupādāne 'py anyad iti pramātuḥ svātantrye 'navasthāparihāryā syāt । na ca kriyaivātmānaṃ kārayati, anirvartitāyāḥ svarūpābhāvāt । athānyad ātmānam upetya kriyāṃ kārayatīti cet । na । anyasya svataḥsiddhatvāviṣayatvādyanupapatteḥ । na hy ātmano 'nyad acetanaṃ vastu svapramāṇakaṃ dṛṣṭam । śabdādisarvam evāvagatiphalāvasānapratyayapramitaṃ siddhaṃ syāt । avagatiś ced ātmano 'nyasya syāt, so 'py ātmaivāsaṃhataḥ svārthaḥ syān na parārthaḥ । na ca dehendriyaviṣayāṇāṃ svārthatām avagantuṃ śaknumo 'vagatyavasānapratyayāpekṣasiddhidarśanāt
units.translation: “A changeless Self cannot be an agent without taking up instruments. But taking up an instrument is itself a change, so to perform that action it would need another instrument; taking up that one would require yet another. If the Self’s agency were independent, the regress could not be avoided. Nor can action itself make itself, since before it is produced it does not exist. If some other agent made action occur, that too fails: no other self-established, non-object, conscious thing is ever seen besides the Self. Everything else—sound and the rest—would be established through awareness ending in a cognition, as its result. If that awareness were other than the Self, it too would be an unjoined, self-interested consciousness, not something for another. We cannot see the body, senses and objects existing for their own sake, since they are established through awareness and the cognition that results.”

units.label: Prose II.2.106
units.deva: ननु देहस्यावगतौ न कश्चित् प्रत्यक्षादिप्रत्ययान्तरम् अपेक्षते
units.iast: nanu dehasyāvagatau na kaścit pratyakṣādipratyayāntaram apekṣate
units.translation: An objection: “When the body is perceived, no other cognition is needed.”

units.label: Prose II.2.107
units.deva: बाढम्, जाग्रत्य् एवं स्यात् । मृतिसुषुप्त्योस् तु देहस्यापि प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणापेक्षयैव सिद्धिः । तथैवेन्द्रियाणाम् । बाह्या एव हि शब्दादयो देहेन्द्रियाकारपरिणता इति प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणापेक्षयैव [हि] सिद्धिः । सिद्धिर् इति च प्रमाणफलम् अवगतिम् अवोचाम, सा चावगतिः कूटस्था स्वयंसिद्धात्मज्योतिःस्वरूपेति च
units.iast: bāḍham, jāgraty evaṃ syāt । mṛtisuṣuptyos tu dehasyāpi pratyakṣādipramāṇāpekṣayaiva siddhiḥ । tathaivendriyāṇām । bāhyā eva hi śabdādayo dehendriyākārapariṇatā iti pratyakṣādipramāṇāpekṣayaiva [hi] siddhiḥ । siddhir iti ca pramāṇaphalam avagatim avocāma, sā cāvagatiḥ kūṭasthā svayaṃsiddhātmajyotiḥsvarūpeti ca
units.translation: The answer: “That may be so in waking. In death and deep sleep, even the body is established only through perception and the other means of knowledge, and the same applies to the senses. External sounds and the rest take the form of bodies and senses; they are established only through perception and the other means. We have said that what is established by a means of knowledge is the resulting awareness, and that awareness is the changeless, self-established light of the Self.”

units.label: Prose II.2.108
units.deva: अत्राह चोदकः -- अवगतिः प्रमाणानां फलं कूटस्थनित्यात्मज्योतिःस्वरूपेति च विप्रतिषिद्धम् । इत्य् उक्तवन्तम् आह -- न विप्रतिषिद्धम् । कथं तर्हि । कूटस्थनित्यापि सती प्रत्यक्षादिप्रत्ययान्ते लक्ष्यते, तादर्थ्यात् । प्रत्यक्षादिप्रत्ययस्यानित्यत्वे ऽनित्येव भवति । तेन प्रमाणानां फलम् इत्य् उपचर्यते
units.iast: atrāha codakaḥ -- avagatiḥ pramāṇānāṃ phalaṃ kūṭasthanityātmajyotiḥsvarūpeti ca vipratiṣiddham । ity uktavantam āha -- na vipratiṣiddham । kathaṃ tarhi । kūṭasthanityāpi satī pratyakṣādipratyayānte lakṣyate, tādarthyāt । pratyakṣādipratyayasyānityatve 'nityeva bhavati । tena pramāṇānāṃ phalam ity upacaryate
units.translation: An objector says: “It is contradictory to say both that awareness is the result of means of knowledge and that it is the changeless, eternal light of the Self.” The teacher replies: “There is no contradiction. How? Though it is eternal and changeless, awareness is indicated at the end of a perceptual or other cognition because it serves that cognition’s purpose. Since the cognition born of perception is impermanent, awareness is figuratively called its result and thus the result of the means of knowledge.”

units.label: Prose II.2.109
units.deva: यद्य् एवं भगवन्, कूटस्थनित्यावगतिर् आत्मज्यतिःस्वरूपैव स्वयंसिद्धा, आत्मनि प्रमाणनिरपेक्षत्वात्, ततो ऽन्यद् अचेतनं संहत्यकारित्वात् परार्थम् । येन च सुखदुःखमोहप्रत्ययावगतिरूपेण पारार्थ्यं तेनैव स्वरूपेणानात्मनो ऽस्तित्वं नान्येन रूपान्तरेण, अतो नास्तित्वम् एव परमार्थतः । यथा हि लोके रज्जुसर्पमरीच्युदकादीनां तदवगतिव्यतिरेकेणाभावो दृष्टः, एवं जाग्रत्स्वप्नद्वैतभावस्यापि तदवगतिव्यतिरेकेणाभावो युक्तः । एवम् एव, भगवन्, अवगतेर् आत्मज्योतिषो नैरन्तर्यभावात् कूटस्थनित्यता, अद्वैतभावश् च सर्वप्रत्ययभेदेष्व् अव्यभिचारात् । प्रत्यभेदास् त्व् अवगतिं व्यभिचरन्ति । यथा स्वप्ने नीलपीताद्याकारभेदरूपाः प्रत्ययास् तदवगतिं व्यभिचरन्तः परमार्थतो न सन्तीत्य् उच्यन्ते, एवं जाग्रत्य् अपि नीलपीतादिप्रत्ययभेदास् ताम् एवावगतिं व्यभिचरन्तो ऽसत्यरूपा भवितुम् अर्हन्ति । तस्याश् चावगतेर् अन्यो ऽवगन्ता नास्तीति न स्वेन स्वरूपेण स्वयम् उपादातुं हातुं वा शक्यते, अन्यस्य चाभावात्
units.iast: yady evaṃ bhagavan, kūṭasthanityāvagatir ātmajyatiḥsvarūpaiva svayaṃsiddhā, ātmani pramāṇanirapekṣatvāt, tato 'nyad acetanaṃ saṃhatyakāritvāt parārtham । yena ca sukhaduḥkhamohapratyayāvagatirūpeṇa pārārthyaṃ tenaiva svarūpeṇānātmano 'stitvaṃ nānyena rūpāntareṇa, ato nāstitvam eva paramārthataḥ । yathā hi loke rajjusarpamarīcyudakādīnāṃ tadavagativyatirekeṇābhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ, evaṃ jāgratsvapnadvaitabhāvasyāpi tadavagativyatirekeṇābhāvo yuktaḥ । evam eva, bhagavan, avagater ātmajyotiṣo nairantaryabhāvāt kūṭasthanityatā, advaitabhāvaś ca sarvapratyayabhedeṣv avyabhicārāt । pratyabhedās tv avagatiṃ vyabhicaranti । yathā svapne nīlapītādyākārabhedarūpāḥ pratyayās tadavagatiṃ vyabhicarantaḥ paramārthato na santīty ucyante, evaṃ jāgraty api nīlapītādipratyayabhedās tām evāvagatiṃ vyabhicaranto 'satyarūpā bhavitum arhanti । tasyāś cāvagater anyo 'vagantā nāstīti na svena svarūpeṇa svayam upādātuṃ hātuṃ vā śakyate, anyasya cābhāvāt
units.translation: The student says: “If so, revered one, eternal and changeless awareness, whose nature is the Self’s light and which is established by itself without any means of knowledge, exists; anything else, being insentient and composite, exists for another. What exists for another is only the awareness of happiness, sorrow and delusion; it has no existence apart from the Self’s awareness, not in some other form. Just as a snake imagined in a rope or water in a mirage has no existence apart from the cognition of it, so duality in waking and dream has no existence apart from that awareness. Thus the uninterrupted nature of awareness establishes it as changeless and eternal; its never varying through any difference in cognition establishes nonduality. The different cognitions vary, and therefore are not ultimately real. Just as the different cognitions of blue, yellow and the rest in a dream are said to be unreal because they vary while awareness does not, so too waking cognitions of blue, yellow and the rest can be unreal, because they vary while awareness itself does not. And there is no other knower of that awareness; it cannot take up or relinquish itself, and there is no other thing.”

units.label: Prose II.2.110
units.deva: तथैवेति । एषाविद्या, यन्निमित्तः संसारो जाग्रत्स्वप्नलक्षणः । तस्या अविद्याया विद्या निवर्तिका । इत्येवं त्वम् अभयं प्राप्तो ऽसि । नातःपरं जाग्रत्स्वप्नदुःखम् अनुभविष्यसि, संसारदुःखान् मुक्तो ऽसीति
units.iast: tathaiveti । eṣāvidyā, yannimittaḥ saṃsāro jāgratsvapnalakṣaṇaḥ । tasyā avidyāyā vidyā nivartikā । ityevaṃ tvam abhayaṃ prāpto 'si । nātaḥparaṃ jāgratsvapnaduḥkham anubhaviṣyasi, saṃsāraduḥkhān mukto 'sīti
units.translation: The teacher says: “Exactly. Ignorance is the cause of worldly existence in waking and dream; knowledge removes that ignorance. Thus you have attained fearlessness and will experience no further sorrow in waking or dream. You are free from worldly suffering.”

units.label: Prose II.2.111
units.deva: ओम् इति
units.iast: om iti
units.translation: Om.

units.label: Prose II.3.112
units.deva: मुमुक्षूणाम् उपात्तपुण्यापुण्यक्षपणपराणाम् अपूर्वानुपचयार्थिनां परिसंख्यानम् इदम् उच्यते । अविद्याहेतवो दोषा वाङ्मनण्कायप्रवृत्तिहेतवः, प्रवृत्तेश् चेष्टानिष्टमिश्रफलानि कर्माण्य् उपचीयन्त इति तन्मोक्षार्थम्
units.iast: mumukṣūṇām upāttapuṇyāpuṇyakṣapaṇaparāṇām apūrvānupacayārthināṃ parisaṃkhyānam idam ucyate । avidyāhetavo doṣā vāṅmanaṇkāyapravṛttihetavaḥ, pravṛtteś ceṣṭāniṣṭamiśraphalāni karmāṇy upacīyanta iti tanmokṣārtham
units.translation: This examination is given for seekers who want to end the merit and demerit they have accumulated, and do not wish to accumulate new actions. The defects caused by ignorance give rise to activities of speech, mind and body; from those activities actions accumulate, producing results that are desirable, undesirable or mixed. It is for liberation from these that the teaching is given.

units.label: Prose II.3.113
units.deva: तत्र शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धानां विषयाणां श्रोत्रादिग्राह्यत्वात् स्वात्मनि परेषु वा विज्ञानाभावः, तेषाम् एव परिणतानां यथा लोष्टादीनाम् । श्रोत्रादिद्वारैश् च ज्ञायन्ते । येन च ज्ञायन्ते स ज्ञातृत्वाद् अतज्जातीयः । ते हि शब्दादयो ऽन्योन्यसंसर्गित्वाज् जन्मवृद्धि[वि]परिणामापक्षयनाशसंयोगवियोगाविर्भावतिरोभावविकारविकारिक्षेत्रबीजाद्यनेकधर्माणः, सामान्येन च सुखदुःखाद्यनेकधर्माणः । तद्विज्ञातृत्वाद् एव तद्विज्ञाता सर्वशब्दादिधर्मविलक्षणः
units.iast: tatra śabdasparśarūparasagandhānāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ śrotrādigrāhyatvāt svātmani pareṣu vā vijñānābhāvaḥ, teṣām eva pariṇatānāṃ yathā loṣṭādīnām । śrotrādidvāraiś ca jñāyante । yena ca jñāyante sa jñātṛtvād atajjātīyaḥ । te hi śabdādayo 'nyonyasaṃsargitvāj janmavṛddhi[vi]pariṇāmāpakṣayanāśasaṃyogaviyogāvirbhāvatirobhāvavikāravikārikṣetrabījādyanekadharmāṇaḥ, sāmānyena ca sukhaduḥkhādyanekadharmāṇaḥ । tadvijñātṛtvād eva tadvijñātā sarvaśabdādidharmavilakṣaṇaḥ
units.translation: “Sound, touch, form, taste and smell are objects grasped by the ear and the other senses; they do not know themselves or one another, just as clods of earth and the rest do not. They are known through the senses. That by which they are known, being the knower, is of a different kind from them. Sounds and the rest are associated with one another; they have many properties: birth, growth, transformation, decay, destruction, union, separation, appearance, disappearance, change and dependence on a changing field or seed. In general, they also have many properties such as pleasure and pain. Since they are known, the knower is distinct from every property of sound and the rest.”

units.label: Prose II.3.114
units.deva: तत्र शब्दादिभिर् उपलभ्यमानैः पीड्यमानो विद्वान् एवं परिसंचक्षीत
units.iast: tatra śabdādibhir upalabhyamānaiḥ pīḍyamāno vidvān evaṃ parisaṃcakṣīta
units.translation: Tormented by the objects of sound and the rest, the wise person should reflect as follows:

units.label: Prose II.3.115
units.deva: शब्दस् तु ध्वनिसामान्यमात्रेण विशेषधर्मैर् वा षड्जादिभिः प्रियैः, स्तुत्यादिभिर् इष्टैः, अनिष्टैश् चासत्यबीभत्सपरिभवाक्रोशादिभिर् वचनैः, मां दृक्स्वभावम् असंसर्गिणम् अविक्रियम् अचलम् अनिधनम् अभयम् अत्यन्तसूक्ष्मम् अविषयं गोचरीकृत्य स्प्रष्टुं नैवार्हत्य् असंसर्गित्वाद् एव मम । अत एव न शब्दनिमित्ता हानिर् वृद्धिर् वा । अतो मां किं करिष्यति स्तुतिनिन्दादिप्रियाप्रियत्वादिलक्षणः शब्दः । अविवेकिनं हि शब्दम् आत्मत्वेन गतं प्रियः शब्दो वर्धयेद् अप्रियश् च क्षपयेत्, अविवेकित्वान् न तु मम विवेकिनो वालाग्रमात्रम् अपि कर्तुम् उत्सहत इति । एवम् एव स्पर्शसामान्येन तद्विशेषैश् च शीतोष्णमृदुकर्कशादिज्वरोदरशूलादिलक्षणैश् चाप्रियैः, प्रियैश् च कैश्चिच् छरीरसमवायिभिर् बाह्यागन्तुकनिमित्तैश् च, न मम काचिद् विक्रिया वृद्धिहानिलक्षणा अस्पर्शत्वात् क्रियते, व्योम्न इव मुष्टिघाटादिभिः । तथा रूपसामान्येन तद्विशेषैश् च प्रियाप्रियैः स्त्रीव्यञ्जनादिलक्षणैः, अरूपत्वान् न मम काचिद् धानिर् वृद्धिर् वा क्रियते । तथा रससामान्येन तद्विशेषैश् च [प्रियाप्रियैः] मधुराम्ललवणकटुतिक्तकषायैर् मूढबुद्धिभिः परिगृहीतैः, अरसात्मकस्य न मम काचिद् धानिर् वृद्धिर् वा क्रियते । तथा गन्धसामान्येन तद्विशेषैः प्रियाप्रियैः पुष्पाद्यनुलेपनादिलक्षणैः, अगन्धात्मकस्य न मम काचिद् धानिर् वृद्धिर् वा क्रियते । "अशब्दम् अस्पर्शम् अरूपम् अव्ययं तथारसं नित्यम् अगन्धवच् च यत्" इति श्रुतेः
units.iast: śabdas tu dhvanisāmānyamātreṇa viśeṣadharmair vā ṣaḍjādibhiḥ priyaiḥ, stutyādibhir iṣṭaiḥ, aniṣṭaiś cāsatyabībhatsaparibhavākrośādibhir vacanaiḥ, māṃ dṛksvabhāvam asaṃsargiṇam avikriyam acalam anidhanam abhayam atyantasūkṣmam aviṣayaṃ gocarīkṛtya spraṣṭuṃ naivārhaty asaṃsargitvād eva mama । ata eva na śabdanimittā hānir vṛddhir vā । ato māṃ kiṃ kariṣyati stutinindādipriyāpriyatvādilakṣaṇaḥ śabdaḥ । avivekinaṃ hi śabdam ātmatvena gataṃ priyaḥ śabdo vardhayed apriyaś ca kṣapayet, avivekitvān na tu mama vivekino vālāgramātram api kartum utsahata iti । evam eva sparśasāmānyena tadviśeṣaiś ca śītoṣṇamṛdukarkaśādijvarodaraśūlādilakṣaṇaiś cāpriyaiḥ, priyaiś ca kaiścic charīrasamavāyibhir bāhyāgantukanimittaiś ca, na mama kācid vikriyā vṛddhihānilakṣaṇā asparśatvāt kriyate, vyomna iva muṣṭighāṭādibhiḥ । tathā rūpasāmānyena tadviśeṣaiś ca priyāpriyaiḥ strīvyañjanādilakṣaṇaiḥ, arūpatvān na mama kācid dhānir vṛddhir vā kriyate । tathā rasasāmānyena tadviśeṣaiś ca [priyāpriyaiḥ] madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyair mūḍhabuddhibhiḥ parigṛhītaiḥ, arasātmakasya na mama kācid dhānir vṛddhir vā kriyate । tathā gandhasāmānyena tadviśeṣaiḥ priyāpriyaiḥ puṣpādyanulepanādilakṣaṇaiḥ, agandhātmakasya na mama kācid dhānir vṛddhir vā kriyate । "aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavac ca yat" iti śruteḥ
units.translation: “Sound, whether merely sound in general or particular tones such as ṣaḍja; whether pleasant words of praise and the like, or unpleasant words that are false, disgusting, humiliating or abusive, cannot touch me, whose nature is seeing, who am unattached, changeless, unmoving, indestructible, fearless, exceedingly subtle and beyond objects. Since I am unattached, sound cannot cause loss or gain in me. What can sound do to me through praise, blame, pleasure or pain? A pleasant sound may strengthen someone who, through lack of discrimination, identifies with sound; an unpleasant one may diminish that person. But neither can do even the slightest thing to me, who discriminate. In exactly the same way, touch in general and its particular forms—cold, hot, soft, rough, fever, stomach pain and the rest—whether pleasant or unpleasant, present in the body or caused by external and adventitious conditions, cause no change, gain or loss in me, who cannot be touched, any more than a blow or fistfight can affect space. Likewise, forms in general and their pleasant or unpleasant particulars, such as the features of women and men, cause me no loss or gain, since I have no form. Nor do tastes in general or their pleasant and unpleasant kinds—sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent—grasped by deluded minds, cause loss or gain in me, whose nature is not taste. Nor do smells in general or particular pleasant and unpleasant ones, such as flowers and perfumes, cause loss or gain in me, who have no nature of smell. Scripture says: ‘That which is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, without taste, eternal and without smell.’”

units.label: Prose II.3.116
units.deva: किं च य एव बाह्यः शब्दादयस् ते शरीराकारेण संस्थिताः, तद्ग्राहकैश् च श्रोत्राद्याकारैर् अन्तःकरणद्वयतद्विषयाकारेण च, अन्योन्यसंसर्गित्वात् संहतत्वाच् च सर्वक्रियासु । तत्रैवं सति विदुषो मम न कश्चिच् छत्रुर् मित्रम् उदासीनो वास्ति । तत्र यदि [कश्चिन्]मिथ्याज्ञानाभिमानेन प्रियम् अप्रियं वा प्रयुयुङ्क्षेत क्रियाफललक्षणम्, तन् मृषैव प्रयुयुङ्क्षति सः । तस्याविषयत्वान् मम -- "अव्यक्तो ऽयम् अचिन्त्यो ऽयम्" इति स्मृतेः । तथा [सर्वेषां] पञ्चानाम् अपि भूतानाम् अविकार्यः, अविषयत्वात् । "अच्छेद्यो ऽयम् अदाह्यो ऽयम्" इति स्मृतेः । यापि शरीरेन्द्रियसंस्थानमात्रम् उपलक्ष्य मद्भक्तानां विपरीतानां च प्रियाप्रियादिप्रयुयुङ्क्षा, तज्जा च धर्माधर्मादिप्राप्तिः, सा तेषाम् एव, न तु मय्य् अजरे ऽमृते ऽभये, "नैनं कृताकृते तपतः", "न कर्मणा वर्धते नो कनीयान्", "सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्य् अजः", "न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यह्" इत्यादिश्रुतिस्मृतिभ्यः । अनात्मवस्तुनश् चासत्त्वाद् इति परमो हेतुः । आत्मनश् चाद्वयत्वविषयाणि, द्वयस्यासत्त्वात्, यानि सर्वाण्य् उपनिषद्वाक्यानि, विस्तरशः समीक्षितव्यानि समीक्षितव्यानीति
units.iast: kiṃ ca ya eva bāhyaḥ śabdādayas te śarīrākāreṇa saṃsthitāḥ, tadgrāhakaiś ca śrotrādyākārair antaḥkaraṇadvayatadviṣayākāreṇa ca, anyonyasaṃsargitvāt saṃhatatvāc ca sarvakriyāsu । tatraivaṃ sati viduṣo mama na kaścic chatrur mitram udāsīno vāsti । tatra yadi [kaścin]mithyājñānābhimānena priyam apriyaṃ vā prayuyuṅkṣeta kriyāphalalakṣaṇam, tan mṛṣaiva prayuyuṅkṣati saḥ । tasyāviṣayatvān mama -- "avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam" iti smṛteḥ । tathā [sarveṣāṃ] pañcānām api bhūtānām avikāryaḥ, aviṣayatvāt । "acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam" iti smṛteḥ । yāpi śarīrendriyasaṃsthānamātram upalakṣya madbhaktānāṃ viparītānāṃ ca priyāpriyādiprayuyuṅkṣā, tajjā ca dharmādharmādiprāptiḥ, sā teṣām eva, na tu mayy ajare 'mṛte 'bhaye, "nainaṃ kṛtākṛte tapataḥ", "na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān", "sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ", "na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyah" ityādiśrutismṛtibhyaḥ । anātmavastunaś cāsattvād iti paramo hetuḥ । ātmanaś cādvayatvaviṣayāṇi, dvayasyāsattvāt, yāni sarvāṇy upaniṣadvākyāni, vistaraśaḥ samīkṣitavyāni samīkṣitavyānīti
units.translation: “Moreover, the external sounds and the rest take the form of bodies, while the ear and other senses that grasp them take the form of instruments, the inner organs and their objects; they are mutually connected and composite in all their activities. Since this is so, for me, the wise knower, no one is an enemy, friend or neutral. If someone, through false knowledge and identification, tries to bring about something pleasant or unpleasant, some result of action, that person acts in vain because I am not an object of it. Scripture says: ‘This Self is unmanifest and inconceivable.’ I am not modified by any of the five elements; scripture says: ‘It cannot be cut or burned.’ The desire to cause pleasure, pain and the rest, arising from seeing only the arrangement of body and senses, and the merit or demerit that follows it, belong only to those people, not to me, who am ageless, immortal and fearless. Scripture says: ‘Actions done or not done do not burn him’; ‘he does not grow or diminish through action’; ‘unborn within and without’; and ‘the suffering of the world does not stain him, who is beyond it.’ The ultimate reason is that things which are not the Self do not truly exist. All the Upaniṣad passages teaching that the Self is nondual should therefore be examined in detail, because duality has no reality.”
